steps: Flake the tuna with its oil, or fry the bacon until just cooked.
Mix in the rest of the filling ingredients.
Roll out the pastry, spread with the filling and roll up lengthways.
Wrap in clingwrap and freeze for about 30 minutes.
Slice 10 mm thick, place on a greased tray and bake at 180°C for about 10 minutes until golden.
Fry the onion in the butter until soft.
Add the livers, stock and seasonings and fry until cooked.
Stir in the sour cream last, take off the heat and serve on toast.

recipes.title: Chicken Livers in Tomato Sauce

steps: Blend the sauce ingredients well, then cook down in a pot until thick.
Heat the oil and butter and fry the livers for about 5 minutes.
Put the livers in a dish, pour over the sauce and serve with fresh rolls or Melba toast.

recipes.intro: Lovely as a starter or light supper.

recipes.title: Renette's Layered Fish Starter

steps: Layer the fish, onion, potato, gherkin, cheese, salad sprinkle and egg in a dish, finishing with mayonnaise on top.
Sprinkle with peri-peri and refrigerate.
Mix just before serving with Melba toast.

recipes.intro: "Baie lekker!" Layered in the fridge and mixed just before serving.
checks: Quantities for cheese, eggs and mayo aren't given, and the original doesn't say whether the haddock is cooked (smoked haddock is usually poached first).

recipes.title: Renette's Bacon & Cheese Toasts

steps: Fry the onion and bacon. Mix with the cheese, egg, mayo and seasoning (more cheese if it's runny, more mayo if it's stiff).
Spread on bread, cut each slice in 3 and grill until golden. Watch closely, it burns easily.

tips: The mixture keeps in the fridge for up to a week.

items: 8 to 10 small tomatoes, peeled and roughly chopped
Mozzarella balls, each cut in three
Milk seasoned with salt and coarse pepper

steps: For the sauce, fry the onion, garlic and oregano in olive oil, add the tomatoes and wine and cook until soft. Add basil just before serving.
Dip one side of each bread round in the seasoned milk.
Sandwich a slice of mozzarella and basil between two rounds, wet sides in, and press the edges together like a jaffle.
Dip in egg and fry until golden. Serve with the tomato sauce.
Cook everything together, thinning with milk to the consistency you like.
Cook everything together until thick and creamy.
Serve with fried croutons.

recipes.title: Zannie's Mussel Soup

items: 1 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped (or 1 tsp dried)
2 chicken stock cubes in 750 ml boiling water

steps: Soften the onion, garlic and parsley in butter. Stir in the flour.
Pour in the hot stock, then stir in everything else.
Cook about 15 minutes over low heat. Add cream if you like.

tips: For extra flavour, make up 1 packet Royco Seafood soup and halve the stock and flour.

items: 1 packet minestrone (or mutton and vegetable) soup powder
Salt, pepper and 2 ml curry powder

steps: Boil the bones in the water for 1 hour.
Add the carrot, onion, potato and celery and cook until soft.
Mix the soup powder with a little cold water and add, with the macaroni and bay leaves. Boil 30 minutes.
Season with salt, pepper and curry.
Add the tomato purée and oats and cook 10 to 20 minutes more. Add the parsley just before serving.

recipes.title: Red Lentil Soup

items: 2 to 3 vegetable or beef stock cubes

steps: Boil the water, stock, lentils and tomatoes for 20 minutes until the lentils are soft.
Add the seasoning, sugar and cordial and blend smooth.

recipes.intro: "Delish!"

items: 3 tomatoes, peeled and chopped (or 1 x 410 g tin)

steps: Fry the onion and garlic in the oil. Add the tomato and mince and fry further.
Add the rest of the meat ingredients and simmer 15 to 20 minutes.
Cook the noodles according to the packet.
White sauce in the microwave: melt the butter in a large jug, stir in the flour and seasoning, add the milk gradually and cook on high, stirring every minute, until thick.
Layer noodles, meat, sauce and cheese, ending with cheese. Bake at 180°C for 20 minutes.
Fry the peppers, bacon and mushrooms.
Cook the soup powder in the stock with the oregano.
Mix everything with the chicken and noodles and spoon into a greased dish.
Pour over the cream, top with the cheese and bake 45 minutes at 180°C.

recipes.title: Chicken, Rice & Blatjang Chip Bake

items: 1 chicken, cooked without salt, deboned and chopped
1 packet cream of chicken soup, made with 2 litres water and cooked

steps: Mix everything together and spoon into an ovenproof dish.
Top with cheese and paprika and bake at 180°C for 20 minutes until heated through.

tips: Freezes well unbaked. Swap the chips for Bacon Kips if you like.

steps: Brown the chops lightly. Add the onion, curry, turmeric and cumin and fry 3 minutes more.
Add the flour and chutney.
Heat the stock and lemon juice and add. Simmer slowly 2 hours or until tender.
Add the pineapple and apple 20 minutes before serving.

items: Pinch of nutmeg, salt and black pepper

steps: Gently fry the onion and garlic in the butter. Stir in the flour.
Add the cream and milk and cook over low heat about 3 minutes, stirring, until it starts to thicken (not too thick).
Stir in the mustard and feta, then gently fold in the fish and the chives.
Season with nutmeg, salt and pepper and serve over pasta.

recipes.title: Sweet-and-Sour Curried Peach Salad

steps: Soften the onions in the oil. Add the curry, turmeric and sauce powder and fry 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the fruit and cook a few minutes, stirring so it doesn't catch.

tips: Add sliced pickled cucumber, 125 g seedless raisins or a chopped green pepper if you like.

items: 1 kg raw broccoli, in small florets

steps: Mix the salad ingredients. Mix the dressing and pour over.
Leave for 24 hours or longer before serving.
Put the lettuce in the bottom of a deep salad bowl and layer the rest on top.
Cover completely with the mayonnaise, cover and refrigerate for 24 hours.
Mix well just before serving.
Fry the onions in oil until translucent.
Add the dry ingredients and fry about 3 minutes (careful, it catches).
Add the rest and cook through.
Cool, pour over sosaties or chops and marinate for at least 24 hours.

items: 2 tbsp (25 ml) melted butter or oil

steps: Whisk the eggs and sugar, then add the butter and half the milk.
Sift the dry ingredients and mix in, then add the rest of the milk gradually to a smooth batter.
Don't stir again once mixed. Cook spoonfuls on a hot plate or pan.
Whisk the eggs and brandy well. Add everything else and whisk smooth.
Let it stand a little, then cook thin pancakes. Sprinkle with cinnamon sugar while hot.

recipes.title: Pancakes (Kook en Geniet)

steps: Whisk the eggs and milk. Sift in the dry ingredients bit by bit, mixing well each time until smooth.
Let it stand a while (the pancakes will be lighter); it can stay in the fridge overnight.

recipes.src: Marikie's Christmas Recipe Folder 2009 (from Kook en Geniet)

items: ¼ cup salt (or a little less)
2½ packets (10 g each) instant yeast (1 packet per kg flour)

steps: Rub the butter into the dry ingredients. (You can freeze this mix in 1 kg bags at this point.)
Add the yeast, the lukewarm liquid and vinegar and knead well (melted butter on your hands helps). Leave to double.
Knock back, shape into balls, let rise again and fry in hot oil.
Sift the dry ingredients. Whisk the egg, oil, milk and water.
Mix together, spoon into a muffin tin and bake 10 minutes at 200°C.
Sift the dry ingredients. Whisk the cream, water and eggs.
Mix, drop spoonfuls onto a greased tray and bake 10 to 15 minutes at 200°C until golden.

items: 1 cup grated red viennas and/or 250 g bacon bits, fried

steps: Mix the cheese, eggs, onion and meat. Add the rest and mix well.
Spoon into muffin tins and bake at 180°C for about 30 minutes.
Spread chutney over the hot muffins and serve straight away.
Mix the crushed chips with melted margarine and press into a tart dish, keeping a little for the top.
Fry the bacon and onion.
Make a white sauce with the margarine, flour and milk, then beat in the eggs.
Add the bacon, onion, cheese, asparagus and mushrooms, mix and pour into the crust.
Bake at 180°C for 1 hour. Decorate with parsley and the reserved crumbs.

recipes.title: Success Cake (Hot-Milk Sponge)

steps: Beat the eggs and sugar. Sift the flour, baking powder and salt.
Bring the milk and oil to the boil together.
Mix the flour into the egg mixture, then add the vanilla and the boiling milk mixture.
Bake at 180°C for 25 to 30 minutes (cupcakes 15 to 20 minutes).

tips: For chocolate cake use 2 cups flour and ¾ cup cocoa.

items: Icing sugar and a little lemon juice, to sandwich

steps: Sift the dry ingredients. Cream the butter and sugar, then beat in the eggs and vanilla.
Combine and pipe biscuits with a cookie press or piping bag.
Bake about 10 minutes at 180°C.
Sandwich with icing sugar mixed with a little lemon juice.
Sift the dry ingredients and add the sugar.
Add the milk gradually, mixing well, then the beaten yolks and the butter.
Whisk the whites stiff and fold in. Cook in a hot waffle iron.
Sift the dry ingredients. Coarsely grate in the butter and rub in.
Beat the eggs and milk and add to make a stiff dough.
Roll out thinly, spread with jam and roll up like a Swiss roll. Cut into 3 cm wheels.
Arrange in a deep greased ovenproof dish and pour over the mixed sauce.
Bake at 180°C for 40 to 45 minutes until golden.

recipes.title: Condensed Milk Fudge

steps: Melt the sugar, water, butter, syrup and salt and cook until the sugar dissolves. Take off the heat and add the condensed milk.
Cook about 25 minutes, stirring constantly (it catches easily), until slightly grainy.
Off the heat, stir in the vanilla and pour into a greased tin.

checks: The water quantity is partly illegible in the original ("! kop"); ½ cup is the usual amount.

steps: Melt the margarine and marshmallows in the microwave for 1½ to 2 minutes.
Mix in the Rice Krispies, press into a greased tin and cut into squares while still slightly warm.
Cream the margarine and sugar and beat in the eggs, then the peanut butter.
Dissolve the bicarb in the milk, add the vanilla and stir in.
Mix in the rest of the ingredients.
Roll into walnut-sized balls, flatten with a fork and bake 10 to 15 minutes at 180°C.

recipes.title: Meringue Roulade with Lemon Cream

items: Extra toasted almonds or other nuts
Fresh fruit (banana, berries) or preserved ginger (optional)

steps: Preheat the oven to 190°C. Spray a Swiss roll tin, line with baking paper and spray the paper.
Whisk the whites to soft peaks, add the castor sugar bit by bit, then the brown sugar, and whisk until stiff (don't overbeat).
Spread evenly in the tin and sprinkle with almonds. Bake about 12 minutes.
Lower to 170°C and bake 25 minutes more, covering loosely with paper if the nuts brown.
Rest 5 minutes, turn out onto baking paper, peel off the lining and cool 15 minutes. Trim the edges.
Heat the butter and sugar in a double boiler. Add the beaten yolks and lemon juice, whisking constantly, until thick. Cool.
Whip the cream stiff and fold in the lemon mixture.
Spread the cream over the meringue, top with fruit or nuts and roll up from one side (Marikie prefers the short side).
Chill a few hours. Dust with toasted nuts and icing sugar.

tips: It freezes well; thaw slowly for about 45 minutes.
checks: The almond weight is printed as "?0 gram" in the original; 70 g is a best reading.

items: 5 ml bicarbonate of soda, dissolved in a little warm water

steps: Sift the flour, baking powder, cream of tartar and salt. Grate in the butter and rub in well.
Whisk the buttermilk, cream, eggs and sugar well, then add the bicarb.
Combine. Shape 12 balls for each of 3 loaf tins and bake about 1 hour at 180°C.
Break each ball in two with a fork and dry out at about 70°C.

recipes.title: Yoghurt Loaf

steps: Mix everything and pour into a small greased loaf tin.
Bake 1 hour at 180°C.

recipes.intro: "Quick, easy and delicious!"

steps: Stir everything together and pour into a loaf tin. Sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake at 180°C for 45 to 60 minutes.

recipes.title: Banana Bread

steps: Melt the milk and butter together.
Mix the flour and sugar and add the milk mixture.
Whisk the eggs and salt, add the bananas and mix everything together.
Dissolve the bicarb in the extra milk and stir in evenly.
Pour into a greased loaf tin. Bake 25 minutes at 190°C, then 25 minutes at 170°C.

recipes.src: Marikie's Christmas Recipe Folder 2009; screenshot of the same recipe

recipes.title: Microwave Mealie Bread

steps: Mix everything and pour into a round microwave ring pan.
Microwave on high for 12 minutes.

checks: The milk and sugar quantities are illegible in the original.

recipes.title: Deep-Dish Apple Pie with Salted Butterscotch

items: 7 to 8 Pink Lady apples, peeled, cored and cut into ½ cm wedges

steps: Pulse the flours, icing sugar and salt in a processor. Add the butter and pulse to rough crumbs, then the water until it comes together.
Press together, wrap and chill 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 200°C with a rack on the lowest rung.
Roll each half of the dough 3 mm thick and line a deep square dish with one. Chill 10 minutes.
Whisk the sugar, cornflour, spices, brandy and cream, then toss through the apples.
Fill the case, dot with butter and cover with the second sheet (or a lattice). Seal, brush with egg and sprinkle with sugar. Cut steam slits.
Bake 15 minutes low, then 60 to 65 minutes at 180°C on the middle rung, covering with foil for the last 15 to 20 minutes.
Cool 10 minutes on a rack.
Melt the butter, add the sugar and cook to a deep caramel, 5 to 6 minutes.
Add the cream and simmer until thick, 8 to 10 minutes. Stir in the vanilla and salt. Serve with the pie and vanilla ice cream.

recipes.intro: Buttery rye pastry, tender apples and a rich salted butterscotch sauce.

steps: Preheat the oven to 175°C and grease a 12-cup brownie tray well.
Mix the base ingredients with a spatula to a soft dough. Press 30 g into each cup and bake 25 minutes. Lower the oven to 160°C.
Mix the curd ingredients, divide among the cups and bake 20 minutes. Cool, then chill at least 2 hours.
Boil the sugar and water. At 110°C start whipping the whites on medium; at 118°C pour the syrup in a thin stream.
Whip on high until the bowl is cool, about 10 minutes. Add the salt and vanilla and beat 30 seconds.
Pipe onto the squares and toast with a blowtorch.

recipes.title: Malva Pudding Milk Tart

steps: Preheat the oven to 175°C and spray a 32 cm rectangular dish.
Beat the eggs and sugar until pale, then add the butter, milk and jam. Sift in the flour and mix.
Mix the vinegar into the bicarb (it fizzes) and add quickly. Pour into the dish and bake 50 minutes.
Melt the syrup ingredients together. Loosen the hot pudding's edges, prick with a fork and ladle the syrup over. Cool completely.
Bring the milk and cinnamon to the boil and set aside.
Whisk the eggs, sugar, cornflour, flour and vanilla until smooth, then whisk in the hot milk.
Cook in a pot over medium heat with the butter until thick.
Spread over the pudding, dust with cinnamon and chill at least 2 hours. Cut into squares.

recipes.intro: Two South African classics in one dish: malva pudding topped with a layer of milk tart.

recipes.title: Old-Fashioned Fudge

steps: Grease a 12-cup brownie tray well.
Melt the butter, add the sugar and stir. Add the cream and condensed milk and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Boil to 115°C (soft ball: a drop in cold water rolls into a ball).
Beat with a hand mixer 3 to 4 minutes until thick and dull.
Divide among the cups and set at room temperature for 90 minutes. Turn out with a good thump.

recipes.credit: Keshree Chundriah for Le Creuset South Africa

recipes.title: Beef Bourguignon

items: 2 kg beef, in large bite-sized pieces
1 cup flour (for dusting and beurre manié)
1 tbsp roast rub (or a bouquet garni)
2 tbsp beef stock in 500 ml hot water

steps: Fry the bacon in 3 tbsp oil until lightly browned and lift out.
Sear the beef in batches. Return the bacon and meat and deglaze with the wine (and brandy).
Add the garlic, tomato paste, stock, carrots, celery, spices and 2 tsp pepper. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook gently 2 hours.
30 minutes before the end, caramelise the shallots slowly in 30 g butter (10 to 15 minutes). Fry the mushrooms in the remaining butter.
Mix a little soft butter and flour to a paste (beurre manié) and stir in bit by bit to thicken. Add the shallots and mushrooms and simmer 10 to 15 minutes.
Season and scatter with parsley. Serve with mash or baguette.

recipes.intro: The French classic with a splash of brandy, perfect for a cold evening.
checks: The original never says when the celery goes in or gives the beurre manié quantities; small amounts (about 1 tbsp each) are typical.

items: 1.5 kg mussels in shells, scrubbed and debearded

steps: Rinse the mussels and discard any open ones that won't close when squeezed.
Soften the onion and garlic in the butter. Add the thyme, bay and wine and turn the heat to high.
Add the mussels, cover and steam 6 to 10 minutes until open. Discard the herbs and any closed mussels.
Stir in the cream and parsley, season and serve with lots of bread.

recipes.title: Sparkling Wine & Garlic Mussel Pot

items: 500 ml Méthode Cap Classique or sparkling wine

steps: Soften the onion in the oil. Add the garlic, lemon peel and thyme for 2 minutes.
Turn up the heat, add the mussels and bubbly, cover and cook 5 to 8 minutes until open.
Simmer, season and reduce slightly. Serve with dill and bread.

tips: Stir in half a cup of cream once the mussels are cooked for a richer sauce.

items: 2 red onions or leeks, thinly sliced

steps: Brush each phyllo sheet with oil and stack in four sets of three. Cover with a damp cloth.
Blanch the spinach, refresh in iced water and squeeze very dry in a cloth.
Caramelise the onion lightly (in the butter), add the garlic for 2 minutes, then the spinach off the heat. Crumble in the feta and season carefully.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (fan) and grease a 30 cm shallow casserole.
Layer phyllo and a third of the filling three times, finishing with phyllo. Brush with oil, crinkle the edges in and sprinkle with sesame.
Bake 50 minutes until golden. Serve warm with a Greek salad.
Squeeze the sausage meat out of the casings and mix with the garlic, ginger, chilli, soy, honey and spring onion.
Roll into about 30 meatballs with wet hands.
Fry in two batches for 6 to 8 minutes until golden and cooked.
Pour in the teriyaki, toss and reduce about 5 minutes until sticky. Serve with the extras.

recipes.title: Asian Coconut Chicken Broth

items: Baby purple kale, toasted sesame seeds, grilled lime and sliced chilli

steps: Blitz the fennel, ginger, garlic, chilli and onion to a paste. Cook in the coconut oil over medium-low heat 5 to 10 minutes.
Add the chicken, lime leaves, star anise, peppercorns and water to just cover. Simmer covered 45 minutes, turn and poach 30 to 45 minutes more.
Lift out the chicken. Add the coconut milk and soy and simmer 30 minutes. Season with fish sauce and strain.
Shred the chicken and return it to the broth.
Blanch the coriander 5 seconds, refresh and dry, then blend with the zest, garlic and oil. Add lime juice and season.
Serve the broth boiling hot with kale, coriander oil, sesame, chilli and grilled lime.

recipes.intro: Very little effort for a lot of flavour, and even better the next day.

items: 30 g basil, chopped (plus sprigs to garnish)

steps: Blend the butter until soft, add the flour to crumbs, then the egg until it comes together. Rest 20 minutes in the fridge.
Press into 4 mini flan dishes and blind-bake at 200°C for 15 minutes (chill first so it doesn't shrink).
Beat the eggs, milk and basil and season.
Fry the tomatoes in the oil until they pop. Divide among the cases and pour over the egg mixture.
Bake at 180°C for 10 to 15 minutes until set and golden. Garnish with basil.

recipes.title: Green Broth with Bacon & Lasagne Sheets

items: 500 g Kassler chops or bacon, cubed
2 to 3 litres vegetable stock or bone broth
Extra virgin olive oil and lemon

steps: Fry the Kassler or bacon in the oil until crisp and set aside.
Soften the garlic, leeks and celery gently 5 minutes without colouring. Add the kale and chard for a minute.
Add the stock, bring to a simmer, then take off the heat and blend smooth (strain if you like).
Simmer gently 20 minutes, seasoning and adding stock as needed.
10 minutes before serving add the lemon rind and lasagne sheets; 2 minutes before, add the spinach, asparagus, broccoli and peas.
Serve topped with the crisp bacon, olive oil and a squeeze of lemon.

recipes.intro: A bright green broth packed with autumn vegetables.

recipes.title: Caramelised Cauliflower Soup with Lemon Burnt Butter

steps: Sweat the leeks and garlic in the oil 5 minutes. Add the cauliflower for 5 minutes, then stock to just cover. Simmer 40 minutes.
Cool, blend with the cream and reheat. Season.
Roast the oiled, seasoned florets at 200°C for 25 minutes, then add the Parmesan and roast 5 to 10 minutes more.
Brown the butter to a rich gold, take off the heat and add the lemon juice.
Serve the soup drizzled with burnt butter, topped with florets and greens.
Sauté the onion, chorizo and garlic in the oil 5 minutes. Add the carrots for 2 to 3 minutes.
Stir in the chopped rosemary, tomatoes and stock. Boil, then simmer 30 minutes.
Add the prawns and saffron and simmer gently 5 minutes.
Scatter with rosemary and Parmesan and serve with bread.

recipes.title: French Onion Soup

steps: Melt the butter over low heat, add the onions and sugar and cook, stirring regularly, until sticky and caramelised (at least 30 minutes).
Add the vinegar and let it evaporate. Off the heat, stir in the flour, then the stock, pepper and bay.
Stir over the heat until slightly thickened, then cover and simmer 15 minutes.
Brush the bread with butter on both sides and toast in a 200°C oven or under the grill.
Divide the soup among ovenproof bowls, top each with 3 croûtes and the Gruyère and grill until bubbling. Finish with parsley.

recipes.src: Le Creuset SA recipe (saved PDF); second French Onion Soup PDF in Recipes folder
recipes.intro: Caramelised onions and beef stock under buttery croûtes and molten Gruyère.

recipes.title: Roasted Tomato Soup

items: Coconut cream and fresh basil, to serve

steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Put all the vegetables in a dish, drizzle with oil and season generously.
Roast 25 to 30 minutes until soft. Cool slightly and blend smooth (squeeze the garlic out of its skins).
Heat in a pot with the stock for 10 minutes.
Serve with coconut cream, basil and toasted ciabatta.

recipes.credit: Health Alignment for Le Creuset South Africa

recipes.title: Spicy Chorizo & Tomato Broth with Cannellini Beans

steps: Sweat the celery, onion and garlic in the oil 5 minutes. Add the vine tomatoes, chorizo and paprika and fry 3 to 5 minutes.
Remove half the tomatoes and chorizo and set aside. Add the tinned tomatoes, chilli and 1.5 litres stock and simmer 25 minutes. Season.
Cut the pastry into uneven shards, brush with egg, sprinkle with seeds and salt and bake at 200°C for 20 minutes.
Toss the beans with the reserved chorizo and tomatoes, divide among bowls and ladle over the broth. Serve with basil and the dippers.

recipes.intro: Spanish-style, served with shard-like puff pastry dippers.

items: Sour cream, tortilla chips, sliced tomatoes, diced red onion, chilli, coriander and pink pickled onions

steps: Fry the garlic, onion, chipotle and spices until soft.
Add the tomatoes and paste, simmer 5 minutes, then add stock to the consistency you like. Simmer 20 to 30 minutes and season.
Remove the chipotles, add the vinegar and blend if you want it smooth.
Serve hot in mugs with all the toppings.

items: 125 g whole Camembert, at room temperature

steps: Mix the yeast, water and sugar and leave a few minutes.
Make a well in the flour, add the yeast mix and gradually stir in. Knead 10 minutes until springy. Cover and leave to double, about 2 hours.
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Arrange even balls in a ring in a greased 26 cm skillet, leaving space in the middle.
Brush with egg, sprinkle with salt and sesame and bake 30 to 35 minutes until hollow-sounding.
Nestle the scored Camembert in the centre, drizzle with honey and bake 5 to 10 minutes until oozing.

recipes.title: The New Prawn Cocktail

items: 12 tiger prawns, peeled and deveined, tails on
6 baby cucumbers (4 sliced, 2 shaved into ribbons)
Black sesame seeds and micro herbs

steps: Dust the prawns in seasoned flour and paprika, dip in egg and coat in the coconut-panko mix.
Shallow-fry 1 to 2 minutes a side until golden.
Divide the melon and cucumber among 6 small dishes, squeeze over lime and top with 3 prawns each.
Drizzle with Japanese mayo and garnish with sesame and micro herbs.

recipes.intro: Coconut-crumbed prawns on a melon and cucumber salad. No soggy salad boats.

recipes.title: MasterChef Chilli Con Carne

items: 1 kg beef mince (or lean chuck, cubed)
1 bunch coriander, leaves picked and stalks chopped
2 tsp chilli powder, or to taste

steps: Brown the meat in batches in the oil over high heat. Set aside.
Stir-fry the onions briefly until lightly browned. Turn down the heat, add the garlic, green chillies and coriander stalks and cook until soft. Return the meat.
Add the tomato purée and cook a couple of minutes.
Seed the chipotles and grind with rock salt. Stir in with all the other spices and heat to release the oils.
Add the wine, cocoa and treacle and reduce until the wine is absorbed.
Add the red pepper, tomatoes and stock (and the beans, see note) and simmer 2 hours, stirring often.
Season, scatter with coriander leaves and serve with sour cream.

recipes.intro: Deep, dark and smoky with chipotle, cocoa and treacle. If you can, leave it overnight and reheat.
checks: The kidney beans are listed but never added in the original. Adding them with the stock is standard.

recipes.title: Vanilla Pound Cake

steps: Cream the butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Add the eggs one by one, then the vanilla.
Fold in the flour; don't overmix.
Line a 20 cm tin with baking paper and bake at 170°C for about 1 hour 35 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Cover with foil if the top browns too fast.
Rest 10 minutes in the tin, then cool on a rack.

recipes.intro: Equal weights of butter, sugar, eggs and flour. It scales easily for bigger tins (see tip).
tips: For a 28 cm tin use 625 g each butter, sugar and flour, 12 eggs and 12.5 ml vanilla. For 35 cm, make that batch twice.

recipes.title: Chocolate Cake with Chocolate Butter Icing

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C and line two 22 cm tins.
Combine everything except the bicarb and hot water. Dissolve the bicarb in the water, add and beat well.
Divide between the tins and bake 35 to 45 minutes, turning halfway, until a tester comes out clean.
Rest 10 minutes in the tins, then cool on a rack.
Sift the icing sugar and cocoa over the butter and beat in the eggs one at a time until it's the right consistency.

recipes.intro: A one-bowl oil-and-yoghurt chocolate cake.
checks: The icing uses raw eggs.

steps: Slowly whisk the icing sugar into the egg white until a thick, stiff paste forms.
Colour as you like and keep in small piping bags until needed.

recipes.title: Italian Meringue

steps: Bring the sugar and water to the boil, stirring until dissolved. Brush down the sides with a wet pastry brush.
Cook to 115°C (soft ball). Start whisking the whites and cream of tartar to soft peaks.
When the syrup reaches 121°C, pour it gradually into the whites with the mixer on high.
Beat on medium until cooled to room temperature, thick and glossy.

recipes.intro: A stable cooked meringue for topping and piping. You need a sugar thermometer.

recipes.title: Stuffed Courgette Flowers with Baby Marrow Velouté

items: Edible flowers (rocket, borage, pansy, marigold, bean, rosemary, fennel)
Baby nasturtium, wild rocket, beetroot and carrot-top leaves

steps: Slice the porcini lengthways, keeping 2 or 3 slices for grilling, and finely chop the rest.
Sauté the chopped porcini in the butter until soft. Cool slightly, mix in the goat's cheese, season and put in a piping bag.
Remove the stamens and pipe in the filling without overfilling. Twist the petals closed and steam for 5 minutes.
Brush the reserved porcini slices and grill on both sides. Season with flaked salt.
Rub everything together to a rough crumble and bake at 175°C for 20 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes.
Melt the butter, add the flour and cook until golden. Off the heat, whisk in the stock, then return to the heat until thick.
Add the cream, bring to the boil and season. Add the baby marrow and mint, cook 1 minute and blend smooth.
Serve the flowers with grilled porcini, velouté, herb crumble and the flower salad.

recipes.intro: Courgette flowers filled with porcini and goat's cheese, with a herb crumble, baby marrow velouté and a garden flower salad.

recipes.title: Baby Squid with Wakame Brioche & Squid Ink Sauce

items: 60 g broad beans, blanched and peeled

steps: Mix the flour, sugar, salt and yeast. Add the butter and water and work in the eggs one at a time to a soft dough.
Mix in the wakame. Put in a greased loaf tin, cover with a damp cloth and rise somewhere warm until doubled (at least an hour).
Bake at 180°C for 25 minutes.
Sweat the garlic, chilli and ginger in the oil. Deglaze with the wine and reduce by two-thirds.
Add the oyster sauce and ink, cook 5 minutes on low, whisk in the butter and blitz.
Toast slices of brioche and top with sea lettuce.
Dust the calamari in flour and flash-fry for 20 seconds. Season with togarashi and arrange on the brioche.
Sauce generously and garnish with sprouts, broad beans and tarragon oil.

recipes.intro: Paired on the show with Nederburg The Beautiful Lady Gewürztraminer 2012.

recipes.title: Stuffed Saddle of Lamb with Sweet Potato Dauphinoise

items: Olive oil, sea salt and pepper
150 g dried apricots, soaked overnight and drained

steps: Preheat the oven to 160°C. Slice the sweet potato 3 mm thick. Grate in the garlic (skins stay behind), season and mix with the cream.
Press into a gratin dish; the cream should come just below the top layer. Bake 1 to 1½ hours until tender. Turn down the oven if the cream splits.
Heat the oven to 180°C. Trim the saddle so it rolls into a neat log.
Toast the cumin, then grind with ¼ tsp each salt and pepper and the sumac. Rub half over the lamb.
Chop the apricots and pine nuts and mix with the breadcrumbs, pistachios, oil and the rest of the spice mix.
Open the lamb out, season, lay over the Parma ham and pile the stuffing along the centre. Fold over and tie every 2 to 3 cm.
Sear 3 to 4 minutes a side in an ovenproof pan, then roast seam-side down for 35 minutes, turning and basting halfway. Rest 10 to 15 minutes.
Cauliflower: sauté the garlic in 2 tbsp oil and the butter, add the florets and cook about 12 minutes. Fry the cumin, crumbs and pine nuts in 1 tbsp oil until golden, toss through with the parsley.
Onions: brown in the butter, add the stock, vinegar, sugar and salt, cover with baking paper and simmer until soft. Add the thyme.
Demi-glace: toast the cumin, add the demi-glace and bring to the boil. Add the tomato and mint and whisk in the butter.
Slice the lamb thickly and serve with everything.

recipes.intro: Rolled saddle of lamb with an apricot and pistachio stuffing, served with sautéed cauliflower, braised red onions, sweet potato dauphinoise and a minted demi-glace.

recipes.title: La Mouette Salt & Pepper Prawns with Chorizo Popcorn

items: Pinch each of salt and sugar

steps: Purée: sweat the onion in oil, add the corn for 2 minutes, then the sugar, salt and vinegar. Add the cream and water, cook 5 minutes, blend, sieve and chill in a squeeze bottle.
Dressing: reduce the fish sauce, sugar, water and tamarind until syrupy. Cool and add the olive oil.
Popcorn: pop in hot oil with the lid on, then season with salt, sugar and smoked paprika.
Baby corn: blanch, refresh, halve, oil, season and char in a griddle pan.
Dredge the prawns in milk, then the salt and pepper flour. Deep-fry at 190°C until golden.
Dot the plate with purée and add chorizo, spring onion, corn, popcorn and baby corn. Top with prawns, radish and micro greens and drizzle with dressing.

recipes.intro: A La Mouette restaurant dish: crisp salt-and-pepper prawns with sweet corn purée, chorizo, paprika popcorn and tamarind dressing.

recipes.title: Tuna Ceviche with Guacamole Cream & Pickled Papaya

items: 2 Granny Smith apples, peeled, cored and cut

steps: Guacamole: blitz everything except the cream until smooth, then add the cream briefly (don't overmix).
Papaya: peel and julienne. Boil the vinegar, water, sugar, cinnamon and habanero, pour over and steep 45 minutes.
Oil: warm the oil with the citrus and chilli to 50°C and steep 5 minutes.
Tuna: slice and season with salt, pepper and the infused oil.
Foam: blend everything with a stick blender, keep aerating until foamy.
Crisps: knead the masa and water, rest 30 minutes, press thin, cut into petals, dry-fry both sides, then deep-fry at 180°C.
Mango: blend to a smooth purée.
Plate the tuna with dots of guacamole and mango, papaya, crisps and foam.

recipes.src: MasterChef Recipes.pdf (MasterChef SA Celebrity, Episode 3: Taste Test)

items: 50 g black olives, stoned and chopped

steps: Cook the spaghetti in well-salted water until very slightly underdone.
Meanwhile cook the garlic gently in the oil until just colouring. Add the anchovies and stir until dissolved.
Add the chilli, olives and capers and turn up the heat until sizzling.
Add the passata and purée and simmer vigorously about 5 minutes. Season.
Toss with the pasta and parsley.

recipes.title: Big-Batch Puttanesca with Bitter Greens Salad

items: ½ tsp crushed red pepper flakes
20 oil-cured black olives, pitted and chopped
1 x 900 g tin chunky crushed tomatoes
1 x 410 g tin diced tomatoes, drained
Crusty bread and grated Parmesan, to serve
2 to 3 tbsp extra virgin olive oil

steps: Heat the oil, garlic, anchovies and chilli over medium heat until the anchovies melt, about 3 minutes.
Add the olives, capers, tomatoes, pepper and parsley. Bubble, then simmer 8 to 10 minutes.
Toss with al dente spaghetti and serve with bread and cheese.
For the salad, squeeze the lemon over the greens, drizzle with oil, toss and season.

recipes.title: Black Macarons

steps: Sift the icing sugar and almonds separately, then combine.
Start whisking the first 90 g egg whites on low.
Boil the water and castor sugar without stirring. At 114°C turn the mixer to full; the whites must be at stiff peaks when the syrup reaches 118°C. Pour in the syrup.
Mix the colouring and the second 90 g whites into the almond mix to make a black paste.
Whisk the meringue until cool, then fold it into the paste bit by bit to a soft-peak consistency.
Pipe onto silicone mats and bake at 145°C for 14 to 16 minutes.

recipes.intro: Italian-meringue macarons tinted black.

items: Rind of 1 lemon (peeled with a vegetable peeler)

steps: Syrup: remove the pith from the rinds and tear into thin strips. Blanch and drain, then boil with the sugar and lemon juice until the rind is translucent (1 to 2 minutes). Cool.
Preheat the oven to 170°C. Beat the butter, sugar and marmalade until pale. Add the eggs one at a time, then the flour and milk, and beat smooth.
Divide among 8 buttered and floured 1-cup moulds and bake 25 to 30 minutes until springy.
Cool 10 minutes, turn out onto a rack over a tray and pierce the tops.
Drizzle with the warm syrup, dust with icing sugar, decorate with the rind and serve with citrus yoghurt.

recipes.title: Ilse's Red Curry of Beef with Cucumber Relish

items: 1 long red chilli, seeded and thinly sliced
½ long red chilli, seeded and julienned

steps: Relish: boil the vinegar, sugar and garlic, strain and cool. Pour over the cucumber, ginger, onion, chilli and coriander.
Fry the curry paste and salt in the oil over low-medium heat until fragrant, about 5 minutes.
Add the beef and seal 2 to 3 minutes. Add the stock and coconut cream (and the ginger) and cook 2 to 3 minutes.
Season with the fish sauce and palm sugar and cook over low heat about 1 hour until tender, adding stock if needed.
Add the lime leaves, chilli and herbs and simmer 5 minutes. Serve with rice and relish.

checks: The minced ginger is listed but not placed in the method; adding it with the stock is a best guess.

items: 1 Granny Smith apple, cored and julienned

steps: Slice the celeriac very thinly, then into julienne. Keep in lemony water as you go.
Drain and dry. Bind the celeriac and apple with the mayo and parsley and season with salt, pepper and lemon.
Lay the trout on the plate and season with salt, pepper and lemon.
Spoon the remoulade into a ring mould on the plate and garnish with parsley and capers.

recipes.title: Ham Hock & Potato Salad with Mustard Mayonnaise

items: 1 braised ham hock, picked into large chunks
8 baby potatoes, cooked, peeled and quartered

steps: Mix the mayo and both mustards and season with salt, pepper and lemon.
Toss the potatoes with the chives, oil, salt and pepper.
Arrange the ham and potatoes on a plate, add dollops of mustard mayo and garnish with parsley.

recipes.title: Prawn Croquettes with Parsley & Pancetta

items: 1 kg prawns, cleaned and cut into small chunks

steps: Make a thick roux sauce with the butter, flour, stock and milk; add the garlic and paprika.
Stir in the prawns, chives and zest, season and chill until firm.
Shape, dust in flour, dip in egg and coat in panko, then deep-fry until golden.
Toss the salad ingredients and serve alongside.

checks: The source file repeats the ham hock method by mistake. These steps are the standard croquette method, not the original; pancetta is in the title but not the list.

items: 75 g each mint, basil and coriander

steps: Pick the duck off the bones and mix with the hoisin, spring onion and red onion. Season.
Fill a wide pan with two parts hot to one part cold water. Dip a wrapper until soft and lay it flat.
Put duck, carrots, noodles and herbs in the centre, fold the near edge over, fold in the sides and roll tightly.
Keep under a damp cloth while you roll the rest.

recipes.title: Dark Chocolate Tart with Burnt Honey & Rosemary Ice Cream

items: 400 g unsalted butter, chilled, in 1.5 cm cubes

steps: Caramelise the honey to deep golden. Add the milk, cream and rosemary, bring to a simmer, then 5 minutes on low. Strain.
Whisk the yolks and sugar until doubled and pale. Whisk in the warm milk, then cook gently, stirring, until it coats a spoon. Cool and churn.
Stir the vinegar, sugar and water and leave 10 minutes, then stir again to dissolve.
Rub the butter into the flour and salt, leaving streaks. Work in the liquid with the palm of your hand without overworking.
Shape into two 2 cm discs, wrap and chill at least 2 hours.
Roll out (out of the fridge 20 minutes first), line the greased tin and chill again.
Blind-bake at 180°C for 15 minutes. Remove the beans, patch any cracks, brush with egg wash and bake 3 to 4 minutes. Brush again and cool.
Warm the cream with the orange peel to just simmering and strain.
Melt the butter and chocolate over a double boiler, add the cream and take off the heat.
Whisk the egg, yolks and sugar until doubled. Fold in the chocolate in thirds.
Pour into the case and bake 12 minutes at 180°C. Dust with cocoa and serve with the ice cream.

recipes.title: Mojito

items: 8 to 10 fresh mint leaves, plus sprigs to garnish

steps: Pick the mint leaves, keeping the tops and stems for the garnish.
Drop the leaves into a highball, add the lime, syrup and rum and stir lightly.
Half-fill with crushed ice and swizzle, pulling the mint up gently without bruising it.
Top with plenty of crushed ice, add a straw and a mint bouquet.

recipes.src: MasterClass Mixology workbook (Lynnette Marrero & Ryan Chetiyawardana)

items: 8 fresh mint leaves, plus sprigs to garnish

steps: Muddle the lemon in a shaker to release the juice, then gently muddle in the mint leaves.
Add the bourbon, syrup and about 6 large ice cubes and shake hard until the ice starts to break.
Pour everything into a rocks glass, push the mint down and garnish with a mint bouquet and straw.

recipes.title: Fancy Free

steps: Stir everything except the peel in a mixing glass with ice until well diluted.
Strain over a large ice cube in a rocks glass and garnish with a flamed orange twist.

recipes.intro: A 19th-century "improved" whiskey cocktail.

recipes.title: Beeswax Old Fashioned (Batched)

items: Citrus peel and a dash of absinthe (optional)

steps: Seal the bourbon and beeswax in a sous vide bag (don't vacuum) and cook at 73°C for 2 hours, agitating to mix.
Freeze 1 hour until the wax sets, snip a corner and strain. Keeps indefinitely.
Combine all the batch ingredients in a bottle.
Pour about 60 ml into a chilled rocks glass, express a citrus peel and add a dash of absinthe if you like.

recipes.intro: Beeswax-washed bourbon gives the drink weight without extra sugar. Needs a sous vide circulator.

steps: Salt the rim of a rocks glass and fill with ice.
Shake the lime, liqueur and tequila hard with 4 or 5 ice cubes.
Double-strain into the glass and garnish with a lime wheel.
Shake everything with 4 or 5 ice cubes.
Double-strain into a coupe and garnish with a lime wheel.

items: 5 to 6 mint leaves, plus a sprig

steps: Dissolve the sugar in the pomegranate juice over medium-high heat (about 5 minutes). Cool, express the orange peels into it and drop them in; remove once cool. Keeps 1 month refrigerated.
Shake the cocktail ingredients with 4 or 5 ice cubes.
Double-strain into a coupe and garnish with mint.

items: 1 long strip pink grapefruit peel, pith removed

steps: Bring the water to a soft boil, add the sugar off the heat and stir. Add the peel and bay and stir until dissolved (about 3 minutes). Cool and strain. Keeps 1 month.
Shake the cocktail ingredients with a full shaker of ice.
Double-strain into a chilled coupe and garnish with a flamed orange twist.
Infuse the herbs in the vinegar overnight. Boil 15 minutes to reduce by half, strain and stir in the sugar and honey. Keeps 3 weeks refrigerated.
Dry-shake the cocktail ingredients for 10 seconds, then shake hard with ice for about 20 seconds.
Double-strain into a coupe and float a parsley leaf.
Dry-shake everything except the bitters for a few seconds.
Add 4 or 5 ice cubes and shake hard.
Double-strain into a coupe and finish with a couple of dashes of bitters.
Dry-shake the lemon, syrup, aquafaba and Scotch, then shake with 4 or 5 ice cubes.
Rinse a highball with the absinthe and a few ice cubes, then discard the ice.
Strain the drink in, top with soda water and garnish with a lemon twist.

recipes.title: Freezer Vodka Martini

items: 1 litre vodka (pour 250 ml off to use elsewhere)

steps: Pour 250 ml out of a 1-litre bottle of vodka and add the water. Freeze.
Pour straight into a martini glass and garnish with an expressed lemon twist.

recipes.intro: Pre-diluted in the bottle and kept in the freezer for an ice-cold, silky martini.

steps: Stir everything except the olive with ice until well integrated.
Strain into a chilled coupe and garnish with a skewered olive.

recipes.title: Vesper (MasterClass Version)

steps: Stir with 4 or 5 ice cubes for about 30 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe and garnish with a lemon twist.

recipes.intro: Made with Cocchi Americano, a little different from my Vesper.

items: 60 ml London Dry (or Old Tom) gin

steps: Stir with 4 or 5 ice cubes for about 30 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe and garnish with a lemon twist.

recipes.title: Nuked Negroni (Batched)

steps: Combine everything except the garnish in a covered microwave-safe glass bowl and microwave for 3 minutes.
Cool, strain and bottle.
Pour about 60 ml over a large ice cube and garnish with grapefruit.

recipes.intro: A covered blast in the microwave infuses the whole batch without losing the alcohol.
tips: No microwave: simmer only the Campari with the fruit and herbs, covered, on low for 30 minutes, cool, strain and mix with the gin and vermouth.

steps: Stir with plenty of ice and strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice. Garnish with a grapefruit twist.
In a wine glass, layer 3 ice cubes, the pepper strips and a basil sprig, then fill with ice.
Add the sherry and stir, then the soda and tonic and stir once more. Top with an ice cube and garnish with basil.

items: 10 mint leaves, plus tops to garnish

steps: Gently muddle the mint with the syrup in a highball. Add the lime and rum.
Half-fill with crushed ice and swizzle until frosty, then fill with more ice.
Mound crushed ice on top, add a straw, float the bitters and add a mint bouquet.
Shake briefly with 3 ice cubes, just to chill.
Strain into a rocks glass of crushed ice, top with more ice and garnish with a mint bouquet and lime.

items: Mixers: club soda, tonic, ginger beer, ginger ale, fresh lemonade
Garnishes: citrus slices, berries, Thai basil, thyme, mint, rosemary

steps: Mix the tequila, Lillet and bitters in a decanter and chill.
Set out the garnishes and keep the mixers on ice.
Pour 50 ml base into an iced highball, top with a mixer and garnish as you like.
Combine everything except the rosemary and wine in a bottle and refrigerate.
Pour 60 ml into a flute, drop in a rosemary sprig and top with sparkling wine.

recipes.title: Chamomile, Rum & Cider Punch

steps: Muddle the lemon peel into the sugar, seal and leave overnight until syrupy. Strain.
Brew the tea strong (5 minutes) and cool.
Mix everything except the cider in a punch bowl, then top with the cider.

checks: The workbook's two-column layout scrambled the bonus-recipe names; this is either "Nectar of Gaia" or "For Whom the Bellflower Tolls".

recipes.title: Assam Tea & Sour Cherry Gin Punch

items: 120 ml lemon oleo-saccharum (see the chamomile punch)
Cherry and lemon slices, cinnamon stick

steps: Mix everything in a punch bowl or pitcher.
Serve over ice, garnished with cherry and lemon slices.

checks: The name is either "Nectar of Gaia" or "For Whom the Bellflower Tolls"; the scrambled layout makes it unclear which.

recipes.title: H's Sweet Tomato Soup

items: Peppadews filled with basil pesto and feta

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Put the tomatoes, chilli, onion, peppers, peppadews and garlic in a roasting tray and pour over the olive oil.
Roast about 30 minutes. Stir, sprinkle with the brown sugar and roast 30 minutes more.
Tip into a pot and blend smooth.
Heat on the stove with the cream and boiling water. Season.
Serve with stuffed peppadews and grated Gruyère.

recipes.intro: Roasted cherry tomatoes, peppers and peppadews blitzed with cream. Garnish with peppadews stuffed with basil pesto and feta.

recipes.title: Mushroom & Chicken Liver Pâté Strudel

items: 300 g mixed mushrooms (portabellini, shiitake, shimeji, oyster)
100 g Dutch Boerenkaas, grated (about a cup)
A good squeeze of lemon juice

steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Soften the onion in the butter over medium heat, about 3 minutes.
Add the mushrooms, garlic, thyme and cinnamon and fry until caramelised, about 5 minutes. Season, then stir in the cheese, cream and lemon juice. Cool.
Roll the pastry out 5 mm thick on a floured surface. Spread the pâté over the middle third and spoon the mushrooms on top.
Fold one side over the filling and tuck it under the other to make a cylinder. Brush with egg.
Cut the other half of the pastry into 5 mm strips, brush with egg and plait over the top. Prick to let steam escape, tuck the ends and brush again.
Chill 10 minutes, then bake 25 to 30 minutes until golden. Rest 10 minutes and serve with a green salad.

recipes.intro: Made for the VIA channel launch: a plaited puff-pastry log of mixed mushrooms and Boerenkaas over a layer of chicken liver pâté.

recipes.title: Citrus Rice Wraps with Citrus-Soy Dipping Sauce

items: 1 tsp vinegar, for the soaking water
Juice of 1 orange and zest of ½

steps: Toast the sesame seeds in a 180°C oven.
Soak the rice sheets one at a time in cold water with the vinegar.
Roll each soft sheet around carrot, cucumber, sprouts and herbs.
Dip one end in sesame seeds and arrange on a platter.
Pound the sauce ingredients in a pestle and mortar and serve alongside.

recipes.src: VIA channel launch recipes; recipe card photo

items: 1 cup African bird's eye chillies, stems removed

steps: Blend everything until finely chopped and saucy.
Simmer in a saucepan over medium heat for 20 minutes, stirring every few minutes.
Adjust the seasoning: it should have a good kick and sourness.
Bottle and refrigerate for up to 2 weeks.

recipes.title: Lobster Raviolo with Spinach Ricotta

items: 100 g lobster meat (behind the head to mid-tail)

steps: Make a well in the flour, add the eggs and salt and work from the inside out. Add a little water if stiff.
Knead about 5 minutes until smooth and silky. Rest at least 20 minutes.
Blanch the spinach in salted water, refresh in iced water, squeeze dry and chop finely. Mix in the ricotta and season. Chill.
Sauté the onion and garlic, add the tomato and cook down until thick. Cool.
Dice 80 g of the tail meat into the tomato. Keep the head end of the tail whole for medallions.
Sauté the onion, then the shells, thyme and garlic. Roast in the oven for 10 minutes.
Mix in the tomato paste and transfer to a pot. Reduce with the brandy, then the wine.
Add the cream, bring to the boil, strain and reduce slowly over low heat.
Butter and flour the ramekins and chill.
Roll the pasta on the thickest setting, folding until silky, then to setting 3. Cut a large circle and a smaller one.
Line a ramekin with the large circle to the top. Pipe in spinach ricotta, then lobster filling.
Moisten the edges, put the small circle on top and seal with no air pockets.
Chill 5 minutes, turn out and boil in salted water for 5 minutes. Drain on paper towel.
Gently sauté the reserved tail in butter until almost cooked. Season with sea salt and slice.
Spoon sauce onto the plate, add the raviolo and arrange the medallions on top.

recipes.intro: One large, ramekin-moulded raviolo filled with spinach ricotta and lobster in tomato, topped with lobster medallions and a bisque-style cream sauce.

recipes.title: Pan-Fried Kudu Sirloin with Blueberry Sauce

steps: Marinate the sirloin overnight in the cassis, Worcestershire and rosemary.
Pat dry, rub with olive oil and season.
Cook on a hot griddle or braai, turning on all 4 sides, about 5 minutes a side. Wrap in foil and rest.
Fry the garlic in the oil for a minute, add the wine and cook off the alcohol.
Dissolve the jam, add the stock and rosemary and reduce on high until it coats the back of a spoon.
Add the blueberries and butter and heat a couple of minutes.
Slice the kudu and serve with the sauce and mash.

recipes.src: Pan fried kudu sirloin with blueberry sauce.docx
recipes.intro: Venison is lean and pairs beautifully with sweet sauces like this blueberry and cassis one.

recipes.title: Thai Steamed Hake on Tatsoi & Mango Salad

items: 1 tbsp each basil, coriander and mint, chopped

steps: Blend the dressing ingredients. Pour out half for the salad.
Add the chilli, lime leaf and lemongrass to the other half and blend. Pour over the fish and marinate 30 minutes.
Toss the salad with the reserved dressing.
Add the marinade to water in a pot under a steamer. Steam the fish on baking paper for 8 to 10 minutes.
Serve with jasmine rice and the salad.

recipes.intro: Light and fresh for a warm summer's day.

recipes.title: Three-Mushroom Pasties

items: 150 g butter, firm but not chilled
1 large egg, beaten with a pinch of salt, to glaze

steps: The saved file stops after the ingredient list. The method still needs to be found.

recipes.intro: Meaty for meat-free pies, with an all-butter vegetarian pastry.
checks: Method missing from the source file.

items: 200 g Sally Williams dark chocolate-coated almond nougat pieces, frozen and chopped

steps: Preheat the oven to 160°C. Cream the butter and sugar until light, then add the vanilla and almond essence and the eggs.
Sift in the flour, salt and baking powder and stir well. Add the nougat.
Shape into two 22 cm logs on a greased tray and bake 35 to 40 minutes.
Lower the oven to 140°C. Cool the logs 10 minutes, then slice diagonally 1 cm thick.
Bake 5 minutes a side and cool on a rack.

items: 110 g Sally Williams almond and cranberry nougat, chopped

steps: Line a baking pan with baking paper and scatter the nougat over it.
Bring the sugar, water, glucose and butter to the boil, stirring.
Cook to golden brown and 140°C (15 to 20 minutes), stirring occasionally.
Off the heat, stir in the nuts quickly and spread over the nougat.
Cool completely, break into big pieces and store airtight.

recipes.title: Nougat Pound Cake

items: 4 Sally Williams chocolate-coated nougat bars, chopped
Extra bars and nougat pieces, to decorate

steps: Preheat the oven to 170°C and line a 20 cm (8-inch) tin.
Cream the butter and sugar until light and fluffy. Add the eggs one by one, then the vanilla.
Fold in the flour without overmixing, then the chopped nougat.
Bake 1 hour 35 minutes, covering with foil if the top browns too fast.
Cool, turn out and decorate with icing and nougat.

checks: The original method creams butter but the ingredient list omits it. 325 g matches the Vanilla Pound Cake this is based on.

items: 1 cup finely chopped Sally Williams nougat, frozen hard

steps: Stir ¾ cup cream with the chocolate and honey over low heat until smooth. Cool.
Beat the remaining 1¼ cups cream to soft peaks and fold into the chocolate in two additions. Fold in the nougat.
Divide among eight ¾-cup ramekins and refrigerate overnight.
Garnish with more chopped frozen nougat.

items: 1 Sally Williams dark chocolate slab, finely chopped

steps: Whip the cream with the vanilla until thick and refrigerate.
Dissolve the sugar and honey in the water, bring to the boil and boil 2 minutes.
Meanwhile beat the egg whites to soft peaks. Pour in the hot syrup while beating and keep beating until cooled.
Fold in the cream, nuts, chocolate and nougat. Freeze overnight.

items: 400 g Sally Williams nougat, frozen and chopped

steps: Bring the milk and vanilla pod to a simmer (don't boil). Whisk the sugar and cornflour, then the egg.
Scrape the vanilla seeds into the milk and whisk the hot milk into the egg mixture. Return to the pot and stir until thick. Cool and chill.
Bake nine 3 x 9-inch rectangles of pastry at 200°C for 15 to 20 minutes. Cool and split horizontally into 18.
Mix the custard with most of the nougat. Layer pastry, custard, pastry, custard, pastry. Finish with a little custard and nougat.

items: 500 g Sally Williams nougat, frozen and chopped

steps: Line a heavy baking sheet with baking paper.
Mix everything together. Put on the sheet, cover with more paper and roll into a 25 x 18 cm rectangle.
Remove the top paper and prick all over with a fork.
Bake at 180°C for 50 to 60 minutes until lightly browned. Cool and cut into blocks.

items: 160 g Sally Williams fine honey nougat
About 30 ml rum, brandy or orange liqueur
Chocolate vermicelli, or cocoa sifted with icing sugar

steps: Freeze the nougat, crush finely in a processor and return to the freezer.
Melt the chocolate in a double boiler, then stir in the butter and cream.
Beat in the yolks one at a time and keep beating over low heat until smooth and thick, 10 to 15 minutes.
Off the heat, add the liqueur and chill a few hours.
Stir in the nougat, roll into balls and coat in vermicelli or cocoa and icing sugar.

items: 320 g Sally Williams nougat, frozen and chopped

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C and line 1 or 2 baking sheets.
Beat the whites with the salt until frothy, add the sugar gradually and beat to stiff peaks. Fold in the cornflour.
Spoon 6 nests, building up the sides.
Turn the oven down to 160°C and bake 20 minutes, then switch off and leave 40 minutes. Cool.
Whip the cream, fill the nests, add fruit and top with nougat.

recipes.title: Smoked Angelfish with Lemon Marmalade & Celeriac Confit

steps: Season the fish and lay it on a perforated tray covered with foil.
Put the wood chips and spices in a roasting tray of the same size (your smoker) and heat on the stove until smoking.
Set the fish tray on top and smoke over medium heat for 6 minutes. Rest 5 minutes before uncovering, then drizzle with oil.
Peel the lemon rind with no white pith. Boil the sugar and water, add the rind and simmer 30 minutes until soft.
Pulse in a processor with the vinegar, castor sugar, oil and lemon juice to a marmalade.
Warm the fat with the garlic and thyme in a roasting tray.
Peel the celeriac, cut discs with a pastry cutter and add to the fat with the stem pieces. Cover and cook at 90°C for an hour. Cool in the fat.
Cut the stems into 4 cm pieces and pan-fry the discs on one side until golden.
Julienne the apple and celery and grate the toasted walnuts.
Plate the fish with celeriac and marmalade, garnish with apple, celery, walnut, dill and coriander.

recipes.intro: Pan-smoked angelfish with a sharp lemon marmalade, celeriac confited in duck fat, apple, celery and walnut.

recipes.title: Superhero Mocktails

items: Tabasco (about a dozen drops per glass)
1 part coffee (as strong as you like), or 2 parts cream and 2 parts coffee

steps: Bamse: shake with ice and strain into a small glass with some ice. Serve with a blue straw; the honey sinks, so it needs stirring.
Bamse beer mocktail: build in a tankard, stirring as you add the honey. Ice is optional.
Batkid: build in a highball glass, add some ice and garnish.
Catwoman: shake without ice and serve in a cocktail glass. Grate over some lime chocolate.

recipes.intro: Four alcohol-free drinks named after superheroes, all built by parts so you can scale them to any glass. If you use cranberry or strawberry concentrate, dilute it 1:1 with water rather than the usual 1:3 or 1:4.

recipes.title: Croque Monsieur Breakfast Casserole

items: A good handful day-old croissants, torn into pieces

steps: Preheat the oven to 160°C (325°F). Layer the croissants, ham and Gruyère in a baking dish.
In a separate bowl, whisk the remaining ingredients (except the chives) until smooth.
Pour over the croissants, top with fresh thyme and bake 30 to 40 minutes until golden and bubbly. Finish with chives.

recipes.intro: Day-old croissants soaked in a mustardy custard with ham and Gruyère. A different, eggier take on the Vol. 1 croissant croque monsieur.
checks: "A handful" of croissants is vague; for 8 eggs and 2 cups cream, about 4 to 5 croissants fills a standard dish.

items: 200 ml (¾ cup plus 4 tsp) warm water
15 ml (1 tbsp) olive oil, for glazing, plus extra for the tray
A handful of white and black sesame seeds

steps: Mix the flour, sugar and salt in a large bowl. Make a well, add the yeast and pour in the water. Mix with your hands; the dough should be very wet and fairly hard to handle.
Cover with cling film and prove about 1 hour, until doubled.
Tip onto a well-floured surface (use plenty of flour so it doesn't stick) and shape into a flat round about 2 to 3 cm high.
Put on an oiled baking tray, cover with a tea towel and prove another 45 minutes. Preheat the oven to 250°C for the last 20 minutes.
With your fingertips, dent a rough circle about 3 cm in from the edge, then fill the centre with criss-cross diagonal lines 2 to 3 cm apart.
Brush with olive oil, sprinkle with the sesame seeds and press them in.
Bake 8 minutes at 250°C, then turn down to 200°C and bake about 5 minutes more, until golden.

recipes.title: Wild Mushroom Tortellini

steps: Make a well in a mound of flour, add the egg and slowly work the flour in until shaggy. Knead until it comes together, wrap and rest in the fridge.
Sauté the onion, garlic and thyme until translucent. Add the mushrooms and cook until all the moisture has gone. Cool before using.
Roll the pasta as thin as possible (it swells when cooked) and cut circles with a medium cookie cutter.
Put a teaspoon of duxelles in the middle of each circle. Brush the edge with egg yolk as glue and fold into a half-moon.
Dab yolk on one corner and wrap the other corner around to meet it.
Cook in salted simmering water until al dente, about 3 minutes.

checks: No sauce is given; brown butter and sage or a little cream and Parmesan are the usual partners.

recipes.title: Caesar Salad the Easy Way

items: ½ cup good mayonnaise (Hellmann's or NOMU)
4 anchovy fillets (or up to a whole small jar)

steps: Blitz the mayonnaise, water, garlic, vinegar, Worcestershire, Tabasco and anchovies until very fine, in a food processor or with a stick blender.
Chop the lettuce into large pieces, rinse and dry, and toss with the dressing.
Grate the Parmesan over, add croutons and toss again.

recipes.intro: A shortcut Caesar on a mayonnaise base, blitzed in the processor.

recipes.title: Caesar Salad with Brioche Garlic Croutons

items: Olive oil (about 1 cm deep in the pan)

steps: Chop the anchovies finely, grate the garlic just as finely and mix together.
Put the yolks in a bowl. (To avoid raw yolks, lower the whole eggs into boiling water for 1 minute, plunge into iced water, then crack the tops and spoon out the yolks.)
Beat the yolks with a balloon whisk, add the lemon juice and mustard and beat well. Gradually whisk in the oil, then the Parmesan and anchovy mix. Season with pepper.
Slice the crusts off the brioche and tear into bite-sized pieces.
Heat the oil (about 1 cm deep) and garlic in a large saucepan over moderate heat. Fry the brioche in batches until crisp and golden. Drain on paper towel.
Halve the lettuces and arrange on a platter. Top with anchovies and croutons, pour over the dressing and serve immediately.

checks: The note names a photo "JAN-Caesar salad", which suggests it is Jan Hendrik van der Westhuizen's recipe, but the source isn't written in the note.

recipes.title: Restaurant Purees: Celeriac, Carrot, Courgette & Cauliflower

items: Ricotta, to serve (500 g per 1 kg puree)

steps: Brown the butter in a large pan over high heat. Add the celeriac and cook over medium heat at least 2 hours, stirring often, until soft and the moisture has evaporated.
Toast and crush the coriander and peppercorns. Heat the milk and cream to 80°C, add the thyme and spices and infuse 1 hour. Strain.
Add half the infused milk to the celeriac and reheat gently. Blend on high (Thermomix speed 8) 3 to 5 minutes, adding the rest of the milk until silky and pipeable. Season.
Put the carrots, water, butter and salt in a saucepan, boil, then cover and simmer on low 20 minutes until tender.
Lift into a blender with a slotted spoon, add ½ cup cooking liquid and 1 tbsp lemon juice and blend smooth, adding liquid as needed. Season with salt and lemon.
Trim the courgettes, keeping only the green skin. Heat the oil, add the chopped skin and cook on high 5 to 10 minutes.
Strip the thick basil stems and chop the rest. Add the basil, chives, salt and garlic and sweat 5 minutes more.
Blend on high 3 minutes, adding up to 50 ml water if needed. Season and chill quickly over ice. To serve, mix 1 kg puree with 500 g ricotta.
Heat the butter and oil in a large pan over high heat. Add the cauliflower, cover with a cartouche and sweat 20 minutes.
Remove the cartouche and cook until deeply golden and very soft.
Add the cream, Parmesan and vinegar, simmer, then take off the heat.
Blend on high 5 minutes, adding milk for a silky, spoonable texture. Season.

recipes.intro: Professional-kitchen prep notes written for a Thermomix. The celeriac, courgette and cauliflower quantities are restaurant batches; halve or quarter them at home.

recipes.title: Beef Wellington with Spinach Pancakes & Chicken Mousse

items: Egg wash (1 egg beaten with 1 tbsp water)
400 g chicken breast, cubed and semi-frozen

steps: Roughly chop the mushrooms in a food processor. Sweat the shallot in a little oil until translucent, add the garlic for a minute.
Add the mushrooms and cook over medium-high heat, stirring, until all the moisture evaporates. Season and cool.
Blend the spinach, eggs, flour and milk on high about 3 minutes until smooth. Rest 30 minutes.
Wipe a hot pan with a little oil, ladle in a little batter and swirl very thin. Cook about 45 seconds a side on low-medium without colouring. Cool.
Blitz the chicken, egg and salt in a cold food processor, scraping down, to a smooth, shiny paste. Move to a bowl set over ice.
Fold in the cold cream by hand with a firm spatula (the processor would split it). Keep refrigerated, then fold in the cooled duxelles.
Season the beef and sear in a very hot pan until dark golden all over, 2 to 3 minutes a side. Cool.
Wrap tightly in cling film and chill at least 30 minutes. Unwrap and brush with Dijon.
Lay the spinach pancakes on a sheet of cling film, overlapping, about 2 cm wider than the beef on all sides.
Spread a 2 cm layer of the mousse-duxelles mix over the pancakes, lay the beef on top and roll up tightly in the cling film. Chill 30 minutes.
Unwrap, place on the puff pastry and roll, sealing the edges. Trim the excess and tuck in the ends. Brush with egg wash.
Preheat the oven to 220°C. Bake on a lined tray 12 minutes, then reduce to 180°C for about 22 minutes more, until the core reads about 30°C for medium-rare.
Rest 10 minutes before slicing.

recipes.src: Notes app (#recipe), notes from a YouTube video
recipes.intro: The full restaurant version: the fillet is wrapped in thin spinach crêpes and a layer of chicken-mushroom mousse before the pastry, which keeps the pastry crisp.
checks: The note gives two core temperatures (30°C, then "38-45°C"); 30°C out of the oven rises during resting. Use a probe and check your target.

recipes.title: Charred Cabbage with Miso Butter

items: 1 savoy or green cabbage, cut into wedges

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C and slowly heat a cast-iron or heavy pan on the stove.
Put the cabbage wedges cut-side down in the dry pan and weigh them down (a small tray with something heavy on top). Cook a few minutes until well charred, then turn, cover and char the other side.
Mix everything for the miso butter except the water, then add hot water a spoonful at a time until it's like yoghurt.
Uncover the cabbage and pour the miso butter evenly over the top.
Cover again and bake 15 to 20 minutes until tender, uncovering for the last few minutes to colour. Sprinkle with sesame seeds.

recipes.src: Notes app (#recipe), food blog post dated 2 October 2022
recipes.intro: Budget-friendly and packed with umami. An amazing side dish, or serve simply with steamed rice and kimchi.

recipes.title: Chef's Beef Bourguignon

items: 750 g chuck, off the bone, cubed
250 g small button mushrooms, stems trimmed and quartered

steps: Lightly dust all the meat in the seasoned flour and tap off the excess.
Heat oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat and brown the meat on all sides in batches. Set aside.

Add a bit more oil and the onion, carrots, garlic and tomato purée. Turn off the heat and put the lid on so the vegetables steam; halfway through, add the thyme, parsley stems and bay. Scrape up the brown bits, then remove the vegetables.
Add the whole bottle of wine and reduce by half.
Return the meat, vegetables and herbs and cover with the stock. Bring to a simmer, cover with a cartouche and the lid and braise in a 160°C oven for 4 to 6 hours, until very tender.
Cool the meat in the liquid. Strain, keeping the meat and discarding the vegetables and herbs.
Reduce the liquid to a coating consistency, skimming off the fat.

In a sauté pan, cook the mushrooms in a little butter until tender; set aside. In the same pan, crisp the lardons; remove and keep the fat. Cook the pearl onions in the fat with a nub of butter until tender and golden.
Return the meat and garnish to the sauce, warm through, scatter with parsley and serve with mash.

recipes.src: Notes app (#recipe), notes from a chef's video guide
recipes.intro: For anyone who wants to learn how chefs build flavour. Three cuts of beef, braised until falling apart, with the garnish cooked separately and added at the end.

recipes.title: Chilli Crisp Oil

steps: Heat the oil on high, add the onion and fry until golden. Add the fresh chilli and ginger.
Reduce the heat slightly and add the garlic, Szechuan pepper, star anise, cinnamon, cumin and dried chilli. Cook until caramelised and crispy.
Turn off the heat, then slowly add the sugar, vinegar, MSG and soy, taking care the oil doesn't boil over.
Cool slightly, then ladle into jars, about half oil and half bits. Seal and keep in the fridge.

recipes.intro: Just use a big pot.

recipes.title: Fried Chicken Kit: Brine, Seasoned Flour, Chipotle Mayo & Dill Pickles

items: 1 chipotle pepper plus a little adobo sauce

steps: Brine: dissolve the salt in the water, add the hot sauce and brine the chicken in the fridge.
Flour: mix everything together and dredge the drained chicken before frying.
Chipotle mayo: blend the mayo, chipotle, adobo and lime and season with salt.
Pickles: bring the vinegar, water, salt and spices to the boil, pour over the cucumbers and dill in a jar and cool.

recipes.intro: The building blocks for proper fried chicken, written as ingredient lists only.
checks: The note gives no methods, brining time or frying temperature; the steps above are standard and not from the source.

recipes.title: Quick Pickling Brine

steps: Heat everything until the sugar and salt dissolve, then pour over sliced vegetables in a jar.

checks: The note has no salt or garlic amounts and no method.

recipes.title: Bertus Basson's Steamed Pork & Rice

steps: Cut the pork into lardons about 1 cm wide and render in a saucepan over medium heat. Keep the rendered fat.

Bring the rice to the boil in 1 litre seasoned water (4 parts water to 1 part rice) over high heat. When the water drops just below the rice, add the green beans, baby corn, peas, lardons and the reserved fat.
Cover and steam 5 to 6 minutes.
Thinly slice the spring onion and coriander. In the lardon pan, cook the eggs over low heat until the whites are set but the yolks still runny.
Serve the eggs over the rice with generous chilli crisp, coriander and spring onion. Season with soy and lime.

recipes.intro: A one-pot rice dish where the vegetables steam on top of the rice. Don't rinse the rice; the starch is part of the dish.
checks: 1 litre of water to 250 ml rice is 4:1, which is a lot for jasmine rice; the note says to steam once the water drops below the rice, so watch it rather than the clock.

recipes.title: Bazaar Pancakes with Cinnamon Sugar

steps: Sift the flour, baking powder and salt into a mixing bowl.
Beat the eggs, milk, water, lemon juice and oil together in another bowl.
Make a well in the dry ingredients, pour in the egg mixture and beat with a balloon whisk until there are no lumps. Cover with a tea towel and rest 30 minutes.
Bring a large pot of water to the boil, lower to a simmer and put a large plate over it, with a lid ready. This keeps the pancakes warm.
Mix the sugar and cinnamon.
Heat a 24 cm non-stick crêpe pan. Ladle in batter and swirl to cover the base. Cook about 1 minute, turn and cook another minute.
Put each pancake on the warm plate, sprinkle with cinnamon sugar and cover. Repeat with the rest of the batter.
Serve warm with lemon wedges.

recipes.intro: Church-bazaar pancakes: thin, rolled with cinnamon sugar and served with lemon.

recipes.title: Bacon & Pea Risotto Balls

steps: Boil the peas for 2 minutes and refresh in iced water.
Blitz with a pinch of salt, a splash of olive oil and 50 ml of the stock to a purée. Set aside.
Heat the stock and keep it warm.
Melt 4 tbsp butter in a heavy pan. Soften the onion, then add the garlic and bacon and fry lightly.
Add the rice with a good splash of olive oil and stir to coat.
Add the stock a ladle at a time, letting the rice absorb each ladle before adding the next.
When all the stock is in, stir in the pea purée, the last 2 tbsp butter and the Parmesan (see note). Spread in a loaf tin and refrigerate overnight.
Heat the oil over medium heat in a deep pan.
Roll the cold risotto into balls. Roll in flour, dip in egg (let the excess drip off) and coat in panko.
Fry until golden and drain on paper towel. Serve with extra pea purée if you like.

recipes.intro: From the canapé episode of Padkos. Make the risotto the day before; cold risotto rolls far better.
checks: The script lists Parmesan but never says when to add it. Stirring it in at the end is standard.

recipes.title: Pork Ribs with Turmeric Gnocchi, Charred Corn & Smoked Cream Cheese

items: Butter, olive oil and basil, for frying
Rub of salt, pepper, mushroom powder and dried basil
Pumpkin seeds, oiled, salted and roasted, to garnish

steps: Warm the cream cheese gently with a fig leaf for 5 minutes. Remove the leaf, put the cheese in a metal bowl and refrigerate for 2 hours to set.
Smoke for 15 minutes with another fig leaf or two on the smoker. Cool and set aside.
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Prick the potatoes all over and bake on a bed of coarse salt for 30 minutes.
Halve and press through a sieve, skin side up. You want about 400 g potato.
Mix in the Parmesan, flour, turmeric, egg and salt.
Roll into 10 cm logs, dust with flour, roll tightly in clingwrap and tie both ends, squeezing out the air.
Poach the logs for 8 minutes, then plunge into iced water.
Slice, dust with flour and fry in olive oil, butter and basil until golden.
Rub the mielies with oil and salt and grill slowly over medium heat until charred in places. Cut off the kernels and keep the cobs.
Melt butter in a deep pan, add the cobs, basil and whey and simmer 5 minutes.
Add the cream, simmer 3 minutes more and strain.
Coat the ribs in the rub and leave for a few hours or overnight.
Braai over the coals until almost cooked, then cut into ribs and cool.
Brown in a pan with olive oil and butter, add the stock and reduce to a glaze.
Add the corn kernels to the frying gnocchi, pour in the corn sauce and let it reduce.
Plate the gnocchi with the ribs, smoked cream cheese and pumpkin seeds.

recipes.af: Varkribbetjie met Borrie-gnocchi en Gebraaide Mielies
recipes.intro: A Padkos plate with four parts: smoked fig-leaf cream cheese, turmeric gnocchi, a corn-cob and whey sauce, and glazed spare ribs.

recipes.title: Shake-Your-Brisket Gatsby

items: 1 x 440 ml beer (an ale works well)
50 ml mango atchar oil (from the top of the jar), plus 1 tsp atchar to stir in
½ chilli, deseeded and finely chopped
Long rolls, split and lightly toasted

steps: Pound the spices and salt in a pestle and mortar.
Rub the brisket with olive oil, then the spice mix. Wrap in foil and leave for 2 to 3 hours.
Preheat the oven to 90°C. Put the brisket fat-side up in a roasting pan and pour the beer around it (not over).
Cover with foil and cook for 10 hours.
Remove the foil, turn up to 120°C and cook 30 minutes more. Serve hot or cooled.
Make sure everything is at room temperature. Whisk the yolks with salt and pepper, then the mustard and lemon juice.
Whisk in the olive oil bit by bit, then the atchar oil, until thick. Stir in a teaspoon of atchar.
Mix all the salsa verde ingredients and toss through the lettuce.
Cut the potatoes into thin strips with a peeler and deep-fry until crisp. Drain.
Fill the rolls with mayo, salsa verde lettuce, brisket and chips.

recipes.intro: The Cape Town Gatsby, Padkos-style: 10-hour beer brisket, mango atchar mayo, salsa verde lettuce and shoestring chips in a long roll.

recipes.title: Churros with Butterscotch Sauce

items: Cinnamon and castor sugar, for coating
150 g molasses sugar (or dark brown sugar)

steps: Heat the oil to 160°C.
Bring the water to the boil, add the flour, sugar, butter and salt and beat with a wooden spoon into a stiff paste. Cool.
At room temperature, beat in the eggs.
Mix cinnamon and castor sugar in a bowl.
Pipe the mixture through a large star nozzle straight into the oil and fry until golden.
Drain and toss in the cinnamon sugar.
Melt the butter and sugar slowly until the sugar dissolves.
Add the vanilla and cream and simmer gently. Watch it doesn't boil over.

recipes.src: Padkos Episode 12 script; Padkos book page (photographed)
recipes.intro: Food-truck churros: crisp, cinnamon-sugared and dunked in butterscotch.

recipes.title: White Chocolate Blondies

items: ½ cup butter, at room temperature

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Butter and line a 20 x 20 cm tin.
Melt the butter and chocolate chips together and cool to room temperature.
Mix in the egg, condensed milk, vanilla and 1 tsp salt.
Fold in the flour until just combined. Don't overmix.
Pour into the tin, sprinkle with the 2 tsp salt and bake 30 minutes. It will puff in the middle.
Cool 10 minutes in the tin, then on a rack. Dust with icing sugar once completely cold.

recipes.src: Padkos Episode 16 script; VIA launch recipes
recipes.intro: Condensed-milk blondies with a salty top, from the last episode of Padkos.

recipes.title: Chocolate Truffle Vetkoek

items: Icing sugar and cocoa, for rolling and dusting

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, then add the water gradually to a manageable dough.
Knead about 8 minutes until smooth. Oil, cover and leave somewhere warm to double, about 2 hours.
Knock back, roll into a 4 cm log, pinch off 4 cm pieces and flatten to 1 cm. Let rise slightly.
Bring the cream just to the boil, cool 30 seconds and pour over the chocolate. Add the vanilla and whisk smooth.
Cool to room temperature (about an hour). Scoop balls with two teaspoons onto wax paper and chill 30 minutes.
Roll in cocoa and icing sugar and chill again.
Wrap each truffle in a piece of dough and deep-fry until golden.
Drain on paper towel and dust with cocoa.

recipes.intro: Vetkoek dough wrapped around a chocolate truffle and fried, so the middle melts.

recipes.title: Slow-Roast Lamb Pitas with Tomato Blatjang

items: 1 to 1.5 kg leg of lamb, bone in (or shoulder)
3 tsp Maizena, mixed with ¼ cup water

steps: Mix the yeast, sugar and salt with the water. Sift in the flour, add the oil and knead 10 minutes.
Cover with a damp cloth and rise for an hour.
Preheat the oven to 230°C. Roll into a log, cut 5 cm pieces, ball them and flatten into rounds.
Bake on a greased tray for 6 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 130°C. Brown the lamb all over in a little oil over high heat. Set aside.
Lower the heat, add the butter and cook the onions until golden. Add the garlic cut-side down for a few minutes.
Add the wine and bring to a bubble, then the stock, rosemary, bay and lemon zest. Pour into your biggest roasting tin.
Add the lamb, rub with mustard, drizzle with olive oil, scatter with cumin and season.
Cover loosely with foil and roast about 5 hours, basting a few times, until it falls off the bone.
Uncover, turn up to 200°C and roast 10 to 15 minutes until crisp.
Rest under foil for 10 to 15 minutes, then pull into big chunks.
For gravy, blot the fat off the pan juices with paper towel, stir in the Maizena mix and bring to the boil. Season.
Halve, deseed and finely chop the tomatoes. Drain in a sieve.
Fry the cumin in the oil for about 30 seconds until it pops and add to the onion and coriander.
Mix in the tomatoes, cover and chill. Salt just before serving.
Fill the pitas with pulled lamb and blatjang.

recipes.intro: From the Padkos launch episode: lamb roasted until it falls off the bone, pulled into homemade pitas with a fresh tomato blatjang.

recipes.title: Lamb Kofta & Boerewors Sosaties (notes)

items: Toasted cumin seeds, chilli, salt, black pepper
Olive oil, smoked paprika, salt, red wine vinegar

steps: Mix the kofta seasoning into the lamb and shape onto skewers.
Mix the jam and Worcestershire for the marinade and brush over the sosaties.
Stir half the mint jelly into the yoghurt for the kofta.
