To smoke the peppers, make a foil pouch with mint stalks and sawdust, poke holes along the side and put it on the Weber with the lid closed.
Thread boerewors, baby marrow and halloumi onto skewers and braai.

recipes.intro: The sosatie episode. The original script only has shot notes and few quantities, so treat this as a sketch.
checks: Incomplete source. Quantities for the spices, relish method and cooking times are missing.

recipes.title: Labneh on Bruschetta with Mint Pesto

steps: 2 to 3 days ahead: mix the yoghurt, garlic, thyme, salt and pepper. Line a bowl with muslin, pour in the yoghurt, gather the corners, twist into a tight ball and tie with string.
Hang in the fridge over a bowl for 2 to 3 days to drain.
To serve: heat a ridged pan until very hot. Butter the bread and toast both sides until golden and crisp.
Mix the olive oil, mint, garlic, lemon juice and zest. Top the warm bruschetta with labneh, drizzle with the mint pesto and season well.

recipes.intro: Hang the yoghurt for 2 to 3 days; the longer it hangs, the thicker it gets.
tips: If it hangs long enough you can roll it into balls and keep them in olive oil in the fridge for two months.
checks: The page's title is cut off at the left edge ("...as met bruschetta").

steps: Combine the sugar, cornflour, salt and yolks in a pot and whisk together.
Add the milk slowly, whisking.
Heat on low, stirring, until it boils and thickens.
Once thick, take off the heat and stir in the butter and vanilla.

items: 30 ml Knorr Brown Onion Soup powder

steps: Brown the beef well in the oil. Add the onion and fry until soft.
Add the tomatoes, paprika and herbs and cook 5 minutes.
Add the water and simmer 60 minutes.
Rub the margarine into the flour, add the herbs and enough water for a stiff dough. Shape 8 dumplings.
Drop the dumplings into the stew about 30 minutes before the end, cover and simmer until fluffy and cooked.
Mix the soup powder with a little water to a paste, stir in and simmer until thick.

recipes.title: Yellowfin Tuna with Patatas Bravas & Saffron Aioli

items: A couple of tablespoons chilli-tomato bravas sauce

steps: Season the tuna with salt, pepper and oil. Sear in a smoking-hot non-stick pan, 20 seconds a side.
Cool, brush with mustard and roll in the parsley.
In the same pan, fry the potatoes in a splash of oil with salt and pepper until coloured. Add the butter and beans and sauté, then the olives, chives and lemon juice.
Swipe bravas sauce on the plate, add the beans, potatoes and olives, top with the tuna and finish with saffron aioli and dressed herbs.

recipes.src: The Chef's Studio "How to Cook: Barcelona" menu card

recipes.title: Chef Matt's Seafood Paella

items: White wine (or 50 ml water for steaming)
Handful of parsley and thyme, chopped

steps: Sweat the onion and garlic in the oil in a paella pan until soft.
Add the chorizo, season and fry until browned. Add the saffron, paprika and tomatoes and cook until almost dry, then stir in the rice.
Bring the stock to the boil, add ¾ of it and boil 5 minutes, then simmer without stirring for about 8 minutes.
Add the prawns (and octopus) and cook 5 minutes more until the rice is done, topping up with stock if dry.
Meanwhile steam the mussels with about 50 ml water in a covered saucepan over high heat for a couple of minutes until open. Strain and cover. Repeat with the clams.
Top the paella with the mussels and clams and scatter with parsley.

recipes.src: The Chef's Studio "How to Cook: Barcelona" menu card

recipes.title: Simple Lemon Syrup

items: Lemons (enough for ½ cup juice, about 3)

steps: Zest 2 lemons into a small saucepan with a Microplane, avoiding the white pith.
Juice the lemons and strain; you want about ½ cup.
Add the sugar and water to the zest and stir over medium heat until dissolved, about 1 minute. Don't let it boil.
Strain the syrup into the lemon juice and stir. Discard the zest.

recipes.intro: For lemonade, cocktails or drizzling over fruit salad.
checks: The number of lemons is cut off in the screenshot.

recipes.title: Matt Manning's Cauliflower Cheese Soup with Parmesan Toasties

steps: Sweat the onion, thyme and garlic in the oil until soft.
Add the cauliflower and butter and season with salt.
Add the stock and cook on high until reduced by half.
Add the milk, cream and Parmesan and bring to the boil.
Blitz until smooth, pass through a sieve and check the seasoning.
Slice the sourdough 1 cm thick, drizzle with the oil and grate over Parmesan. Top with another slice and toast in a griddle pan on both sides.
Bring the vinegar, wine, sugar, spices and salt to the boil and cook until the sugar dissolves.
Pack the waterblommetjies tightly into sterilised jars, pour over the warm pickle and seal while warm.
Refrigerate at least 2 weeks.
Lift out and marinate in olive oil with the lemon zest and garlic.

recipes.title: The Pan(demic) Cake

steps: Mix the rum, maple, bitters and a little cinnamon sugar over ice.
Top up with the beer and garnish with cinnamon sugar.

recipes.intro: Lockdown breakfast-for-dinner in a glass.

steps: Pour the mezcal over ice in a coupe and top with cream soda.

recipes.title: Annette Human's Instant Koeksisters

steps: Heat the sugar and water in a deep pan over low heat without a lid, stirring often until the sugar melts.
Boil slowly 7 to 8 minutes without a lid (not fast, or it gets too thick). Off the heat, stir in the lemon juice and vanilla.
Sift the flour, baking powder and salt and rub in the butter. Cut in the milk with a palette knife to a dough. Work lightly.
Roll out 5 mm thick on a floured surface, cut thin strips and plait (or use a koeksister cutter).
Heat the oil until fairly hot, not smoking. Fry 3 or 4 at a time, one side then the other, until deep golden.
Lift out and dunk straight into the syrup, which will have cooled to lukewarm.
Once soaked, drain on a rack. Eat cold.

recipes.intro: Once you have the knack, these take under an hour.

steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Lay the pastry on a work surface.
Cut the wors into lengths as long as the pastry is wide.
Place a piece of wors on the pastry and cut off enough pastry to wrap it. Brush the edge with egg, fold over and shape into a half-moon.
Place on a lined tray, brush with egg and repeat.
Bake 25 minutes until crisp. Serve warm with watercress.
Mix the cheeses. Lay out 4 tortillas and sprinkle with half the cheese.
Top each with about 4 slices ham and 5 ml pesto, then the rest of the cheese and another tortilla.
Cook one at a time in a hot non-stick pan, pressing with a spatula. Flip carefully when crisp and cook until the cheese melts.
Cut into wedges and serve warm.

recipes.title: Tomato Tart with Parmesan Catalan, Basil & Olives

items: Small knob unsalted butter, for the tin
1 sheet (30 x 12 cm) good puff pastry

steps: Mix the marinade ingredients, season lightly and infuse at room temperature for 1 hour. Preheat the oven to its lowest setting.
Score, blanch (10 seconds) and peel the tomatoes. Quarter and seed them and dry on an oven rack for 6 hours.
Marinate the dried tomatoes in the fridge overnight.
Next day, preheat the oven to 200°C. Drain the tomatoes and arrange them presentation-side down in a greased 26 x 8 cm tart tin.
Cover with the pastry, trim and seal with a fork. Pierce three times.
Bake 20 minutes, then lower to 180°C, brush with egg wash and bake 8 minutes more. Cool before turning out.
Cut into 8, warm 2 to 3 minutes and serve with a quenelle of Parmesan Catalan, semi-dried tomatoes, olives, balsamic reduction, basil oil, a shard of tuile and basil leaves.

recipes.time: 1 hr (plus 6 hr drying and overnight marinating)
recipes.intro: A restaurant-style plated tart. The Parmesan Catalan, semi-dried tomatoes, balsamic reduction, basil oil and Parmesan tuile are separate recipes in the original book.

recipes.title: Lemon Posset with Berry Consommé

items: 1 kg ripe strawberries, hulled and roughly chopped

steps: Finely grate the lemon zest, then juice and strain the lemons and measure 115 ml.
Bring the cream, zest and sugar to the boil, stirring until dissolved. Simmer 3 minutes.
Off the heat, whisk in the lemon juice. Strain into a jug, pressing the zest, and leave 5 minutes, then skim.
Pour into glasses, cool, cover and refrigerate 24 hours to set.
Mix the berries and sugar in a bowl, cover with clingwrap and set over simmering water on low heat for 1 hour.
Refrigerate for another hour, then strain through a double layer of muslin without pressing. Discard the pulp.

recipes.src: Photographed cookbook page (from the Canteen restaurant)
recipes.intro: Very simple, very impressive, and the most popular dessert at Canteen. Serve plain, with the berry consommé spooned over, or with fresh berries and chopped pistachios.

recipes.title: Air-Fryer Garlic Butter Flatbreads

steps: Preheat the air fryer to 190°C for about 5 minutes.
Mix the flour, baking powder, salt and sugar, then the yoghurt, to a soft dough. Knead briefly.
Divide into balls and flatten into rounds.
Air-fry in batches until puffed and golden on both sides.
Brush with the garlic butter (and parsley) while hot.

recipes.title: Old-Fashioned Orange-Bourbon Caramels

steps: Line a 23 cm (9-inch) square tin with baking paper, leaving overhang.
In a 3-litre heavy saucepan, combine the butter, sugar, 1 cup cream and syrup. Bring to the boil over medium-high, stirring gently.
Clip on a sugar thermometer and lower to medium. Cook without stirring 35 to 40 minutes, to 120°C (248°F, firm ball). Take off the heat.
Stir the remaining 1 tbsp cream with the bourbon, vanilla and zest and gently stir into the caramel without scraping the sides.
Pour into the tin and leave about 2 hours until firm.
Lift out, cut into 72 pieces with a buttered knife and wrap in wax paper.

tips: Keeps 2 weeks airtight at room temperature.

recipes.title: Mealie & Cheese Buttermilk Bread

items: 3 ml (a generous ½ tsp) baking powder

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C and grease a 26 x 13 cm loaf tin.
Sift the flour, salt and baking powder. Add the corn, parsley, half the cheese and the buttermilk and stir lightly with a fork.
Spoon into the tin, sprinkle with the rest of the cheese and bake 1 hour or until a skewer comes out clean.

recipes.intro: Made in a flash, for the braai or for breakfast.

recipes.title: Braaied Butter Chicken Curry

items: A big knob fresh ginger, finely chopped
A knob of fresh ginger, finely chopped

steps: Mix the marinade ingredients, add the chicken, massage well and refrigerate overnight.
Bring to room temperature, thread onto kebab sticks and braai over very hot coals to char and caramelise (not cook through), brushing with extra marinade. Cool, then cut into pieces.
Heat a no. 3 potjie over medium-high coals. Fry the onions in oil and butter until soft and browning. Add the garlic and ginger for a minute, then the spices for another minute.
Stir in the tomato purée, fish sauce and sugar, bring to a simmer over low coals and cook 20 minutes.
Optional: blitz the sauce smooth with a hand blender.
Add the chicken and simmer 15 minutes. Stir in the crème fraîche and fenugreek and season.
Rest, covered, 10 minutes. Serve with naan or rice, toasted almonds and coriander.

recipes.intro: The universal curry, taken to a whole new braai level. Pair it with a pale ale.

recipes.title: Crispy Batter Mix

items: ¾ cup cold water (add when mixing)

steps: Keep the dry mix in a jar.
When ready to fry, whisk in the water to a smooth batter, dip and deep-fry until golden.

recipes.serves: Coats about 500 g chicken or fish

recipes.title: Chocolate Marshmallow Cookie Sandwiches with Toffee Sauce

items: 200 g chocolate chips or dark chocolate, chopped
1 x 2 litre good vanilla ice cream

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C and line two trays. Cream the butter and sugars until light. Beat in the eggs one by one and the vanilla.
Sift the dry ingredients and fold in, then the chocolate and marshmallows. It's a very stiff dough.
Scoop 12 even spoonfuls onto the trays (an ice-cream scoop helps) and bake 10 to 12 minutes. Cool on a rack.
Heat the sugar and water in a deep pan over medium heat until a dark caramel forms. Don't stir.
Whisk in the butter, then the cream, and whisk over the heat to a thick sauce.
Sandwich scoops of ice cream between two cookies and serve with warm toffee sauce.

recipes.intro: The ideal dessert for guests. Bake the cookies and sauce the day before; the ice cream comes straight from the shop.

recipes.title: Massaman Beef Roast with Coconut & Coriander Sauce

items: 1 lemongrass stalk, white part only, chopped

steps: Dry-roast the whole spices 5 to 8 minutes over medium heat, then grind fine.
Blend with the fresh ingredients and oil to a paste.
Rub the meat generously with paste (keep 125 ml for the sauce). Marinate 2 days in a sealed zip-lock bag in the fridge.
Preheat the oven to 160°C. Sear the roast in butter until golden all over, then put on a baking tray and drizzle with olive oil.
Roast to your liking using a meat thermometer. Cover with foil and rest 15 to 20 minutes. Keep the pan juices.
Mix the reserved paste with the pan juices in a pot on the stove. Add the coconut milk and cook until thick.
Strain and blend with 10 g coriander. Reheat.
Serve with the pomegranate and garnish with the rest of the coriander.

checks: The page gives doneness as "rare 120-130°C, medium 135-145°C"; those match Fahrenheit internal temperatures. In Celsius aim for about 52°C rare, 60°C medium, 65°C medium-well.

steps: Cover the octopus with water in a pot, bring to the boil and boil 45 minutes.
Put in a dish, drizzle with olive oil and add garlic, salt and pepper. Leave to marinate and cool for at least an hour.
Cut the legs apart into 8 strips and return them to the marinade until ready.
Braai over medium-high heat about 4 minutes a side.
Squeeze over the lemon, season if needed and scatter with parsley.

recipes.title: Weeknight Chilli con Carne with Cream Cheese

items: 2 x 420 g tins red kidney beans, drained
1 x 250 g tub cream cheese, to serve

steps: Heat the oil in a medium pot. Add the onion, garlic and mince and stir-fry 5 to 8 minutes until browned.
Add the tomatoes, paste, chillies and herbs and cook to a thick sauce, 10 to 15 minutes. Season.
Stir in the beans and bring back to the boil. Serve hot with spoonfuls of cream cheese.

recipes.intro: The cheapest mid-week meal for feeding a crowd. Serve with warm tortillas.
tips: For nachos, spoon the sauce over a 250 g bag of nacho chips, top with 200 g grated cheddar and grill until golden. Serve with cream cheese.

recipes.title: German Coffee Cake (Streuselkuchen)

items: 150 g unsalted butter, plus extra for greasing
225 g unsalted butter, at room temperature

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Grease and line a deep 30 x 35 cm tray; line another tray with greaseproof paper.
Melt the sugar with a splash of water over high heat without stirring (swirl). Once golden, sprinkle in the coffee and pour onto the paper-lined tray to set.
Rub the streusel ingredients to fine crumbs and chill.
Cream the butter and sugar until pale, beat in the eggs one by one, then fold in the flour and baking powder. Mix in the three coffees and spread in the deep tray.
Smash the caramel and mix into the streusel. Sprinkle half over the batter; squeeze the rest into clumps and drop them over.
Bake about 35 minutes until golden and cooked. Cool 10 minutes, then on a rack.

recipes.intro: A homage to the Saxon Streuselkuchen, here with three kinds of coffee and caramel shards in the crumble. Great served still warm with coffee or tea.

recipes.title: Milk Tart with Shattered Caramel

steps: Sift the flour and icing sugar and rub in the cubed butter. Add the egg and salt, then the milk to bring it into a scruffy ball. Don't overwork. Wrap and chill 30 minutes.
Oil a deep 24 cm loose-bottomed tin. Roll the pastry ½ cm thick, line the tin, patch any holes, prick and freeze 20 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Line with clingfilm and rice or beans, bake blind 10 minutes, remove the weights and bake 10 minutes more until biscuity.
Split the vanilla pod, scrape the seeds and simmer pod and seeds in the milk for 15 minutes. Off the heat, stir in the butter.
Beat the eggs with the cornflour, flour and sugar. When the milk has cooled a little, whisk it in gradually.
Return to the pan and whisk over low heat 5 to 10 minutes until thick. Discard the pod.
Pour into the case, sift over the cinnamon from a height and bake 20 minutes. Cool on a rack.
Just before serving, melt the sugar in a pan over medium heat until lightly golden and pour over the tart to set in a thin, crackly layer.

recipes.intro: A simple, light milk tart, with an optional brûlée-like caramel poured over the top.
checks: The caramel instructions are cut off at the bottom of the photographed page; the last step is the standard finish.

recipes.title: Dry Grilled Chicken with Ginger, Greens & Noodles in Broth

items: 1 heaped tbsp fresh ginger, finely sliced
300 to 400 g Chinese greens (pak choi, Chinese broccoli, gai lan)
1 or 2 red chillies, deseeded and finely sliced

steps: Bone, skin and trim the chicken and season with salt. Cook on both sides on a very hot griddle until done. Rest 3 minutes and slice at an angle 1 cm apart.
Meanwhile bring the stock, ginger and garlic to the boil, then simmer. Steam the greens above the stock (or in it) until tender.
Cook the noodles in salted water, drain and divide among 4 deep bowls. Top with greens, then chicken, then chilli, coriander and soy.
Check the broth's seasoning and pour it over (or serve it at the table). Finish with a squeeze of lemon or lime.

recipes.title: Fresh Egg Pasta (Everyday & Special)

steps: Tip the flour onto a clean surface or into a processor or mixer and add the eggs (and yolks).
Bring together and knead to a smooth, silky, elastic dough. Add flour if sticky, a little egg if dry.
Wrap and rest about 30 minutes, then roll and cut as you like, dusting with semolina.

recipes.src: Photographed cookbook page (likely Jamie Oliver, The Naked Chef)
recipes.intro: Two doughs, one method. No salt or oil needed, just the freshest eggs and good flour. Make extra and dry it in jars.
checks: Only the first part of the method was photographed. Resting and rolling are the standard steps.

recipes.title: Pork Chops with Thyme, Lemon & Pesto

items: 4 two-rib pork loin chops (or regular chops)

steps: Pound the thyme with 1 tsp salt, then the garlic and 1 tsp pepper. Stir in the lemon juice, zest and oil.
Smear over the chops and leave at least 10 minutes.
Cook on a very hot griddle or pan, charring each side golden without burning, about 8 minutes over medium-high. Don't overcook.
Rest a few minutes and spoon pesto over. Serve with salad and mash or salt-baked jacket potatoes.

recipes.src: Photographed cookbook page (likely Jamie Oliver, The Naked Chef)
recipes.intro: Ask your butcher for a two-rib chop with one rib removed and batted out slightly. Best on a ridged griddle.

recipes.title: Proper Mayonnaise

steps: Whisk the yolk, mustard, 3 small pinches of salt, the vinegar and lemon until the salt dissolves.
Whisking fast, add the oil drop by drop. Once a quarter is in, add it a little quicker.
If it splits, whisk in a tablespoon of boiling water.
When thick and creamy, check the seasoning. Flavour with herbs or roasted nuts if you like.

recipes.title: Aïoli

steps: Smash the garlic with the salt in a pestle and mortar.
Whisk the yolk and mustard, then add the oils bit by bit, faster once a quarter is in.
Add the garlic and lemon to taste (and basil, fennel tops, dill or roasted nuts if you like) and season.

recipes.intro: Use one peppery olive oil and one mellow one. Great with cold roast pork.

recipes.title: Pesto Sauce

steps: Pound or pulse the garlic with the basil, then add the cooled pine nuts and pound again.
Turn into a bowl, stir in half the Parmesan and enough oil to bind it semi-wet but firm.
Season, add the rest of the cheese and more oil, tasting as you go. Finish with lemon if it needs it.

recipes.title: Salsa Verde

steps: Finely chop all the solid ingredients and put in a bowl with the mustard and vinegar.
Slowly stir in the oil to the consistency you like. Balance with pepper, salt and vinegar.

recipes.intro: Best chopped by hand. Keeps a day. Great with grilled, roasted or boiled meat, fish and vegetables.

recipes.title: Pickled Green Chillies

items: 1 litre white wine or rice vinegar

steps: Score each chilli from stalk to tip on one side and scrape out the seeds with a teaspoon handle.
Pour over boiling water, leave 5 minutes and drain.
Put the peppercorns, bay, coriander, chillies and salt in a large jar.
Heat the sugar and vinegar until dissolved and quite hot (not boiling) and pour into the jar.
Cool, close and refrigerate at least 2 weeks. Keeps 4 months.

recipes.src: Photographed cookbook page (likely Jamie Oliver, The Naked Chef)
recipes.intro: Brilliant in stir-fries and broths, or just with cheese and bread.

recipes.title: Bread Pudding with French Meringue & Almond Custard

items: 10 slices white bread (2 days old is best)

steps: Preheat the oven to 160°C and grease an ovenproof dish.
Cut the crusts off, spread each slice with butter and jam and cut into 4 triangles. Pack in the dish buttered side up with currants in between.
Whisk the almond milk, yolks, sugar and salt, pour over and leave 20 minutes.
Sprinkle with cinnamon and almonds and bake 40 minutes. Lower the oven to 150°C.
Stir the sugar, salt and water over low heat until dissolved (don't boil before it's dissolved).
Boil fast to hard ball (120°C). Whisk the whites stiff as the syrup gets close.
Pour the syrup in a thin stream onto the whites while whisking. Set the bowl in cold water and whisk until it holds its shape.
Spread or pipe over the pudding, scatter with almonds and bake 15 minutes at 150°C. Dust with cinnamon.
Whisk the yolks, sugar and salt and stir in the milk slowly.
Cook over very low heat or in a double boiler, stirring, until it coats the back of a spoon. Serve with the pudding.

recipes.af: Broodpoeding met Franse Meringue en Amandelvla
recipes.intro: The almond milk here is homemade: milk infused with torn peach leaves. The more leaves, the stronger the almond flavour.

recipes.title: Coconut Cake

steps: Preheat the oven to 170°C. Grease and line two 20 cm cake tins.
Beat the butter and castor sugar until light. Add a little of the milk and the yolks and beat well.
Fold in the rest of the milk, the flour and baking powder.
Whisk the whites stiff. Stir a little into the batter, then fold in the rest gently.
Divide between the tins and bake 30 to 40 minutes until cooked. Cool completely.
Spread one cake with apricot jam and put the second on top.
Topping: mix all the topping ingredients and the yolks in a pan and stir over low heat until thick. Spread over the cake and decorate with coconut shavings.

recipes.intro: "My mother says her mother was a master baker." The family letters and books are full of coconut recipes; this layered coconut cake is the one they kept.

recipes.title: Ouma's Milk Tart (Two Tarts)

items: Fine cinnamon or cinnamon sugar, to sprinkle

steps: Crust: cream the butter and sugar. Add the vanilla and egg and beat well. Fold in the flour and baking powder.
Divide the dough in two and press as thin as possible into two greased pie dishes (or roll between two sheets of baking paper). Prick all over and bake 15 to 20 minutes at 180°C until crisp. Cool.
Filling: heat the milk in a pot. Mix the sugar, cornflour and butter, stir in a little warm milk, then the rest. Stir over low heat until it starts to thicken.
Whisk the yolks, whisk in a little of the warm mixture, then return it all to the pot. Stir over medium heat until thick and smooth.
Spoon into the crusts, cool and sprinkle with cinnamon.

recipes.intro: There are many versions of the classic, but this is the one the family always uses. The great-grandmother taught how to make the crust.

recipes.title: Maple Rum Syrup

steps: Heat the syrup and butter in a small pan over medium heat, stirring until the butter melts.
Stir in the rum and use immediately.

recipes.intro: For chicken and waffles, pancakes or French toast.

recipes.title: Ouma Wessie's Homemade Ginger Beer

steps: Pour the water into a large bowl, add the sugar and stir until dissolved.
Add the yeast, ginger and raisins, mix well and pour into bottles.
Seal and stand at least 2 days. Serve ice-cold.

recipes.intro: Real ginger beer is made with yeast, sugar and raisins. Ouma Wessie always had a few bottles fermenting in old Coca-Cola bottles in her fridge, and the game was who got the most raisins in their glass.
tips: No Jamaica ginger? Use a 5 cm piece of freshly crushed ginger.

recipes.title: Eggs Benedict on Rosti with Smoked Trout

items: 2 medium potatoes, peeled and coarsely grated

steps: Squeeze the water out of the potatoes and mix with the rest of the ingredients. Season.
Heat the oil in a large non-stick pan. Set a large cookie cutter in the pan and spoon in half the mixture for a perfect circle. Once set, repeat.
Turn and fry until crisp and golden. Keep warm.
Whisk the yolks, lemon juice and mustard in a bowl over gently simmering water.
Add the butter in small splashes, whisking well each time, until thick and smooth. Season.
Bring a nearly full pot of water to the boil and add the vinegar.
Crack each egg into a small bowl and slip into the barely simmering water.
Turn off the heat, cover and leave 4 minutes. Lift out with a slotted spoon, first egg first.
Put the rosti on plates, top with trout, a poached egg and hollandaise. Finish with capers, dill, broad beans and a little paprika.

recipes.src: Snowflake, The Journal Volume 4 "Eggs for Breakfast" (screenshot)
recipes.intro: The New York classic, on a crisp potato rosti and topped with Franschhoek trout, capers and broad beans instead of ham.
tips: Keep an ice cube handy: if the hollandaise starts to split, drop it in and whisk.
Crack the egg into a fine sieve first to drain the thin whites for neater poached eggs.

recipes.title: Egg Boiling Times

steps: 6 minutes: liquid yolk and soft white. Perfect in an egg cup.
6½ minutes: soft, jammy yolk. Best for eggs on toast or soft-boiled eggs in a salad.
8 minutes: soft yolk, but firm enough to hold its own.
10 minutes: the early stage of hard-boiled, with a smidge of softness in the middle.
12 minutes: hard-boiled with a lighter yolk.
14 minutes: traditional hard-boiled, lightest yolk and firm white, but not overcooked.

recipes.title: Ice Cream Profiteroles with Dark Chocolate

items: ½ tub vanilla ice cream with roasted almonds and chocolate sauce (Spoonfulls Tin Roof)
100 g dark chocolate (Frey Supreme Dark Sea Salt)

steps: Put the water, milk, butter and sugar in a pot, cover and bring to the boil over high heat.
Add the flour all at once and stir to combine. Stir over low heat for 2 minutes until it forms a ball.
Transfer to a bowl to cool slightly. Preheat the oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with baking paper sprayed with cooking spray.

Add the beaten eggs a little at a time, mixing well after each. It will look split at first but comes together. Stop when the dough is smooth and thick and drops off the spoon when shaken; you may not need all the egg (or need a little extra if it's too thick).
Spoon into a piping bag (or ziplock bag draped over a jug) and pipe small rounds with gaps between them.
Dip a finger in water and press down the pointy tips so they don't burn.
Bake at 200°C for 25 minutes until puffed and golden. Cool.
Melt the chocolate in the microwave on defrost in 15-second blasts, stirring in between.
Halve the profiteroles, put a scoop of ice cream on each bottom half and replace the tops.
Drizzle with the chocolate and serve straight away.

recipes.title: Kick-Ass Bread with Bertus

steps: Mix the flour, yeast and sugar with the paddle attachment of an electric mixer, adding the water.
Add the salt and mix until the dough is smooth and pulls away from the side of the bowl.
Pour into a large floured container and prove until at least doubled.
Preheat the oven to 250°C. Gently pour the dough onto a floured surface and grease and flour a baking sheet.
Gently shape the loaves without knocking out the air bubbles.
Bake at 250°C for 10 minutes, then turn down to 175°C for 40 minutes.

Juice and zest of ½ lemon

recipes.title: No-Knead Bread

steps: Weigh the flour, sugar, salt and yeast into a bowl. Pour in the water, vinegar and oil and mix to a dough.
Put in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with cling wrap and leave to rise somewhere warm.
With wet hands, lift, stretch and fold a quarter of the dough at a time towards the centre. Rest 20 minutes and repeat 3 times.
After the last stretch and fold, cover and refrigerate at least 12 hours.
Heat the oven to its highest setting. Tip the dough onto a floured surface, shape gently into a square, then roll up into a rectangle. Rest while the oven heats.
Brush with water, score with a sharp knife and bake at full whack for 15 minutes, then at 200°C for about 30 minutes more.
It's done when the base sounds hollow when tapped.

recipes.time: 1 hr 30 min (plus rising and 12 hr chilling)
recipes.intro: The easiest no-fuss bread ever: all you need is a bowl, an oven and some patience.

recipes.title: Bertus's Chocolate Fondant

steps: Melt the chocolate and butter together.
Whisk the eggs and sugar until fluffy and fold the flour through.
Fold in the chocolate mixture. Rest 60 to 90 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Fill buttered moulds and bake 7 to 8 minutes, depending on the size of the mould.

recipes.title: Peanut Butter Peri-Peri Prawns

steps: Devein and butterfly the prawns (or ask your fishmonger to).
Melt the butter in an extra-large pan, sauté the prawns, then pour in the lemon juice.

Pour in the peri-peri sauce and coconut milk, bring to a simmer and season.
Serve with fresh crispy Portuguese rolls to scoop up the sauce.

recipes.title: Bacon Chipotle Lasagne in the Potjie

items: A handful of oregano, finely chopped (or 2 tbsp dried)

steps: Heat a flat pot, add a splash of oil and fry the bacon slowly so the fat renders and it crisps. Drain on paper towels.
Add the onions, celery and carrots to the bacon fat and fry until soft and browned. Add the mince and fry until the liquid cooks out and it starts to sizzle and brown.
Add the butter, herbs, garlic, chillies and paprika and fry a few minutes until fragrant. Add the tomatoes, chutney, fish sauce, beer and stock and mix well.
Lower the heat to medium-low and simmer slowly with the lid open a crack for 1½ to 2 hours, stirring now and then, until reduced and silky. Take off the heat.
Soak the pasta sheets in hot water for 10 minutes. Mix the sour cream and yoghurt.
Remove the ragu (no need to wash the pot). Spread a ladle of ragu in the pot and top with pasta, trimming sheets to fit the round pot.
Top with ragu, dollops of the cream mixture and a little bacon, cheddar and mozzarella. Repeat for 4 to 5 layers.
Finish with pasta, the cream mixture, cheddar, mozzarella, Parmesan and a little smoked paprika.

Clear a circle in the coals for the pot and surround it with medium-low coals, none touching the pot. Bake with the lid on for 30 minutes, rotating to manage hot spots, then put a few coals on the lid to brown the top. (Or bake uncovered in the oven at 180°C for 40 minutes.)
Rest at least 20 minutes before serving with salsa verde.

recipes.title: Unicorn Wings

items: Karoo Dust or Sweet and Spicy Dust

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Trim off the wing tips at the V of the joint.
Season the wings generously with the dust, drizzle with oil and roast 20 minutes to parcook. Baste with the pan juices.
Heat all the marinade ingredients in a small pot, whisking until silky. Taste: add hot sauce for more heat, or beer if too thick.

Toss in a braai bowl with the remaining marinade and a final shake of dust.

recipes.src: Darling Brew / Beer Country cookbook, p69 (photographed)
recipes.intro: Spicy, sweet and savoury, and if you char them just right you'll be riding the unicorn with every bite. Pair with a hoppy American amber.
tips: Foolproof braaied chicken: parcook chicken in the oven before it hits the grill. It cooks evenly and cuts down braai time.

recipes.title: Braaied Caesar Salad

items: Sea salt, black pepper and oil
Your favourite marinade or beer barbecue sauce
4 large slices sourdough, buttered on both sides

steps: Whisk the yolks and mustard, then slowly add the olive oil while whisking. Once emulsified, slowly whisk in the canola oil to a thick mayonnaise.
Mix in the garlic, anchovies, Parmesan and lemon. Season and chill. Thin with a splash of beer or water if too thick.
Fry or braai the bacon slowly until crisp and drain.
Season the chicken, drizzle with oil, brush with marinade and braai over medium-hot coals until caramelised and cooked through.
Toast the sourdough on both sides until golden.
Spread the bread with dressing, top with lettuce and avo, then torn chicken and bacon. Finish with Parmesan shavings and more dressing.

recipes.intro: First made on the pilot episode of Beer Country, braaiing outside Ronnie's Sex Shop in the Klein Karoo. If you're making a salad, serve it on the biggest, tastiest crouton you can find. Ronnie approved. Pair with a filtered weiss.

recipes.title: Sweet and Spicy Snoek with Braaied Rotis

items: 1 large onion, thinly sliced into rounds
6 freshly made rotis (from your local Muslim or Indian takeaway)
Sliced spring onions, fresh coriander and lime wedges

steps: Fry the onion in the oil until soft and golden. Add the garlic for a minute, then the curry powder and chilli for another minute. Add the jam, chutney and butter and stir until melted and glossy. Take off the heat.
Put the snoek skin-side down in a large flip grid. Season and baste the flesh generously. Lay the onion rings over and baste again. Close the grid snugly without squashing.
Braai flesh-side down over hot coals about 5 minutes until the marinade and onions caramelise. Flip once and cook skin-side down about 3 minutes more, until the belly bubbles.
Rest a minute, then pull the onions and flesh off the bones. Meanwhile braai the rotis until crisp.
Pile the snoek and onions on the rotis, drizzle with leftover marinade and garnish with spring onion, coriander and lime.

recipes.intro: Snoek, caught on a hand line, all teeth and fury. One of South Africa's most sustainable fish, given a sweet and spicy twist. Pair with a Belgian tripel.

recipes.title: Braaied Lamb Ribs with Citrus Rosemary Vinaigrette

items: A small handful each chopped rosemary and thyme

steps: Bring the beer to the boil and take off the heat. Dissolve the salt, then stir in the rest of the brine ingredients.
Score the skin of the ribs in a diamond pattern. Set up a Weber for indirect cooking with a large pile of charcoal or 6 to 8 pieces of wood for a 2-hour cook.

When the coals are white, arrange the ribs bone-side down on the cool side. Baste with brine, close the lid (vent above the meat) and keep it at 180 to 190°C. Baste every 30 minutes, adding coals as needed.
At 2 hours, check that the meat is tender. Remove the ribs, spread the coals and add more if needed, then braai fat-side down slowly to crisp the fat.
Rest 10 minutes. Whisk the vinaigrette ingredients and season. Serve the ribs hot and crisp with the vinaigrette.

recipes.intro: Lamb ribs reward patience with crispy fat and succulent meat; the citrus vinaigrette cuts through the richness. Pair with a West Coast IPA.

recipes.title: Tiger Slaw

items: ½ medium red cabbage, finely sliced
1 red chilli, deseeded and finely chopped
1 small knob fresh ginger, finely chopped
½ tsp very finely chopped lemongrass
A big handful of your favourite sprouts
A handful of fresh coriander, chopped

steps: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan over medium-high heat until they colour. Cool.
Mix the cabbage and carrots in a large bowl, add everything else including the sesame seeds and mix well.
Season and smash it.

recipes.intro: Not made from real tigers, but just as dangerous. Fiery, punchy, and it keeps you going back for more. Pair with a session IPA.

recipes.title: Koeksisters with Chocolate Ganache & Peanut Butter Whipped Cream

items: 150 g Lindt 70% dark chocolate, finely chopped

steps: Heat the cream gently in a medium pot until just hot enough to melt the chocolate. Add the chocolate and stir until smooth and glossy. Set aside.
Whip the sugar, vanilla and cream to soft peaks. Fold in the peanut butter and whip to stiff peaks. Add more peanut butter for more flavour.
Serve the koeksisters with both dips. Go for the ganache-to-cream double dip.

recipes.intro: The quickest, tastiest braai cheat dessert: bought koeksisters jacked up with two epic dipping sauces. Pair with a coffee stout.

recipes.title: Country Pumpkin Pie

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Roast the pumpkin in a large tray for 45 minutes until soft. Blitz to a smooth purée and stir in the cinnamon.
Blitz the biscuits to fine crumbs, add the cinnamon and butter and mix. Press half into the base of a 24 cm springform tin with a tumbler, then use the rest to build the sides. Chill 30 minutes.
Blind bake the base 8 minutes and cool completely.
Cream the butter and sugar until light. Add the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla and pumpkin purée. Sift the flour, baking powder and salt and add slowly with the machine running.
Pour into the crust and bake 45 minutes. The centre stays a little jiggly but sets as it cools. Cool completely, run a knife around the edge and unmould.
Break the bacon into shards and crush the nuts. Serve each slice with ice cream, bacon shards and nut crumble.

recipes.intro: Sweet, savoury and wrapped in a coconut-biscuit crust. A big deal in America, seldom seen on our shores. Pair with an ESB or English brown ale.

recipes.title: Cheese & Corn Bread

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C and butter an oven dish or loaf pan.
Sift the flour, salt and cayenne together. Add the spring onions and cheddar.
Mix the eggs, milk and oil separately, add with the creamed corn to the flour mixture and stir well until smooth.
Bake at 180°C for 75 minutes.

recipes.title: Apple & Pistachio Tart with Hot Milk Syrup

items: 1 tin pie apple slices (or any fruit)
A handful of pistachios (or other nuts)

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C and butter or spray a tart pan.
Beat the butter and sugar, add the eggs and whisk until light.
Sift in the flour, baking powder and salt and mix well, then add the milk and mix until smooth.
Pour into the pan and arrange the apple slices and nuts on top.
Bake 40 minutes at 180°C.
Meanwhile heat the milk, evaporated milk, sugar and vanilla in a saucepan. Pour over the hot tart as it comes out of the oven.

recipes.title: Banana Bread Doughnuts with Caramel

items: 350 g (625 ml) cake flour, plus extra for rolling
1 x 360 g tin caramel condensed milk

steps: Put the bananas, milk, sugar, butter, egg, yeast, flour and nuts in the bowl of an electric mixer and beat on high with the K-beater until it comes together in a ball.
Put in a clean bowl, cover with cling film and leave somewhere warm 45 to 60 minutes, until doubled.
Turn out onto a floured surface and press out 1 cm thick with your fingertips. Cut 3 cm rounds.
Put on a floured baking tray and leave somewhere warm until doubled, 15 to 20 minutes.
Heat the oil and fry the doughnuts 2 to 3 minutes a side until golden. Drain on paper towel.
Mix the coconut, icing sugar and cinnamon and roll the warm doughnuts in it.
Spoon the caramel into a piping bag with a 5 mm nozzle. Make a small hole in the side of each doughnut with a knife tip and pipe in caramel. Serve with extra caramel.

recipes.intro: If any of these doughnuts are left over, eat them for breakfast.

recipes.title: Peppermint Crisp Caramel Cake

items: 1 x 360 g tin caramel condensed milk
2 x 50 g Peppermint Crisp bars, finely grated
200 ml chocolate sauce of your choice

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Line a 30 x 15 cm Swiss roll tin with baking paper and spray well.
Beat the 3 eggs on high 8 to 10 minutes until thick and foamy. In another bowl whisk the whites to soft peaks and fold into the egg foam with a large metal spoon.
Gently fold in the almonds, icing sugar, flour and butter (the foam is what makes it rise). Spread in the tin and bake 12 to 15 minutes until golden and cooked. Cool in the tin and turn out.
Line a 15 x 7 cm loaf tin with cling film. Cut the sponge into 4 pieces of 15 x 7 cm.
Sprinkle the gelatine over the water and leave 1 minute.
Melt the caramel over high heat, take off the heat and stir in the soaked gelatine until smooth. Cool to room temperature, but not set.
Whip the cream to stiff peaks and fold into the caramel.
Put a sponge strip in the tin, spread with ⅓ of the filling and sprinkle with ¼ of the Peppermint Crisp. Repeat twice and finish with sponge. Keep the remaining chocolate aside.
Chill 4 to 6 hours or overnight. Turn out, peel off the cling film, pour over the chocolate sauce and sprinkle with the rest of the Peppermint Crisp.

recipes.intro: Nobody says no to this. Make it once and you'll never need another dessert. Shared alongside Ingrid Jones's story of the family Peppermint Crisp tart, always made in a long Pyrex dish.

recipes.title: No-Bake Raspberry Cheesecake

steps: Line a round 15 cm cake tin, 20 cm deep, with cling film. Sprinkle the gelatine over the water and leave until spongy.
Mix the biscuits and butter to a damp crumb and set aside.
Whisk the condensed milk, lemon juice and zest in a large bowl. Add the cream cheese and mix until smooth.
Whip the cream to soft peaks.
Fold the cream and the melted gelatine into the filling, layer with the crumb in the tin and chill until set. Top with raspberries and icing sugar.

recipes.intro: Traditionally set as a triangle; this version is easier and just as good.

recipes.title: Pineapple Beer

items: 4 to 5 litres freshly boiled water (depending on the size of the pineapples)
4 cups (800 g) sugar, or more to taste
Ice and fresh pineapple slices, to serve
Equipment: a well-washed 10-litre bucket, a dishcloth, a fine sieve or muslin, 2 x 2-litre cooldrink bottles

steps: Remove the green tops, then rinse and scrub the pineapples well.
Cut the pineapple, skin and all, into pieces.
Put in the bucket, pour over the boiling water, add the sugar and stir to dissolve.
Cover with a clean dishcloth and leave somewhere warm for 2 to 3 days. The longer it stands, the more it ferments.
Strain through a fine sieve or muslin into the bottles. Don't seal them too tightly.
Chill and serve with lots of ice and a slice of pineapple.

recipes.intro: Use both the skins and the fruit; it gives the beer a stronger flavour.

recipes.title: Baked Beignets

items: 3¾ cups flour, plus more as needed
¼ cup icing sugar, for dusting

steps: In a mixer with the whisk, combine the water, sugar and yeast. Leave about 10 minutes until foamy.
Preheat the oven to 95°C (200°F). Line 3 baking sheets with baking paper.
Add the egg, buttermilk, 3 tbsp butter, salt and vanilla and whisk to combine.
Switch to the dough hook. Slowly add the flour on medium-low until the dough comes away from the bowl, adding more flour a tablespoon at a time if needed. Knead on medium 5 minutes.
Put in a greased bowl. Turn the oven off and put the bowl inside with the door ajar to rise (keep it away from the elements).
Remove the bowl, close the door and preheat to 95°C (200°F) again.
Roll the dough about 5 mm (¼ inch) thick on a floured surface and cut 5 cm (2-inch) squares with a pizza cutter.
Put on the sheets, turn the oven off and put the sheets in with the door ajar to rise 30 minutes, covered with sprayed cling film.
Remove the sheets and preheat to 190°C (375°F). Brush the tops lightly with milk.
Bake each sheet 10 to 12 minutes until light golden. Cool 5 minutes, brush with melted butter and dust generously with icing sugar. Best warm and fresh.

recipes.intro: Light, puffy French beignets dusted with icing sugar, made a little healthier by baking instead of frying. Oven temperatures converted from Fahrenheit.
tips: To eat the next day, skip the butter and sugar and store airtight. Brush with butter, warm 10 to 15 seconds in the microwave and dust with sugar.

recipes.title: Perfect Chocolate Chip Cookies

items: ½ cup unsalted butter, at room temperature
½ cup firmly packed light brown sugar

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line 2 baking sheets with baking paper.
Sift the flour, bicarb and salt together.
In another bowl, beat the butter and sugars with an electric mixer on medium until smooth.
Add the egg and vanilla and mix on low until combined.
Gradually add the flour and mix until just incorporated. Don't overmix.
Stir in the chocolate chips with a wooden spoon, just until combined. Chill the dough if it's warm.
Scoop onto the trays, 6 to 8 per tray.
Bake one sheet at a time until the edges and bottoms are lightly browned and the tops feel firm: 8 to 10 minutes for small cookies, 10 to 13 for large.
Cool 5 minutes on the trays, then on racks.

recipes.intro: Buttery, chewy, thick and packed with chocolate chips.
tips: To avoid flat cookies, use butter at room temperature (not softened or melted) and chill warm dough. Check your bicarb isn't expired.

recipes.title: Amagwinya (Vetkoek)

items: Lukewarm water, enough for a soft dough

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, then stir in enough water to form a soft, pliable dough. Once most of the flour is incorporated, switch to your hands.
Knead until smooth and elastic, 8 to 10 minutes (or use a mixer with a dough hook).
Put in an oiled dish, cover and leave to rise until doubled.
Knock the dough down and knead back to its original size. Divide into 12 equal pieces and shape into rough circles.
Heat the oil to about 170°C. Test with a sprinkle of flour: if it sizzles and gradually browns, it's ready.
Fry, flipping to brown evenly on both sides.
Put the browned amagwinya in a pot, cover with a lid and leave 5 minutes. This keeps them soft inside with a crunchy outside.

recipes.title: MasterChef Koeksisters

steps: Bring the water, sugar and cream of tartar to the boil. Once boiling, add the lemon juice and simmer 10 minutes.
Cool to room temperature. Pour half into a bowl set over ice to cool quickly; put the rest in the fridge.
Sift the flour and baking powder and rub in the margarine with your fingertips.
Whisk the ½ egg into the water. Make a well in the flour, pour in the water mixture and mix to a dough. Knead until smooth.
Cover with cling film and rest at least 15 minutes, or up to 5 hours. Heat the oil to 160°C.

With an oiled rolling pin, roll the dough 5 mm thick on an oiled surface. Cut 6 x 15 cm rectangles and cut each lengthways into 3 strips, leaving one end uncut. Plait and press the ends together firmly.
Fry in batches of 6 for 6 to 7 minutes, until dark golden. Drain a few seconds on paper towel and keep the rest covered so they don't dry out.
Dip the hot koeksisters into the ice-cold syrup, lift out with a slotted spoon onto a wire rack.
The syrup warms with use, so halfway through swap to the second batch of syrup from the fridge.

recipes.intro: The syrup has to be ice-cold and the koeksisters hot; split the syrup and keep half in the fridge so it stays cold.

Add the chicken and brown, then the coconut milk, tomato purée, lime leaves and vegetables. Simmer until cooked.
Balance with tamarind, fish sauce, honey and salt.

recipes.title: Japanese Milk Rolls

steps: Mix the bread flour and water until smooth. Stir in a clean pot over medium heat until thick. Scrape into a bowl, cover with cling film and cool to room temperature.
Put the rest of the ingredients except the coriander in the bowl of an electric mixer, add the cooled paste and knead on medium until smooth and it comes together in a ball, 5 to 8 minutes.
Put in an oiled bowl and leave somewhere warm until doubled, 25 to 30 minutes.
Turn out on a floured surface, divide into 7 and roll each into a neat ball.
Spray a baking tray and arrange the balls in a wreath. Press a coriander leaf on each, cover with a damp tea towel and leave to rise until doubled, 12 to 15 minutes. Heat the oven to 180°C.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes until golden and cooked. Serve warm with butter.

recipes.title: Spinach, Mushroom & Ricotta Gnocchi

items: 1 x 200 g bag spinach, wilted in boiling water

steps: Heat the oil in a medium pot, add the onion and garlic and stir-fry 2 to 3 minutes until starting to brown.
Add the tomatoes and wine, lower the heat and simmer 10 to 15 minutes until thick. Blitz smooth in a food processor and season well.
Process the ricotta and wilted spinach on high until smooth. Add the Parmesan, egg and flour, mix well and season.
Bring a pot of water to the boil. Spoon the mixture into a piping bag with a 1 cm nozzle and pipe 1 cm pieces into the boiling water.
Cook until they float, then drain.
Heat the butter in a frying pan and stir-fry the mushrooms 5 to 8 minutes. Stir in the tomato sauce, then the gnocchi. Season and serve warm.

recipes.intro: A different gnocchi made without potato: a lovely dinner or light lunch.

recipes.title: Bacon, Herb & Cheese Muffins

items: 1 x 200 g packet bacon, coarsely chopped

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Sift the flour, baking powder and salt.
Heat the butter in a frying pan, add the onion and stir-fry until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add the bacon and fry until golden and crisp, 10 to 12 minutes. Stir in the herbs.
Add the cheese and bacon mixture to the flour.
Whisk the egg and milk and stir into the flour until just combined.
Spray six 250 ml ovenproof cups (or a standard 12-hole muffin pan) and divide the batter between them.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes until golden and cooked. Serve with butter and cheese.

recipes.intro: Who can say no to a warm muffin the butter melts into? These are so good they're a meal on their own.

recipes.title: Classic Caesar Salad

steps: Sauce: put the anchovies, garlic and salt in a small bowl and press-and-mix with the back of a spoon to a paste. Add the yolks, lemon juice, mustard and Worcestershire and keep mixing until combined.

recipes.title: Homemade Butter

Put the butter in a clean bowl and work with a wooden spoon until smooth and creamy.

recipes.title: Smoked Trout Mille-Feuille

steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Lay a sheet of phyllo on the work surface and brush with butter. Top with another sheet and brush again. Repeat with all the pastry.
Put a 30 cm cake tin on the pastry and cut out a circle. Use a 15 cm cookie cutter to cut a smaller circle in the middle, leaving a ring.
Put the ring on a lined baking tray and bake 20 minutes until golden and crisp. Cool.
Meanwhile peel the celery into ribbons with a vegetable peeler and put in iced water for 2 minutes. Mix the cream cheese and horseradish.

Separate four layers of the baked pastry and put on a platter. Spread with a few spoonfuls of the cream cheese, then a quarter of the trout, some drained celery ribbons, cucumber, salad leaves and sprouts.
Top with four more layers of pastry and repeat until everything is used, ending with filling. Serve.

recipes.title: Chef Matt's Carbonara

200 g streaky bacon, cut into lardons (Matt uses Richard Bosman bacon)

Press flat with your hands to about 1 cm thick. Spread with pesto and crumble over the feta.

Halve the onions and press into the dough. Drizzle with oil and sprinkle with salt.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes until golden and crisp. Cool slightly, turn out and serve lukewarm.

recipes.src: Afrikaans menu cookbook, "Laatmiddagkuier" menu (photographed; tips signed "Herman sê")
recipes.intro: If there's a shortcut in the kitchen, take it. The secret is a high oven so it gets a lovely golden crust.
tips: Swap the pesto for sun-dried tomatoes in oil, puréed with their oil to a coarse paste.

recipes.title: Peppermint Crisp Tart

items: 4 x 80 g slabs mint crisp chocolate

steps: Process the biscuits to fine crumbs, add the butter, mix and press into a 20 x 20 cm dish.
Soak the gelatine in the water until spongy.
Beat the caramel and cream cheese in an electric mixer until well mixed. Gradually add the cream and beat well.
Chop the chocolate very finely in a food processor (or grate it).
Dissolve the gelatine in the microwave, or over a bowl of boiling water, until melted.
Add the chocolate and gelatine to the filling and whisk well. Pour over the base and chill until set. Garnish with chocolate curls.

recipes.src: Photographed cookbook page, p212 (title not visible)

recipes.title: Snowflake Apple Pie

items: 1 x 385 g tin sliced pie apples

steps: Cream the butter and castor sugar. Add the egg and beat until light and fluffy.
Sift the flour and salt and fold into the butter mixture, alternating with the milk.
Turn into a greased 23 cm pie dish and arrange the apple slices on top. Mix the sugar and cinnamon and sprinkle over.
Bake at 180°C for about 40 minutes.
Syrup: heat the sugar and milk and bring to the boil until the sugar melts. Off the heat, add the essence.
Pour over the pie as it comes out of the oven. Serve hot, with custard if you like.

recipes.intro: The classic recipe off the back of the flour packet, with a hot milk syrup poured over.
tips: Use 3 peeled, cored and sliced fresh green apples instead of the tin.

recipes.title: Must-Make Salsas

steps: Purée everything in a food processor on high until smooth and creamy. Season.
Bring the vinegar, peppercorns, chillies and sugar to the boil. Put the radishes in a small glass bowl and pour over the hot vinegar. Cool to room temperature.
Mix everything together and season well.

recipes.src: Afrikaans menu cookbook, "Soort van Meksikaans" menu, p183 (photographed)
recipes.intro: Make plenty and serve in small bowls on crushed ice. Your guests will think you're very fancy. Lay a colourful table and drink tequila.

recipes.title: Orange & Raspberry Margarita Punch

steps: Crush the raspberries and sugar in a large bowl with a potato masher.
Put in a large punch bowl (or a big glass jar) and pour the ice over. Add the rest of the ingredients, stir and serve.

recipes.src: Afrikaans menu cookbook, "Soort van Meksikaans" menu (photographed)
recipes.intro: Hot summer days call for something with a kick. Very refreshing and it'll quench your thirst in minutes. For a virgin version, leave out the tequila.
tips: Frozen raspberries work: thaw them before crushing with the sugar and add the juice from the packet too. Any berry in season works.

recipes.title: One-Pot Creamy Cauliflower Soup

items: 1 large head cauliflower, trimmed and roughly chopped
A generous pinch of salt and black pepper
Flash-fried mushrooms and toasted hazelnuts, to serve (optional)

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion (and leeks) 8 to 10 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and sage and cook another minute.
Add the cauliflower, stock and milk and simmer 15 minutes until the cauliflower is tender.
Off the heat, cool slightly and blend smooth. Season and serve in warm bowls, topped with golden mushrooms and toasted hazelnuts if you like.

recipes.intro: Speedy, full of goodness and endlessly comforting. Officially soup weather in Cape Town.
checks: The leeks are listed but the method only mentions the onion; cooking them together is assumed.

recipes.title: Yorkshire Pudding

steps: Preheat the oven to 220°C.
Pour a tablespoon of oil into each mould of a greased muffin tin and heat in the oven at least 10 minutes.
Blitz the eggs in a blender until frothy, add the milk and blitz again.
Gradually add the flour until you have a pouring-cream consistency. Season and rest 10 minutes.
When the oil is smoking hot, open the oven and pour the batter into the moulds.
Close the door and cook 10 minutes, then turn down to 180°C and cook another 15 minutes. Don't open the door until they're golden and crisp.
Remove from the oven and out of the tin.

recipes.src: The Chef's Studio Instagram recipe card (screenshot)
recipes.intro: An English savoury "pancake" that can be served many ways. The Chef's Studio's favourite: with onion gravy.

recipes.title: Wild Coast Seafood Potjie with Dombolo

items: 1 tbsp cornflour, dissolved in ⅓ cup water
500 g yellowtail, cut into large chunks
A handful of flat-leaf parsley, chopped

steps: The dombolo take a while, so start them first. Whisk the flour, sugar, yeast and salt in a large bowl. Add the water and melted butter and mix to a dough.
Knead on a clean surface for 8 minutes until soft and supple. Oil the bowl, return the dough, cover and prove until doubled.
Turn out and divide into 7 equal balls. Put a ball in each greased enamel cup.
Heat oil and butter in the flat pot and soften the leeks, celery, fennel, garlic, ginger and thyme.
Add the stock, lager, fish sauce and sugar and simmer. Stir in the cornflour mixture to thicken.
Add the seafood and cream, set the dombolo cups in the pot, cover and steam until the dombolo are cooked and the seafood is just done.
Finish with parsley, spring onion, lemon, celery salt and pepper.

recipes.time: 20 min prep, plus dombolo proving, 1 hr cooking
recipes.intro: Greg's ode to the seafood buffet with white parsley sauce on everything that he grew up eating on Transkei holidays.
checks: Only the start of the method was photographed (up to dividing the dough). The potjie steps after that are assumed from the ingredient list, not from the book.

recipes.title: Miso Caramel Doughnuts

items: 350 g (625 ml) cake flour, plus extra for rolling

steps: Put the water, milk, sugar, butter, eggs, yeast and flour in an electric mixer and beat on high with the K-beater until the dough forms a ball.
Put in a clean bowl, cover with cling film and leave somewhere warm 45 to 60 minutes until doubled.
Turn out on a floured surface and press 1 cm thick. Cut 8 cm rounds and a 2 cm hole in the middle of each.
Put on a floured tray and leave somewhere warm until doubled, about 30 minutes.
While the dough rises, bring the topping ingredients to the boil in a pot and cook 3 to 5 minutes to a caramel-like sauce.
Heat the oil and fry the doughnuts 3 to 5 minutes a side until golden. Drain on paper towel.
Dip in the warm caramel and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

recipes.intro: Miso became the buzzword of MasterChef Australia: fermented soybean paste with a salty, sweet character. The caramel tastes almost like salted caramel, with the miso balancing the sweetness.
checks: Read from a photo of small, angled magazine print; double-check amounts.

recipes.title: Mojito Cake

items: Zest of 2 limes, plus extra to decorate
250 g cream cheese, at room temperature

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Put the eggs and sugar in the bowl of an electric mixer and set over a pot of boiling water. Whisk until lukewarm (test with your fingertip).
Move the bowl to the mixer and beat on high 8 to 10 minutes until thick and foamy. Meanwhile line two 18 cm loose-bottomed tins with baking paper and spray well.
Add the butter, vanilla and flour to the egg mixture and fold in gently with a spatula. Divide between the tins and bake 25 to 30 minutes until golden and cooked.
Syrup: while the cakes bake, bring the syrup ingredients to the boil. Pour over the warm cakes and cool.
Icing: beat the ingredients until light and creamy. Put one cake on a plate and spread with half the icing. Put the second cake on top, flat side up, and pipe small rosettes with the rest.
Decorate with extra mint and lime zest.

recipes.intro: This sponge will be a hit in your house. Change the flavour with the syrup you pour over it.

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Line a 23 x 23 cm tin with baking paper and grease.
Combine the flour, bicarb, cornflour and salt.
Heat the butter in a pan until brown and foamy.
Whisk the sugars in a stand mixer with the whisk attachment, adding the butter on high.
Add the eggs one at a time, whisking between each, then the vanilla.
Whisk in the dry ingredients until just combined. Fold through the chocolate and strawberries.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely in the tin, about 1 hour.
Ripple cream: simmer the strawberries, lemon juice and sugar until jammy (add a dash of water to loosen). Cool and fold through the whipped cream.

recipes.title: Steak Tartare Sandwich on Mosbolletjie

steps: Mix the beef with all the other tartare ingredients by hand. Correct the seasoning and refrigerate.
Mix the anchovy into the mayonnaise and refrigerate while you make the toast.
Toast the mosbolletjie slices and make sandwiches with a smear of anchovy mayo and a thick layer of tartare.
Trim the crusts to make them pretty (the trimmings are a treat for the chef).

recipes.intro: Inspired by a Joe Beef (Montreal) recipe seen on Mind of a Chef with David Chang. Steak tartare between two slices of bread makes perfect sense. Mosbolletjie's sweet aniseed flavour works brilliantly with the beef.

recipes.title: Another Spoonful Pudding

steps: Cream the butter and sugar. Add the beaten eggs.
Dissolve the bicarb in the milk and add with the jam.
Sift in the dry ingredients and add the egg mixture. Add the vanilla and pour into an ovenproof dish.
Bake in a moderate oven at 180°C for 45 minutes, until light brown.

checks: The method is printed as it appears; with 1 litre milk and only cornflour as the starch it bakes like a set custard. Check before making.

recipes.title: Chef Shanice's Lamb Curry

steps: In a big pot over medium heat, cook the onion until golden.
Add the cardamom, cinnamon and cloves, then the hot and medium curry powders.
Add the cumin, coriander, garam masala and turmeric.
When it smells fragrant and not burnt, add the meat, then the ginger and garlic.
Turn the stove to low. Add the water gradually with the potatoes, stirring continuously to mix the spices and meat together.
Simmer until the meat is tender and flavourful. Add chopped coriander before serving.
Serve with rice or roti and cucumber raita.

recipes.src: The Chef's Studio Instagram recipe card (screenshot)
recipes.intro: The key to a good curry: low and slow.
checks: The card lists "10 x tbsp hot curry powder" and "6x tbsp medium"; that is a lot of curry powder, so taste as you go. The garlic quantity isn't given.

recipes.title: Savoury Crêpe Stack with Spinach, Feta & Mushrooms

items: 300 g spinach, finely shredded and wilted
1 small bunch spring onions, thinly sliced
½ cup smooth low-fat cottage cheese

steps: Pour the flour onto a clean surface and make a well. Break in the eggs, then whisk in the milk, then the mustard, butter, brandy and salt.
Heat a medium non-stick pan until very hot (spray if you like). Ladle in a little batter and tilt to spread. Fry 1 minute, flip and brown the other side. Stack between sheets of greaseproof paper.
Preheat the oven to 160°C. Combine the filling ingredients.
Put a warm crêpe in a greased pie dish and layer filling on top. Repeat with the remaining crêpes and filling.
Cover with foil and bake 30 minutes, then uncover and bake 20 minutes more. Garnish with spring onion.

recipes.intro: From a TASTE piece on crêpes by food editor Abigail, who remembers church bazaar ladies flipping pancake after pancake on gas burners.
tips: Wine pairing suggested: Klein Roosboom Merlot.

Other ideas from the article: apricot jam and lemon folded into triangles; two crêpes with cream and strawberries folded into a square pocket with maple syrup; mushrooms, cream, Gruyère and ham folded into quarters and baked 5 minutes at 180°C; lemon zest in the batter and lemon curd inside; tinned apple slices cooked into the batter with honey and Greek yoghurt.

recipes.title: Lamb Boerewors Baked in Batter with Chilli Tomato & Onion Sauce

steps: Preheat the oven to 230°C. Blend the eggs, milk, water, flour and salt and chill while you cook the boerewors.
Grease a 25 x 18 x 2.5 cm baking pan. Cut the boerewors to fit, add a few rosemary sprigs and bake 10 minutes until it starts to colour.
Whisk the batter if needed, pour over the boerewors and bake 15 minutes more until puffed and golden.
Heat the tomato and onion with the chilli in a saucepan until warmed through. Serve with the boerewors.

recipes.intro: A South African toad-in-the-hole for a Thursday night. Wine suggested: Spice Route Pinotage 2011.

recipes.title: Eggs Benedict Pizza

items: 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, plus 1 tbsp for brushing
200 g lightly smoked trout, thinly sliced

steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Sift the salt and sugar with the flour, add the yeast and combine.
Add the olive oil to the water, add to the flour, mix and knead 10 minutes until smooth. Roll into a ball.
Press the dough with your finger: if it springs back quickly it's kneaded enough; if not, knead 5 minutes more.
Put in a greased bowl, cover with a clean cloth and leave somewhere warm 45 minutes, until doubled.
Knock down, roll out on a lightly floured surface, put on a baking tray, brush with oil and season. Bake 15 minutes.
Bring a pan of water to the boil and add the vinegar. Swirl a whirlpool, crack in 1 egg and cook 3 to 4 minutes. Lift out and repeat.
Blanch the asparagus in salted boiling water 45 seconds and refresh in iced water. Repeat with the spinach.

Hollandaise: set a bowl over simmering water (not touching). Whisk the yolks and water until pale and thick. Whisk in the butter a piece at a time; it thins at first, then thickens to lightly whipped cream. Off the heat, whisk in the lemon, salt and pepper.
Top the base with spinach, then the eggs, asparagus and trout. Season and drizzle with hollandaise.
Grill 5 minutes until the hollandaise browns. Serve immediately.

recipes.intro: Wine suggested: Villiera Cru Monro Brut Méthode Cap Classique 2007.

recipes.title: Tomato & Bread Salad with Anchovies and Capers

items: 6 anchovy fillets in oil, drained and finely chopped (about 20 g)
⅓ tsp flaked salt, plus extra to finish
100 g sourdough, crusts on, sliced 2 cm thick, lightly toasted and cut into 4 cm chunks
500 g ripe tomatoes, cut into 4 cm chunks
1 lemon: finely grate 1 tsp zest, then juice to get 2 tsp
5 g basil leaves, finely chopped, plus a few to serve
1 tsp Urfa chilli flakes (or ½ tsp other chilli flakes)

steps: Put the garlic, anchovies and oil in a medium saucepan with the salt over low heat. Cook gently 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the garlic and anchovies soften when mashed. Don't let it bubble or the garlic burns.
Off the heat, add the toasted bread and toss to coat. Move the bread to a large bowl, leaving the oil in the pan.
Mix the tomatoes, lemon zest and juice, capers, parsley and basil.
To serve, add the tomatoes to the bread and toss carefully. Transfer to a platter, drizzle with the remaining anchovy oil and finish with chilli flakes and flaked salt.

recipes.src: Photographed cookbook page, "Raw Veg" chapter p33 (very likely Yotam Ottolenghi's SIMPLE)
recipes.intro: Get as big a range of tomatoes as you can for a clash of colour. Good every day through summer, alone or with a thin tuna steak. The toasted bread keeps 4 hours and the tomatoes 6 hours in the fridge (hold back the basil); assemble just before serving.

recipes.title: No-Bake Lemon Meringue Cheesecake

items: 500 g cream cheese, at room temperature

steps: Grease and line a 22 cm loose-bottomed tin. Mix the biscuits and butter, press into the base and about 3 cm up the sides, and chill 30 minutes.
Sprinkle the gelatine over the lemon juice, leave a few minutes, then melt in the microwave to dissolve.
Beat the cream cheese, sugar and zest, then add the slightly cooled gelatine mixture. Beat in the soured cream and fold in the whipped cream.
Spoon into the crust and chill at least 2 hours to set. Spread the lemon curd carefully on top.
Whisk the whites, cream of tartar and sugar in a heatproof bowl over simmering water until the sugar dissolves and it reaches 70°C.
Off the heat, beat on medium-high about 5 minutes until thick, glossy and cool.
Swirl over the lemon curd like clouds, scorch with a blowtorch and dust with icing sugar.
Mix everything in a saucepan over low heat, stirring constantly until it thickens and starts to boil gently. Strain and cool.

checks: The lemon curd lists no sugar; check the original before making it.

recipes.title: Raisin Rusks (Not Sweet, Slightly Salty)

items: 500 g margarine or butter, softened overnight at room temperature
About 1.5 litres lukewarm water, added bit by bit

steps: Mix the dry ingredients and rub in the margarine.
Add the water little by little and knead well until your hands come away dry.
Leave to rise fully in the bowl you kneaded in.
Knock down, shape into balls and pack into pans. Leave to rise fully again.
Bake about 1 hour at 180°C, then dry out well.

recipes.intro: A big-batch buttermilk-free rusk: not sweet, slightly salty. Leave the margarine out of the fridge overnight; don't melt it in the microwave.
tips: In winter, warm the flour slightly in the microwave first; the dough rises more easily.

recipes.title: Royal Pasta Dough

items: 400 g good-quality Tipo 00 flour, plus extra for dusting

steps: Pile the flour and semolina into a large bowl and make a well. Separate the eggs and put the yolks in the well (freeze the whites for meringues).
Add the oil and 4 tbsp cold water and whip with a fork until smooth, then gradually bring in the flour. When it gets hard to mix, use floured hands to form a ball.
Knead on a floured surface about 4 minutes until smooth and elastic. It shouldn't be too wet or dry; tweak with water or flour. Wrap and rest 30 minutes.
Clamp a pasta machine to a clean table. Divide the dough into four, keeping it covered with a damp cloth.

Stage 1: flatten a piece by hand and run it through the thickest setting, then the next one down. Fold in half and run through the thickest setting again; repeat a few times until super-smooth and the sheet fills the machine.

Stage 2: roll the sheet down through each setting, dusting with flour, keeping light tension so there are no kinks. About 2 mm for linguine, tagliatelle and lasagne; 1 mm for filled pasta like ravioli and tortellini.

recipes.intro: Italy is full of rules and old wives' tales about pasta, and they contradict each other. The key question: does it eat well with the sauce you're pairing it with?

recipes.title: White Chocolate Cream Cheese Ganache Sponge

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Grease two 25 cm loose-bottomed tins, line with paper, dust with flour and shake out.
Whisk the yolks, water, vanilla and oil and add the sugar gradually. Whisk until pale yellow and thick.
Whisk the whites to soft peaks. Sift the flour, baking powder, salt and cornflour and fold into the yolk mixture, then fold in the whites.
Divide between the tins and bake 35 minutes. Cool in the tins, then on a rack.
Melt the white chocolate and cool.
Mix 100 ml of the cream cheese with the yolks. Beat in the melted chocolate a spoonful at a time, then the rest of the cream cheese a spoonful at a time, beating well each time.
Beat in the butter a spoonful at a time until smooth and thick. Chill until firm enough to spread.
Sugared fruit: brush fruit pieces with egg white and press into castor sugar.

Chocolate shards: melt chocolate in a double boiler, spread thinly on a WizBake sheet and roll it up carefully like a newspaper. Secure and chill until hard; unroll and the chocolate breaks into shards.
Halve both cakes to make four layers. Spread a third of the caramel on the first layer, then a layer of ganache. Repeat until all the layers are stacked.
Cover the cake with the remaining ganache and decorate with chocolate shards and sugared fruit.

recipes.credit: Mareli Visser, winner of the Koekedoor competition
recipes.intro: Vanilla sponge with white chocolate cream cheese ganache and fruit. The name has "only vanilla" in it, but the word doesn't fit.
checks: Read from a photo of small newspaper print; double-check amounts.

recipes.title: Sort-of Boeuf Bourguignon (with Lamb)

items: 1 x 250 g packet bacon, coarsely chopped

steps: Preheat the oven to 220°C. Heat the oil in a medium pot until hot.
Add the garlic, onion, carrots and bacon and stir-fry 5 to 6 minutes until the onion starts to brown. Add the lamb and fry 5 minutes more.
Add the wine, rosemary, pickling onions and mushrooms. Stir in the flour and season well.
Put the pot, uncovered, in the hot oven and bake 20 to 25 minutes until it forms a thick sauce. Serve warm.

recipes.src: Afrikaans menu cookbook, p136 (photographed; tips signed "Herman sê")
recipes.intro: A quick oven version of the French classic, made with lamb.
checks: The page caption next to it reads "genoeg vir 2 persone", which doesn't match 1.5 kg of lamb; 6 is assumed. 25 minutes is also short for lamb cubes to become tender, so check them before serving.

recipes.title: Cauliflower Soup with Chilli Butter

items: 1 head (500 g) cauliflower, broken into florets

steps: Heat the butter in a medium pot. Add the onions and garlic and stir-fry 3 minutes until starting to brown.
Add the cauliflower and stir-fry 5 minutes more. Add the chilli, stock and milk and bring to the boil.
Cook 10 to 15 minutes until soft. Season and purée in a food processor until smooth. Serve warm with sambals.

recipes.src: Afrikaans menu cookbook, "Kortpad Indiese geure" menu, p100 (photographed)
recipes.intro: Cauliflower is one of the cheapest vegetables and has an unfairly bad reputation. The secret is not to overcook it and to season it well. This soup is a must-make.
tips: For extra flavour, melt 60 ml butter over medium heat until it starts to brown, add 30 ml chilli flakes, take off the heat and spoon over the soup.

recipes.title: Shortcut Thai Green Curry

items: 1 x 80 g packet green curry paste

steps: Heat the oil in a medium pot. Add the onion, garlic and chillies and stir-fry 2 to 3 minutes until starting to brown.
Add the chicken and fry 5 minutes. Add the curry paste and fry 1 minute more.
Pour in the coconut cream, season and bring to the boil. Cook over medium heat until thick and creamy and the chicken is cooked.
Stir in the mangetout and coriander. Serve warm with cumin rice.

recipes.src: Afrikaans menu cookbook (photographed; tips signed "Herman sê")
recipes.intro: The author once took a cooking class in Thailand where you make green curry paste from scratch: a lot of work. Supermarkets now have pastes almost as good. The secret is good ingredients with the bought paste, and always a handful of chopped coriander.

recipes.title: Brioche Bread Buns

items: 2 packets dried fast-acting yeast (14 g total)
630 ml whole milk, slightly warm (36°C, body temperature)
1 egg, beaten, for egg wash (or flour for dusting)

steps: Line 2 large baking trays (deep ones are even better) with baking paper.
Put the yeast, sugar, milk and melted butter in a mixing bowl, then add the flour.
Mix and knead at least 15 minutes in a stand mixer or by hand. Kneading develops the gluten; this step is very important.
Oil the bowl, add the dough, cover and prove at least 1 hour, until doubled.
Punch out the air and divide into 12 even balls (weigh the dough and divide by 12). Roll into smooth balls, cupping your hand in a circular motion or pinching underneath so they're round on top.
Put 6 on each tray, cover with large clear plastic bags and prove again until doubled and puffy, 1 to 2 hours.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (fan). Dust with flour or brush with egg wash.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes until golden all over.

recipes.time: 20 min prep, 2-3 hr proving, 30 min baking
recipes.intro: Ideal for lunchboxes, sandwiches, burger buns and with soup.
tips: Keeps 3 days airtight; freezes for 3 months (defrost 1 to 2 hours in an airtight container).

recipes.title: Hungarian Mushroom Soup with Fresh Dill

items: 450 g (1 lb) mushrooms, sliced (white or cremini)
3 cups vegetable stock (or chicken stock or bone broth)
1 tbsp chopped fresh dill (or 2 tsp dried)

steps: Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and mushrooms and cook until the mushrooms release their liquid and it evaporates, 10 to 15 minutes.
Mix in the flour and paprika and cook 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the stock, soy sauce and milk, bring to a gentle boil, then simmer 10 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in the sour cream, lemon juice, dill and parsley. Season.

recipes.intro: Creamy, with hints of smokiness and great umami. The perfect bowl to warm you up in winter.

recipes.title: Traditional Roosterkoek

items: 1 kg flour, plus extra for sprinkling
500 ml (2 cups) lukewarm water, plus extra as needed

steps: Make a braai fire with enough coals to braai on a grid about 30 cm above them.
Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a big bowl and make a well in the middle.
Pour the oil and water into the well and mix with a fork until the dough starts to come together, adding water bit by bit as needed.

Turn out onto a floured surface and knead until smooth and elastic. Shape into a ball, put in a lightly oiled clean bowl, cover with cling film or a cloth and leave somewhere warm 1 hour, until doubled.
Knock down and divide into 12 to 14 pieces. Roll into balls and press flatter. Sprinkle with flour.
Put on the grid and braai 20 to 25 minutes over the coals until cooked, turning often so they brown evenly.
Serve with butter, apricot jam and grated cheddar.

recipes.time: 20 min prep, 1 hr rising, 20-25 min braai

recipes.title: Roasted Tomato Cheesecake with Parmesan Crust

items: Breadcrumbs or crushed crackers (for the crust)

steps: Toss the cherry tomatoes with olive oil, salt and pepper and roast until blistered.
Mix breadcrumbs with melted butter and Parmesan and press into a baking dish to form the crust.
Beat the cream cheese with the ricotta (or sour cream), garlic, basil and lemon zest.
Add the eggs and mix gently. Pour over the crust.
Bake until set and lightly golden.
Top with the roasted tomatoes and garnish with fresh basil.

recipes.intro: A savoury cheesecake. The post gives ingredients and steps but no quantities.
checks: The source gives no quantities, oven temperature or baking time, and its photos look AI-generated. Test it before relying on it.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Fritters with Caramel-Orange Syrup

steps: Whisk the pumpkin, salt, eggs and flour together.
Fry teaspoonfuls in hot oil until puffed and golden. Lift out with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towel and keep warm.
Bring all the syrup ingredients except the cornflour and 15 ml milk to the boil, stirring constantly. Simmer 1 to 2 minutes.
Mix the cornflour and milk, stir in and simmer until the sauce thickens slightly. Pour over the poffertjies and serve warm.

recipes.intro: The pumpkin fritter's frivolous niece. As with pampoenkoekies, cook the pumpkin dry before mashing or the poffers fall apart when you fry them.

recipes.title: Chicken Liver Pâté

steps: Heat half the butter in a pan and fry the onion and garlic slowly until soft.
Add the livers and fry until just cooked. Add the sherry and brandy and flambé. Simmer until the alcohol cooks off. Take off the heat and cool slightly.
Process the liver mixture until smooth. Add the cream in a thin stream until velvety and spreadable.
Season and spoon into a pâté dish. Melt the rest of the butter and pour carefully over the pâté. Chill until serving.

recipes.intro: Chicken livers are one of those things you either love or hate; the author falls in the first group. Eat with fresh, crusty bread, sweet-sour gherkins and a piece of mature soft cheese.
tips: Flavour the butter for the top with herbs that complement the pâté: heat fresh bay leaves in the butter to release their flavour, and lay a leaf or two on the pâté before pouring over the butter.

recipes.title: Peppermint Crisp Delight Cones

items: 2 tins (380 g each) Nestlé Caramel Treat
8 sheets baking paper, roughly A5 size
