steps: Paddle 1 tin of caramel in a bowl with a spatula until smooth. Finely grate three Peppermint Crisp bars and break the other two into chunks for garnish.
Whisk the cream and vanilla seeds until firm. Fold into the caramel, then fold in the grated Peppermint Crisp.
Wrap each cone in paper to form a collar about 5 cm above the cone and secure with tape.
Put the second tin of caramel in a piping bag and pipe some into the bottom of each cone. Fill with the Peppermint Crisp mixture so it sticks up above the cone.
Freeze standing up, preferably overnight (cut holes in an upturned ice cream container to hold them).
To serve, remove the collars and garnish with the Peppermint Crisp chunks. Good with extra whipped cream and caramel popcorn.

recipes.intro: A grown-up frozen treat that mashes together a draai roomys, a King Cone and the boere tannie classic, Peppermint Crisp tart.

recipes.title: Koeksister Ice Cream

steps: Bring the milk, cream, half the sugar and a pinch of cinnamon to the boil. (The sugar sinks and stops the milk burning.)
Meanwhile cream the yolks and the rest of the sugar in a mixer on high. Lower the speed and add the scalding milk mixture to make a smooth custard; the heat of the milk cooks the yolks.
Cool completely, then churn in an ice cream machine until smooth.
Near the end of churning, add the koeksister pieces. Spoon into a lidded container and freeze.

recipes.src: Photographed cookbook page (same book as Peppermint Crisp Delight Cones)
tips: Cheat's version: soften bought vanilla ice cream, mix in the chopped koeksisters and refreeze. Also works with leftover Christmas pudding.

recipes.title: Sort-of Bobotie with Honey Peaches

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Heat the oil in a medium pot, add the onions and garlic and stir-fry 3 to 5 minutes until starting to brown. Add the spices and fry 1 minute more.
Put the mince in a large bowl, add the onion mixture and tomatoes, season and mix.
Spoon into an ovenproof dish about 3 cm deep and press the bay leaves into the meat.
Whisk the milk and eggs, pour over and bake 30 to 35 minutes until golden and cooked.
While the bobotie bakes, put the peaches cut side up on a baking tray, sprinkle with the sugar and bake alongside until golden.

recipes.intro: The author doesn't brown the mince separately; it cooks in the oven with the custard. The peaches are a different take on blatjang.
tips: For something fresh on the side, thinly slice onions and tomatoes, drizzle with olive oil and white wine vinegar, season and sprinkle with chopped red chilli.

recipes.title: Handwritten Roti & Samoosa Notes

steps: Roti: mix the flour, salt and water to a dough. Roll out, spread with butter, roll up into a spiral, flatten and roll out again.
Spice mix: fry finely chopped onion until brown without oil, then add the spices with a little water. Add chicken and potato, then potato sauce, and cook.
Samoosas: mix the cheese, onion and spice and fold into the pastry.

recipes.intro: Quick notes from a notebook: a roti dough, a curry spice mix and a samoosa filling idea.
checks: These are rough handwritten notes. Cooking times and the frying method for the roti are not given.

recipes.title: Air-Fryer Pull-Apart Milk Rolls

items: 230 g Eureka Mills white bread flour
To activate the yeast: 3 tbsp warm water and 1 tsp sugar
Parchment paper, to line the air fryer

steps: Mix the yeast, warm water and sugar in a bowl and leave 10 minutes.
Add the flour, sugar, salt, milk and yeast mixture to a mixing bowl and knead until a rough dough forms.
Add the butter 1 tbsp at a time and knead. A sticky dough will form; don't add more flour. Knead until all the butter is absorbed, about 5 minutes.
Cover and rest somewhere warm until doubled.
Punch out the air and divide into 8 balls.
Line the bottom of the air fryer with parchment (leave the sides). Put the balls on the paper and leave until doubled again.
Preheat the air fryer to 160°C for 5 minutes, then bake 18 to 20 minutes.
Brush with butter while still warm.

recipes.intro: Kids and adults love these pull-apart rolls, and they're great with a pasta dinner.
tips: Cover your palms in a little olive or vegetable oil when you handle the dough to stop it sticking.

recipes.title: Milk Tart Croquembouche

ingredients.group: Choux puffs (double for a tagine lid)

items: 50 g cornflour (Maizena), mixed with a little of the measured milk
3 drops almond essence (or essence of your choice)

steps: Preheat the oven to 190°C. Bring the water to the boil in a medium pot, add the butter and stir until melted.

Add the flour all at once and stir fast with a wooden spoon until it leaves the sides and forms a ball. Take off the heat and beat in the eggs one at a time, beating well after each; it must be stiff.
Line two trays with baking paper. Pipe 2 cm rounds and press the tips down with a wet finger.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, then lower to 160°C and bake 20 minutes more. Make a small hole under each with a sosatie stick and cool on a rack.
Bring the milk, sugar and salt to the boil. Whisk the yolks into the cornflour mixture, then very slowly whisk the hot milk in.
Cook 5 minutes, stirring constantly with a whisk. Add the essence and butter and mix well.
Whisk the whites to soft peaks and fold in. Cool, then pipe into the puffs through a 1 cm nozzle.
Fill a big bowl with iced water. Heat the sugar and water over medium heat without stirring. Boil until golden, then dip the base of the pot in the iced water to stop it cooking.
Dip the bottom of each filled puff in caramel and stack them tightly in a cone. The caramel holds them together.

recipes.intro: A challenge from her Facebook friends: build a croquembouche with a South African twist. "Croquembouche" means "crunch in the mouth". A Moroccan tagine lid makes the perfect cone mould.
tips: Bake the puffs a day ahead and keep airtight; fill them on the day. The croquembouche can be assembled three to four hours ahead.
checks: Read from photographed newspaper print; double-check amounts.

recipes.title: Katkoppe (Vetkoek Meatballs)

steps: Soak the bread in milk. When soaked, squeeze out as much milk as possible and crumble the bread finely; keep the milk for the batter.
Add the mince, onion, eggs, vinegar, flour, salt, baking powder, braai spice, flavour enhancer and pepper to the bread and mix. Shape into small meatballs.
Beat the flour, baking powder, eggs, salt and milk together until smooth and lump-free.
Dip the raw meatballs in the batter and fry over medium heat in hot, deep oil until light brown and cooked through. Drain on paper towel.

recipes.credit: Mrs Marie Botma of Koes, Namibia (then South West Africa)
recipes.intro: Mrs Botma says they often travel long distances, and these "cat heads" are handy to eat in the car. Meatballs and vetkoek at the same time.

steps: Whisk the eggs and yolks in a saucepan until well combined.
Add the butter, sugar, lemon juice and zest and put over medium heat.
Stir constantly until the butter melts and the curd thickens and turns glossy and smooth.
Pour into clean glass jars and cool to room temperature before closing.
Keeps up to a month in the fridge.

recipes.title: A Little Spanish Table: Six Tapas Classics

items: Flaky sea salt and black pepper
6 garlic cloves, whole or lightly smashed
⅓ cup extra virgin olive oil
Flaky sea salt and black pepper
½ cup extra virgin olive oil

steps: Grill or toast the bread until the edges are charred and crisp.
Rub the cut garlic over the hot toast. Halve the tomatoes and grate the cut side on a box grater, discarding the skin.
Spread the pulp to the edges, pour over the oil and finish with salt and pepper. Eat straight away.
Warm the oil gently with the garlic (starting cold draws out the sweet flavour).
Once the garlic is pale gold and fragrant, raise the heat and add the prawns in a single layer. Cook until just pink and curled.
Off the heat, stir in the lemon and parsley. Serve straight away with bread to mop up the oil.
Roast the whole vegetables at high heat until the skins blister and char all over.
Steam in a covered bowl so the skins loosen. Peel and tear into long strips.
Arrange on a plate, pour over the oil and finish with salt, herbs and pepper. Rest a few minutes before serving.
Brown the chorizo in the oil, then add the garlic and tomato and cook down.
Stir in the paprika briefly, then the stock and chickpeas and simmer until creamy.
Fold in the spinach in the last few minutes. Serve topped with the eggs and a drizzle of oil.
Cook the potatoes and onion slowly in the oil until tender, then drain, saving the oil.
Beat the eggs with salt and fold in the warm potatoes. Rest a few minutes.
Cook in a little of the reserved oil over medium heat until the edges set but the centre is soft. Flip onto a plate, slide back and finish so the middle is barely set.

recipes.credit: Healthy Eating Feed and Real Food Ritual (@healthyeatingfeed, @realfoodritual)
recipes.intro: Six simple Spanish dishes from one carousel, each built around good olive oil.
checks: The carousel had six recipes; only five were photographed clearly.

recipes.title: Patatas Bravas (Spicy Fried Potatoes)

items: ⅓ cup extra virgin olive oil

steps: Fry the potatoes in the oil over medium heat until deeply golden and crisp. A slow fry gives the crackly shell.
Make the bravas sauce: cook the garlic, tomatoes, paprika and cayenne until thick and glossy. Season.
Pile the potatoes in a bowl and spoon the warm sauce over.
Finish with aïoli and parsley and serve while crisp.

recipes.credit: Healthy Eating Feed and Real Food Ritual (@healthyeatingfeed, @realfoodritual)
tips: Don't crowd the pan; too many potatoes drop the oil temperature and they go soft.

recipes.title: Beef Broth with Roasted Marrow Bones

steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Roast the soup bones uncovered in a large roasting pan for 30 minutes. Add the carrots, celery and onions and roast 30 minutes more. Drain off the fat.
Move the bones and vegetables to a large saucepan. Add the 125 ml warm water to the roasting pan to loosen the browned bits and add all the pan juices to the saucepan.
Add the rest of the ingredients and enough cold water to just cover.
Bring slowly to the boil, then simmer uncovered 4 to 5 hours, topping up with water for the first 2 hours to keep everything covered. Season.
Strain through a cheesecloth-lined colander and discard the bones and vegetables.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Roast the marrow bones on a foil-lined tray until the marrow is soft, translucent and starting to separate from the bone, about 15 minutes.
Spoon the hot broth into bowls and put two marrow bones in each. Serve immediately.

recipes.src: Photographed cookbook page, "Soups and Broths" chapter
recipes.intro: An ultra-refined dish you'd find at some of the best restaurants, but don't be intimidated. Let the marrow slowly infuse the broth and you have an elegant starter.
tips: Broth bank: covered, the broth keeps 3 days in the fridge or 4 to 6 months frozen.

recipes.title: G.O.A.T. Sandwich Bread

items: 8 g bread improver (or a pinch of vitamin C)
40 ml vegetable oil, plus extra for greasing

steps: Mix both flours, the sugar, salt, milk powder, yeast, bread improver, water and oil in a bowl to a dough.
Turn out and slap and fold: slap it down, fold it over itself with both hands, rotate 90 degrees and repeat for 5 to 6 minutes until no longer sticky (or mix on high in a stand mixer for 10 minutes).
Knead until the dough stretches thin enough to be translucent without tearing (the windowpane test). Shape into a ball, put in a lightly oiled bowl, cover and rest 1 hour, until doubled.
Punch out the air and roll out on a floured surface to 60 x 12 cm. Roll up tightly from the short end, pinch the seams shut and close the ends.
Put in a buttered loaf pan, cover with a plastic bag and prove 45 minutes, until doubled and above the pan. Preheat the oven to 180°C 15 minutes into the proof.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes until golden brown. Cool completely.

recipes.src: Photographed cookbook page, "Bread That Will Make You Crumb" p35
recipes.time: 30 min prep, 2 hr proving, 35 min baking
recipes.intro: The author's most-made bread: for butter, toast, sandwiches, breadcrumbs, croutons, fairy bread and croque monsieurs. So soft, with an amazingly golden crust and a nice chew.

recipes.title: Peppermint Crisp Braai Pie

items: 2 x 400 g rolls puff pastry, thawed
Ice cream of your choice, to serve

steps: Prepare the fire: you need medium-high coals to cook the pastry evenly without burning.
Mix the caramel in a bowl until smooth so it spreads easily. Chop or grate the chocolate finely.
Unroll a sheet of pastry onto a sprayed hinged grid, removing the plastic. Spread with caramel and sprinkle with chocolate.
Put the second sheet on top and pinch the sides closed.
Close the grid and cook over the coals 10 to 15 minutes a side until golden and cooked through.
Slide onto a board, cut and serve with ice cream.

recipes.intro: The classic Peppermint Crisp tart taken to a whole new level, on the braai.
tips: Spray the inside of the grid with non-stick spray so the pastry doesn't stick.

recipes.title: By the Seashore: Seared Scallops with Pak Choi & Pickles

items: 20 ml aged white balsamic vinegar (Giuseppe Giusti)

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Remove the roe and rinse the scallops under cold water to remove sand (hold each in your palm so it doesn't break). Press dry on a clean cloth.
Melt the butter and pour into a baking tray; it should cover the scallops once they're seared.
Heat a frying pan. Dust both sides of the scallops lightly with cornflour and season with Maldon salt.
Sear until evenly golden on both sides without overcooking, then move to the buttered tray and finish in the oven until just cooked.
Remove the roe and rinse under running cold water. Slice paper-thin and lay on a baking tray as close together as possible without overlapping.
Sprinkle with Maldon salt, cover with wax paper and roll with a rolling pin into a paper-thin sheet.
Dry in the oven at 70°C with the fan on for 2 to 3 hours, until dry, crisp and colourless.
Melt the butter in a small pot with the water and bring to the boil.
Trim the stems and use only the leaves. Blanch in the butter water until cooked, then drain on paper towel. Season with salt if needed.
Bring a pot of salted water to the boil.
Shave thin ribbons from the asparagus with a peeler, starting at the base so the tips don't break.
Blanch until tender and season with salt.
Shimeji: whisk the balsamic glaze, lemon oil and salt. Blanch the mushrooms and marinate in the pickle for at least 30 minutes.
Radishes: whisk the vinegar, oils and salt. Slice the radishes very thinly lengthways on a mandoline (1 to 2 mm), blanch for a few seconds and put in the pickle.

recipes.intro: A restaurant plate: seared scallops, a paper-thin dried scallop crisp, buttered pak choi, asparagus ribbons, and pickled shimeji mushrooms and radishes.
checks: The plating instructions and a final butternut component are on pages that weren't photographed clearly.

recipes.title: Earl Grey Granita with Lemon & Honey Ice Cream

items: Juice and zest of ½ lemon

steps: Steep the teabag in 1 litre water heated to 80°C. Stir in the sugar and bergamot and leave about 10 minutes.
Heat the glucose in a small pot until it bubbles slightly. Remove the teabag, add the glucose and cool.
Churn well in an ice cream machine, then keep in an airtight container in the freezer.
Heat the honey and lemon juice, stir in the zest, take off the heat and strain.
Bring the milk and cream to the boil. Whisk the yolk and sugar, pour in the hot milk slowly and return to the heat to thicken. Add the 20 ml syrup, cool with cling film on the surface and churn.
Halve the lime and slice thinly. Bring the sugar and a splash of water to the boil, add the slices and cool. Dry in the oven at 80°C briefly until crisp.
Freeze small teacups. Put 1 tsp granita in each, pipe 30 ml ice cream on top and smooth with the back of a spoon. Finish with a lime slice.

recipes.src: Afrikaans fine-dining book, p45 (photographed; photo credit Restaurant Mosaic)
recipes.intro: Served in a small frozen teacup: a spoon of tea granita topped with lemon-honey ice cream and a candied lime slice.
checks: The quantities seem very small for 1 litre of water (one teabag and 2.5 ml sugar); they may be a misprint. The right edge of the page is cut off.

recipes.title: Party Kebabs for 50: Boerewors & Turkish Lamb

items: Garlic, olive oil, salt and pepper

steps: Thread the boerewors on skewers with chunks of baby marrow and red onion (and peppadews) and braai.
Cook the tomatoes, jalapeños, peppers and garlic in olive oil to a smoor and season. Serve the kebabs in hotdog buns with lettuce and smoor.
Season the lamb mince with salt, cumin, chilli and pepper, shape onto skewers and braai.
Serve with a tomato, onion, parsley, mint and avocado salad, yoghurt and pita.

recipes.intro: A catering list for a big event: boerewors kebabs with peri-peri tomato smoor in hotdog buns, and Turkish-style lamb mince kebabs with salads and yoghurt.
checks: This is a shopping list, not a recipe; the steps are assumed. The spice amounts for the lamb (300 g cumin, 250 g pepper for 10 kg) look very high, and how the apricot jam is used isn't stated.

recipes.title: Ginger Biscuit Lemon Cheesecake Tart

steps: Crush the biscuits and mix with the almonds, sugar, melted butter and zest. Press into a tart tin.
Beat the cream cheese and sugar, add the lemon extract and the cornflour mixed with water, then the eggs one at a time.
Pour onto the base and bake until just set.

checks: Only the ingredient list was photographed; the method, oven temperature and time are not from the source.

items: 680 g (1½ lb) stewing beef, trimmed and cut into 2.5 cm cubes

steps: Melt the butter in a large pot and cook the onion until translucent. Stir in the caraway and paprika.
Dredge the beef in the flour, add to the onions and cook 2 to 3 minutes.
Add about ¼ cup broth to lift the brown bits, then the rest of the broth, the tomatoes (and potatoes and carrots), salt and pepper.
Bring to the boil, cover and simmer 1½ to 2 hours until tender.

recipes.title: Sweet Lace Tuile

steps: Whisk everything together.
Pour a thin layer into a hot non-stick pan and cook until the water evaporates and a golden lace forms.
Lift off with a spatula and drain on paper towel.

recipes.intro: A lacy, crisp garnish for plated desserts.
checks: The screenshot shows only the quantities; the method is the standard one for lace tuiles.

recipes.title: Bosduifklip Mussel Sosaties

steps: Soak wooden sosatie sticks in water.
Halve each bacon rasher and cut the gherkins and pineapple into small pieces.
Thaw and clean the mussel meat well.
Wrap each mussel in bacon and thread onto the sticks, alternating with gherkin and pineapple.
Braai over medium coals for 15 to 20 minutes, until the bacon is crisp and cooked.

recipes.intro: Bacon-wrapped mussels with gherkin and pineapple on a stick, straight off the coals in Namaqualand.

recipes.title: Stuffed Pork Fillet on the Coals

items: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
15 ml fresh thyme leaves, finely chopped
50 g pitted mixed olives, roughly chopped
Olive oil and basting sauce of your choice

steps: Butterfly the fillet open without cutting right through. Season well.
Spread the mustard over the inside. Mix the cream cheese and thyme and spread thickly over the mustard. Scatter with olives.
Fold the fillet closed, tie with kitchen string, rub with olive oil and season the outside.
Braai over medium coals until half-cooked, then baste after every turn until done to your liking.
Rest, covered, for at least 7 minutes. Slice and serve with potatoes and salad or vegetables.

recipes.intro: A whole pork fillet on the coals is one of David-Thys's specialities. They stuff it with whatever is in the fridge; on the show it was mustard, cream cheese and olives. Just don't overcook it.
tips: Other favourite fillings: kerriewors with sun-dried tomato, feta and rosemary; or ripe brie with sliced green fig preserve.

recipes.title: Tant Myntjie's Scones

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C and line a few baking trays.
Drizzle the melted butter over the flour and rub it in well. Mix in the baking powder, salt and sugar.
Whisk the milk and eggs and cut into the dry ingredients bit by bit with the soft butter. Don't overmix.
Turn out onto a floured surface, press flat by hand and cut out scones.
Bake about 15 minutes until golden. Serve with butter, jam and cheese.

recipes.intro: A big-batch farm scone from the West Coast.

recipes.title: Lena Swarts's Rooibos Roosterkoek

steps: Mix the flour, yeast and salt. Add enough rooibos to make a fairly stiff dough and knead well.
Cover and leave in a warm place to rise. Knock back and rise again.
Pinch off pieces, shape into balls and flatten slightly.
Braai over medium coals, turning often, until evenly toasted, light and hollow-sounding.
Serve with farm butter, jam and grated cheese.

recipes.intro: Clanwilliam is the rooibos capital of South Africa. On Erik and Melinda de Milander's farm, Oude Muur, roosterkoek queen Lena Swarts showed us how to make it with rooibos tea.

recipes.title: Roerbrood (Stirred Boermeel Bread)

items: 3 x 250 ml (3 cups) white bread flour
Wheat kernels or mixed seeds, to sprinkle

steps: Grease two medium loaf tins very well (this bread sticks).
Mix the flours, salt, sugar and yeast. Mix the vinegar with the water and add.
Stir with a wooden spoon for about 5 minutes. It should be a slack mixture; add a little more water if it's stiff.
Spoon into the tins, cover with an oiled bag, wrap in a blanket and leave somewhere warm for 20 to 30 minutes until the tins are full.
Meanwhile preheat the oven to 180°C. Sprinkle with seeds and bake about 1 hour until golden and cooked through.

recipes.intro: Sulene bakes with boermeel (wheat that is simply milled and not further processed) mixed with bread flour. The flavour and texture are wonderful. Replace with brown bread flour if you can't find boermeel.

recipes.title: Namaqualand "Snails" (Garlic Steak Bites)

steps: Season the steak. Melt the butter and fry the garlic over low heat until fragrant. Add the lemon juice.
Fry the steak in the garlic butter until half-cooked. Rest a few minutes, then cut into 1.5 cm cubes.
Toss the cubes in the garlic butter for a few seconds.
Spoon into snail dishes (or onto spoons), spoon over garlic butter and sprinkle with cheese.
Flash under a very hot grill until the cheese melts. Serve with brown bread fingers.

recipes.intro: Not snails at all: cubes of aged rump in garlic butter, served in snail dishes under melted cheddar.

recipes.title: Gerda Coetzee's Malva Pudding

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C and grease a medium ovenproof dish.
Cream the butter and sugar well. Beat in the egg and milk.
Sift over the flour and ginger, add the vinegar and stir.
Mix the bicarb into the jam and add. Mix to a smooth batter and pour into the dish.
Bake about 35 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Meanwhile heat the syrup ingredients over low heat until the sugar dissolves, then simmer 3 minutes.
Prick the hot pudding with a fork and spoon over the boiling syrup. Serve warm with custard.

recipes.src: Plaaskombuis recipes for VIA (Episode 7); Gerda's own notes
recipes.intro: A proper farm malva, from Groot Riet.

recipes.title: Stewed Dried Peaches

steps: Cover the peaches with boiling water and leave 30 minutes to plump.
Put the peaches and soaking water in a pot with the cinnamon, bring to the boil and simmer gently until soft.
Mix the custard powder and sugar with a little cold water.
Stir half into the peaches and boil for a few minutes until slightly thickened. Add the rest if you want it thicker.
Remove the cinnamon and serve.

recipes.intro: A Namaqualand side for venison, curries and roasts.

recipes.title: Curried Lamb Pot

items: 1.5 kg mutton or lamb, in pieces

steps: Brown the onions in hot oil in a heavy pot. Add the meat and jam.
Add the boiling water, cover and stew 1½ to 2 hours until tender. Add the vegetables.
30 minutes before serving, mix the curry, flour, sugar, coriander, salt, pepper and lemon juice and stir into the pot.
Serve with rice, blatjang and banana.

recipes.intro: Served on the show with the Stewed Dried Peaches.

recipes.title: Lemon Meringue Tart

items: 1 packet (200 g) Marie or Tennis biscuits, crushed

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Mix the crumbs and butter and press into a small tart dish. Chill.
Whisk the condensed milk, lemon juice and yolks and pour into the crust.
Whisk the whites to stiff peaks, then add the sugar a spoon at a time until thick and glossy.
Spread the meringue over the filling, covering it completely.
Bake 15 to 25 minutes until golden. Cool to room temperature.

recipes.intro: The condensed-milk classic.

recipes.title: Shank Pie with Batter Topping

items: 2 tbsp thick white onion soup powder

steps: Brown the onion and meat with salt and pepper. Pressure-cook for 2 hours or until tender. Cool.
Remove the bones and shred the meat. Add the vegetables and cook through, then thicken with the soup powder.
Spoon into a greased ovenproof dish.
Whisk the egg, oil and milk. Mix the flour and salt, whisk in the wet mix until smooth, then the baking powder. Add milk if stiff.
Pour over the meat, decorate with onion rings and bake at 180°C for 20 to 30 minutes.

recipes.intro: Pressure-cooked shank under a pour-over batter crust.

recipes.title: Molshope (Cheesy Potato Mounds)

steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water until soft. Drain, mash well and stir in the butter, cream cheese, baking powder and salt. Cool slightly.
Preheat the oven to 180°C and grease a medium dish.
Use an ice-cream scoop to make mounds in the dish (dip the scoop in iced water if it sticks).
Sprinkle with cheese, drizzle with cream and bake 20 to 30 minutes until golden.

recipes.intro: "Molehills": scoops of creamy mash baked under cheese and cream.

recipes.title: Sweet Potatoes with Muscadel

steps: Peel the sweet potatoes, keeping them in lemon water, then cut into rough chunks.
Layer in a heavy pot with sugar and dots of butter, repeating until everything is used.
Pour over the muscadel and bring to the boil, then lower to a gentle simmer.
Cover and simmer about 1½ hours until soft.
Uncover and simmer until the liquid has almost cooked away and the sweet potatoes are caramelised.

recipes.intro: Layered, buttery, caramelised and boozy. Adapted and halved from the original.

recipes.title: Oxtail & Stampkoring Potjie

steps: Heat the oil in a large potjie over hot coals and fry the onions for a few minutes.
Season the oxtail and brown with the onions.
Add 1 litre of wine (more if the meat isn't covered). Cover and simmer over medium coals until almost falling off the bone, up to 3 hours. Top up with wine or water as needed.
Add the potatoes and mushrooms, season, cover and simmer until the potatoes are soft.
Add a little water if needed, spread the stampkoring in an even layer and pour the braai sauce over everything.
Cover and simmer until the wheat is swollen and cooked.
Sprinkle with cheese, cover until melted, and serve.

recipes.credit: Jan Ponk & Renske van Zyl, Vredendal (Plaaskombuis)
recipes.intro: Oxtail braised in white wine, then finished with potatoes, mushrooms and stampkoring (cracked wheat) in the same pot.

recipes.title: Seafood Potjie

items: 30 ml each sea salt and black pepper
1 to 2 raw crayfish tails, in pieces (optional)

steps: Heat the oil and butter in a large flat potjie and soften the onions, peppers and garlic.
Add the rice and fry until every grain is coated. Add the mushrooms and cook.
Add the tomatoes and half the salt and pepper. Cover and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the seafood mix, mussel meat, calamari and the rest of the seasoning. Add the wine and cook over high heat until the rice and seafood are just done and most liquid is absorbed.
Pack the half-shell mussels on top, cover and steam about 10 minutes.
Add the cream and cook through. Add the crayfish (if using), then the parsley and cheese. Serve with lemon.

recipes.intro: A West Coast paella in a flat potjie, finished with cream, cheese and parsley.

recipes.title: The Clark Kent Calzone

items: 2 tsp dry yeast (or active yeast mixed with water)
A generous drizzle of olive oil

steps: Mix all the dough ingredients together and knead thoroughly.
Place in a greased bowl, cover with a damp cloth and leave to rise for 1 hour.
Roll out the risen dough and form small balls. Place on a baking tray and leave to rise for another hour.
Combine the ingredients for your chosen filling and mix well.
Mix the tomato sauce ingredients together and set aside.
Preheat the oven to 240°C.
Roll out a dough ball and place a handful of filling in the centre.
Fold the dough over the filling, seal the edges and trim into a half-moon shape.
Place on a greased baking tray and drizzle a little tomato sauce over the top.
Bake for 10 minutes, or until golden brown.

recipes.intro: The very first dish I made in the food truck. Luca Castiglione, who owned the truck before us (it was called Limoncello back then), was my guide to this recipe. I put my own spin on it with a Biltong and Brinjal filling.

recipes.title: The Joker Hotdog

items: 250 ml mayonnaise (1 cup), or the homemade mayo below

steps: Make sure all the ingredients are at room temperature.
Lightly whisk the egg yolks and season with salt and pepper. Whisk in the mustard and lemon juice.
Add the oil in small amounts, whisking continuously, until thick and creamy. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Combine the cabbage and carrots in a large bowl and stir in the mayonnaise until evenly coated.
Mix the honey and sriracha. Brush over the frankfurters and grill or fry until caramelised.
Place each frankfurter in a roll and top with a generous serving of coleslaw.

recipes.intro: Arnold Tanzer, culinary producer on MasterChef and a mentor to me, was catering a BBC production in Cape Town when we parked the truck to feed the crew. We made my favourite dish in the world: Sriracha and honey glazed frankfurters with mayonnaise coleslaw. And we make our own mayo!
checks: Vol. 1 also lists "½ cup olive oil" and "pinch of cayenne" under the mayo, which look like a copy-paste from another recipe. Left out here.

recipes.title: Taco Whiz

items: 300 g assorted small tomatoes, sliced and marinated in basil and olive oil
2 mielies, boiled, charred and kernels cut off
Fresh coriander and onion ash, to garnish

steps: Burn the onion rings until black, then blitz to a powder in a food processor (this is your onion ash).
Add all the dough ingredients to the processor and mix until a dough forms. Rest for 15 minutes under a damp cloth.
Roll palm-sized balls out very thin and cook in a dry pan for about 2 minutes a side. Set aside.
Char the brinjals over an open flame or on the braai, then peel.
Blend with the fried onion and garlic until smooth.
Sear the tuna for about 1 minute a side.
Mix the spring onion, ponzu, olive oil and cayenne. Slice the tuna and leave it in the marinade until serving.
Blend everything in a food processor until fine.
Layer in this order: taco, aubergine purée, tomatoes, lettuce, onion, tuna, corn, onion ash, then coriander and chimichurri.

recipes.intro: My friend Chef Henry Vigar shared these tuna tacos with burnt corn, chimichurri and smoked aubergine purée on Padkos, and now I'm sharing them with you.

recipes.title: Butter Chicken

steps: Combine the chicken, masalas, cumin, salt, yoghurt and oil. Marinate for a few hours or overnight.
Fry the chicken in a non-stick pan until almost cooked. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, heat the cooking oil and sauté the onion until soft and translucent.
Add the paprika, garlic and ginger and cook gently until fragrant.
Stir in the passata and simmer for about 20 minutes, until the oil starts to separate.
Return the chicken with the butter and cream and cook for a few minutes until heated through.
Stir in the coriander and turn up the heat until the sauce just begins to bubble.
Mix the flour, salt and water to a dough.
Roll into a long sausage and divide into four balls. Roll each ball out into a long shape and spread generously with butter.
Roll up lengthways, coil and press flat again, then cook in a hot dry pan until blistered on both sides.

recipes.src: The Optimist Cookbook Vol. 1; Padkos Episode 4 script
recipes.intro: One of my favourite humans from MasterChef is season 1 runner-up Sue-Ann Allen. We cooked together in the Bo-Kaap for Padkos and made butter chicken rotis. It is a staple in our house.
checks: Roti method in the Padkos script is cut off after "stamp the dough on a hard surface". The last step is a standard finish, please confirm.

recipes.title: The Vixen Burger

steps: Mince the chuck and brisket together. Mix in the eggs and season with salt and pepper.
On a lightly oiled surface, roll handfuls into balls and flatten (use a mould if you like).
Place on wax paper on a tray and refrigerate for at least 10 minutes. Patties can also be frozen.
Cook the patties to your liking and lightly toast the buns.
Layer lettuce, tomato, patty, smoked provolone and Zannie's sweet mustard sauce.

recipes.credit: Chef Pete Goffe-Wood (patty); Aunt Zannie (mustard sauce)
recipes.intro: My friend and MasterChef SA judge Pete Goffe-Wood's burger patty is incredible. The sweet mustard sauce is my late aunt Zannie's, and it is delectable.

recipes.title: Poke-Mon (Tuna Poké with Biltong Dust)

items: 1 kg fresh tuna, diced into 1 cm cubes
A small bowl of seaweed, fried for 10 seconds

steps: Combine everything except the citrus juices in a large bowl and leave for a few minutes.
Add the naartjie, lime and lemon juice and stir well.
Top each serving with 2 to 3 slices of spanspek and garnish with sesame seeds and fried seaweed.

recipes.src: The Optimist Cookbook Vol. 1; Padkos Episode 6 script
recipes.intro: Suzie Holtzhausen is a super-chef, especially with seafood. We had the best fun making this very South African take on poké: tuna ceviche with biltong dust and naartjie, served with spanspek and deep-fried seaweed.

recipes.title: Killer Croquettes (Mac & Cheese Croquettes)

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Cook the macaroni in salted water until al dente and drain.
Whisk the cream, milk and 3 eggs together and season.
Combine the pasta with the cream mixture and Parmesan. Spread evenly in a baking tray.
Cool, then refrigerate until completely firm, ideally overnight.
Cut into cubes. Dredge in flour, dip in beaten egg and coat in breadcrumbs.
Deep-fry at 180°C in batches until golden. Drain on paper towel and serve immediately.

recipes.intro: I met Chef Matt Manning at a OneIngredient dinner in 2013, and he later filmed with me for Padkos. These mac and cheese croquettes are insane: golden, crispy, cheesy bites for a snack, starter or party.
checks: Vol. 1 says to preheat the oven but never uses it. The tray may be meant to bake briefly to set, please confirm.

recipes.title: The Spider-Man Vetkoek (with Peri-Peri Chicken Livers)

items: 10 red chillies, deseeded and finely chopped

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt. Gradually add the water to form a manageable dough.
Knead for about 8 minutes until smooth and elastic. Grease lightly, cover and leave in a warm place to double (about 2 hours).
Knock back and roll into a long log about 4 cm thick. Pinch off 4 cm pieces and flatten to 1 cm. Leave to rise slightly on a greased surface.
Deep- or shallow-fry until golden on both sides. Drain on paper towel.
Sauté the onion, chillies and peppers over medium heat for 10 to 15 minutes until soft.
Deglaze with the vinegar, add the paprika and simmer for 20 minutes. Blend until smooth.
Mix the sauce with the raw livers and leave for a few minutes.
Fry the livers in olive oil and season.
Split the vetkoek and fill with the livers. Serve warm.

recipes.src: The Optimist Cookbook Vol. 1; Amagwini docx
recipes.intro: I cooked with the late, great Lentswe Bhengu and went to Langa to try umqombothi and skaapkop. In the spirit of offal we made magwinya with peri-peri chicken livers. It was a magical day.

recipes.title: West Coast Mussels with Hoenderbeentjie Breadsticks

items: 1 kg fresh West Coast mussels, in the shell
A generous glug of olive oil
100 g pickled beach greens (or cos lettuce)

steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Roll the dough into 10 cm logs and thin out one end to look like a chicken drumstick.
Sprinkle with salt and herbs and bake for 12 minutes until golden.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot, add the mussels, cover and steam until they open.
Add the wine, cover and steam for 2 minutes to cook off the alcohol. Strain the liquid and keep it.
Remove the mussels from the shells, warm them in the liquid, then lift them out.
Add the cream to the liquid and heat gently.
Plate 5 or 6 mussels per person with gooseberries, sea coral, sea lettuce and pickled greens. Spoon over the sauce and serve with the breadsticks.

recipes.src: The Optimist Cookbook Vol. 1; Padkos Episode 11 script
recipes.intro: Kobus van der Merwe of Wolfgat in Paternoster was one of my favourite guests in the truck: generous of spirit and kind at heart. We foraged for mussels and seaweed and made these, with his clever drumstick-shaped breadsticks to mop up the sauce.

recipes.title: Prawn, Avo & Mango Salad

items: 2 mangoes, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes
1 long red chilli, deseeded and finely chopped
1 tbsp avocado or extra virgin olive oil

steps: Peel and devein the prawns. Roughly chop half and keep the rest whole.
Combine the chopped prawns, mango and avocado in a large bowl.
Zest half a lime and juice both. Whisk the zest and juice with the coriander, chilli, honey and oil. Season well.
Toss the dressing through the salad.
Spoon onto lettuce leaves and top with the whole prawns, lime wedges and micro herbs.

recipes.intro: From season two of Padkos: a light, tropical salad with sweet mango, creamy avo and a zesty citrus dressing.
tips: Great with a chilled Sauvignon Blanc or a crisp rosé.

recipes.title: Chef Henry's Cheesy Truffles

items: 100 g Fontina, grated (or another melting cheese)

steps: Bring the milk to a simmer.
In another pan, melt the butter, add both flours and cook for 1 minute without colouring.
Add the hot milk gradually, whisking. Bring to the boil and cook for 5 minutes until it pulls away from the sides.
Off the heat, whisk in the Fontina, a drizzle of truffle oil and salt. Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Roll into walnut-sized balls. Roll in semolina, dip in egg and coat in breadcrumbs.
Deep-fry at about 180°C until golden. Give them a few seconds in a hot oven if needed.

recipes.src: The Optimist Cookbook Vol. 1; WhatsApp from Henry Vigar
recipes.intro: Henry Vigar shared this with me. I had my 40th at his restaurant La Mouette in 2015. Perfect as a canapé, snack or indulgent starter.
tips: Serve with Zannie's Sweet Mustard Sauce.

recipes.title: Bertus Basson's Caesar Salad

steps: Use the side of a chef's knife to paste the garlic and anchovies together.
Whisk the Worcestershire and mustard sauces with the lemon juice, Parmesan, pepper and anchovy paste.
Add the oils slowly while whisking to emulsify.
Toss the cos through the dressing, then add the croutons and extra Parmesan.

recipes.intro: We filmed three seasons of Goed Beter Bertus for VIA, and Bertus always made time to feed the crew. He whipped this up for a quick lunch. Joosh it up with bacon bits or chicken if you like.
tips: Add seared fresh tuna if you have it.

recipes.title: Moroccan Roast Carrot and Avocado Salad

items: About 60 ml extra olive oil and vinegar, for dressing

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Parboil the carrots for 10 minutes, drain and put in a roasting tray.
Pound the cumin, chillies, salt and pepper, then the garlic, thyme, oil and vinegar to a paste. Toss through the carrots.
Add the orange and lemon halves cut-side down and roast for 25 to 30 minutes until golden.
Cut the avocados into wedges and combine with the carrots and ciabatta.
Squeeze the roasted citrus juice into a bowl with the pan juices, equal parts olive oil and a splash of vinegar. Season.
Toss everything with the leaves, cress and dressing. Top with yoghurt and sesame seeds.

recipes.intro: A real winner next to any winter stew. We filmed this vibrant, warm salad for Ilse Kook! on kykNET.

recipes.title: Tomato and Pancetta Braai Chicken with Olives

items: 1 red onion, cut into thin wedges
¼ cup fresh basil and oregano, plus extra

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Brown the chicken in 2 tbsp oil in an ovenproof dish and set aside.
Soften the onion in the same dish, then stir in the chilli.
Layer half the sliced and cherry tomatoes, then the chicken, then the rest of the tomatoes and herbs. Season.
Drizzle over the wine and remaining oil and tuck in the garlic.
Roast uncovered for 1 to 1½ hours until golden and jammy.
Add the olives, lay the pancetta over the chicken and grill for 4 to 5 minutes until crisp. Crumble and scatter with herbs.

recipes.src: The Optimist Cookbook Vol. 1; Ilse Kook screenshots
recipes.intro: Another from Ilse Kook. Hearty and perfect for a family feast. It is a go-to in our house, and the leftovers are incredible, if there are any.

recipes.title: Gregg Hammond's 24-Hour Herb-Crusted Beef Fillet

items: ¼ cup freshly crushed black pepper

steps: Trim any sinew. Put the fillet in a snug container, cover with the balsamic and refrigerate for 6 hours or overnight.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Pat the fillet dry.
Mix the herbs and pepper and roll the fillet in them.
Roast for 15 minutes.

recipes.credit: Gregg Hammond (Come Dine With Me SA)
recipes.intro: From season one of Come Dine With Me South Africa. The episode winner, Men's Health model Gregg Hammond, made this incredible fillet.
checks: Vol. 1 gives only 15 minutes roasting. Rest before slicing; timing depends on thickness and doneness.

recipes.title: Heirloom Tomato and Whipped Feta Tart

items: 250 g mixed heirloom baby tomatoes, halved

steps: Preheat the oven to 210°C. Line a 26 cm square roaster with the pastry, folding the edges over slightly.
Mix the lemon zest into the whipped feta, spread over the pastry and scatter the tomatoes on top.
Brush the edges with milk, fold over and brush again.
Bake for 20 to 30 minutes until golden.
Cool slightly, then finish with chives, olive oil, salt and pepper.

recipes.src: The Optimist Cookbook Vol. 1; Le Creuset PDF
recipes.intro: Easy and super-tasty. Adapted a little from one of the tarts we filmed for Plaaskombuis.

recipes.title: Andrea Burgner's Cilbir (Turkish Eggs)

items: 2½ cups plain Greek yoghurt (or Homemade Labneh)
A few fresh or dried sage leaves

steps: Stir the garlic into the yoghurt and spread over two plates.
Bring a small pot of water to the boil, add the vinegar and poach the eggs for about 3 minutes each. Keep warm.
Melt the butter, fry the sage until crisp, add the paprika and take off the heat.
Place the eggs on the yoghurt, spoon over the paprika butter, season and serve with warm bread.

recipes.intro: Andrea Burgner of The Leopard in Johannesburg started out as a home cook with a knack for great combos. This Turkish-style breakfast is a go-to.
tips: For no-fuss poaching, line a cup with oiled clingwrap, crack in the egg, tie it up and poach in the parcel.

recipes.title: Easy Milk Tart

steps: Crush the biscuits finely, mix with the melted butter and press into a greased medium tart dish. Refrigerate.
Heat 750 ml of the milk with the essences until just below boiling. Melt in the butter.
Mix the sugar, cornflour and custard powder with the remaining 250 ml milk, then whisk in the eggs.
Temper the egg mixture with a little hot milk, then pour it back into the pot in a thin stream, stirring.
Stir over medium heat until thick and boiling.
Pour into the crust, dust with cinnamon and leave to cool before slicing.

recipes.src: The Optimist Cookbook Vol. 1; Plaaskombuis Episode 11 notes
recipes.intro: On Plaaskombuis I travelled with Elma Postma to cook in farm kitchens across South Africa. Owen and Louise McGregor serve this easy milk tart at their farm stall, Bagdad Café.

recipes.title: Broccoli Chicken Bake

items: 1 tin (425 g) cream of mushroom soup
1 cooked chicken, deboned and cut into pieces

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Cook the broccoli for 10 minutes until just tender (not mushy) and drain well.
Mix the soup, curry powder and mayonnaise.
Layer the broccoli and chicken in a greased dish and pour over the sauce.
Mix the melted butter with the breadcrumbs and cheese and sprinkle over the top.
Bake for about 30 minutes until golden. Serve with noodles and a fresh salad.

recipes.src: The Optimist Cookbook Vol. 1; Marikie's green recipe folder (photographed)
recipes.intro: My mom, Marikie, made this for us as kids and it is still one of my favourites. You'll need a whole rotisserie chicken.
checks: Vol. 1 says 1 cup cheddar + 1 cup gouda but the method mentions Parmesan; Marikie's handwritten card says 250 ml grated cheese. Card version used.

recipes.title: Handrie's Tamatiebredie

items: 1 kg lamb stewing meat or shanks, in chunks
A good glug of Worcestershire sauce
2 x 400 g tins chopped tomatoes (or 6 ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped)
Fresh coriander or parsley, to garnish

steps: Coat the lamb in the flour and allspice and brown well in hot oil. Set aside.
Lower the heat and soften the onions. Add the garlic and ginger for a minute, then the coriander and paprika.
Add the tomato paste, bay leaves, Worcestershire and water. Return the meat, bring to the boil and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the tomatoes and sugar, season, cover and simmer gently for about 1½ hours until tender.
Add the potatoes for the last 30 to 40 minutes. Top up with water if needed.
Garnish and serve with rice, pap or crusty bread.

recipes.intro: Of everything my husband makes, this is probably my favourite. He starts early and takes his time to get it just right. A perfect comfort dish for winter.

recipes.title: Tata's Khuku (Mandela's Favourite Chicken)

items: 4 chicken drumsticks and 4 thighs (or 1 chicken in 8 pieces)

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Put the onions in a roasting tray with the chicken on top.
Mix the chutney, ginger and spices, then whisk in the stock.
Pour over the chicken and roast skin-up for 20 minutes, then turn every so often.
After an hour, season and serve with lemon wedges and coriander.

recipes.src: The Optimist Cookbook Vol. 1; photographed recipe card
recipes.intro: From my good friend Arnold Tanzer, who made this for a Mandela Day shoot. It was the late President Nelson Mandela's favourite dish.

recipes.title: Orzo & Chicken Bake

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Toss the onions, peppers, garlic and rosa tomatoes with oil, salt and pepper and roast for 25 minutes.
Scatter the orzo over, spoon the crème fraîche into the middle, pour over the stock and bake for 10 minutes.
Stir, add the chicken thighs and bake for another 25 minutes.
Top with the cheese and season to taste.

recipes.intro: Really delicious and easy.
checks: The tin of tomatoes is listed but never added in Vol. 1. It most likely goes in with the stock.

recipes.title: Beef Lasagne

steps: Soften the onion, garlic, carrot and celery in the oil. Brown the mince.
Add the paste, tomatoes, wine, oregano, sugar and seasoning. Simmer for 20 to 30 minutes.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 to 2 minutes, then whisk in the warm milk until thick. Season with nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Layer meat sauce, sheets, meat sauce and béchamel, finishing with béchamel.
Top with the cheeses, cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes. Uncover and bake for 15 to 20 minutes more.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.intro: Our friends Darren and Ashleigh Lindsay's boys, Charlie and Ollie, love this one.

recipes.title: Anita's Mac 'n Cheese

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Cook the pasta until al dente and drain.
Melt the butter, whisk in the flour, then add all the milk and whisk over low heat for 5 to 10 minutes until thick.
Off the heat, stir in the cheddar, then the macaroni.
Layer cheese sauce-macaroni, then tomato, twice, ending with cheese. Top with Parmesan.
Bake for 15 minutes until golden.

recipes.intro: Nobody beats my mother-in-law Anita Basson's mac and cheese. She is particular about what goes in, and I haven't got it quite like hers yet, but this is a version I checked with her.

recipes.title: Easy Focaccia

steps: Mix everything in a bowl with a wooden spoon. Cover and rest in a warm place for 10 minutes.
With wet hands, stretch and pull the dough. Cover and prove for 30 minutes.
Oil your hands and stretch and pull again. Coat with oil, clingwrap and refrigerate overnight (or two nights).
Line a tray with baking paper and oil. Add the dough, cover and prove for 2 hours.
Dimple with oiled fingers, add olives and oiled rosemary and bake at 200°C for 18 to 22 minutes.

recipes.intro: A good focaccia turns any meal into a feast. Give the dough time: make it and do the first prove two days before you bake.

recipes.title: Whole Roasted Cauliflower with Cheesy Béchamel

steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Simmer the whole cauliflower in salted water for 10 to 12 minutes. Drain and steam-dry.
Oil and season it in a greased dish and roast for 20 to 25 minutes.
Make a roux with the butter and flour, whisk in the milk and simmer 5 to 6 minutes. Add the mustard, cheese and seasoning.
Pour over the cauliflower and bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden and bubbling.

recipes.intro: A show-stopping vegetarian centrepiece.

recipes.title: Cannellini Beans with Roast Tomatoes & Basil

items: 1 x 400 g tin cannellini beans, drained
1 tbsp crème fraîche or cream cheese

steps: Roast the tomatoes, thyme, garlic, oil and salt at 190°C (fan) for 20 to 25 minutes.
Squash the garlic into the tomatoes, add the beans and return to the oven for 5 to 10 minutes.
Remove the thyme, stir in the crème fraîche and basil and season.

recipes.intro: A favourite in our house. Handrie makes this, and it is best with crusty toasted sourdough.

recipes.title: Ham & Cheese Croissant Croque Monsieur

steps: Preheat the oven to 175°C. Whisk the milk, eggs, garlic, mustard, salt, pepper, thyme and cayenne.
Halve the croissants lengthways and cut each half into 4.
Layer half the croissants in a greased 25 cm skillet or 2-litre dish, then ham and half the cheese, then the rest of the croissant.
Pour over the egg mixture, press down and rest 20 minutes (or refrigerate overnight).
Top with the rest of the cheese and bake uncovered for 40 to 45 minutes until puffed and golden.

recipes.intro: Make it the night before and pop it in the oven in the morning.

recipes.title: Biltong Soup

items: 80 g biltong, finely grated, plus slices to garnish

steps: Melt the butter and sauté the garlic briefly. Stir in the flour, spices and pepper.
Gradually add the milk, stock and cream, stirring. Simmer, adding milk if too thick.
Stir in the biltong and cheeses until melted. Add the sherry just before serving.
Garnish with biltong slices and serve with warm bread.

recipes.intro: A family favourite and pure nostalgia. Rich and delicious. I later realised it's really a thinned roux, which is what makes it so rich.

recipes.title: JH's Clear Chicken Soup with Herb Dumplings

items: 4 chicken breasts, bone in and skin on
1 celery stalk with leaves, in chunks

steps: Brown the chicken in oil, add everything else, cover and bring to the boil.
Simmer gently for at least 3 hours, seasoning halfway.
Discard the skin and bones, shred the meat and return it to the soup.
Rub the butter into the flour, baking powder and salt. Add the chives and enough milk to make a dough.
Roll small balls. Drop into about 300 ml hot soup, cover and simmer 5 minutes, turn and cook 5 minutes uncovered.
Serve the soup with a few dumplings and chopped parsley.

recipes.src: The Optimist Cookbook Vol. 1; cookbook photo
recipes.intro: From one of my food heroes, Jan Hendrik van der Westhuizen. We ate at his Michelin-starred JAN in Nice in 2017. He is as charming as he is talented.

recipes.title: Gazpacho

items: 350 g mixed baby tomatoes, halved, and basil to garnish

steps: Score an X in the tomatoes, blanch for 15 seconds, refresh in iced water, then peel, core and deseed.
Blend with the onion, garlic, peppers, cucumber and basil until smooth.
Add the tomato juice and vinegar, season and chill overnight.
Garnish with baby tomatoes and basil.

recipes.src: The Optimist Cookbook Vol. 1; Le Creuset PDF
recipes.intro: Easy and super-delicious. It reminds me of one of my favourite cocktails, the Bloody Mary.

recipes.title: Homemade Labneh

steps: Stir the seasoning into the yoghurt.
Spoon into a muslin-lined sieve over a bowl, gather and twist the cloth.
Drain in the fridge for 12 hours (spreadable) to 24 hours (firm and tangy).
Keeps up to 1 week. Serve with olive oil, za'atar, herbs or nuts.

recipes.intro: Thick, tangy strained yoghurt cheese. Great as a dip or spread, and in the Cilbir.
tips: Roll firm labneh into balls and keep them in a jar of olive oil and herbs for mezze.

recipes.title: Seven Layer Salad

items: 500 ml mayonnaise (or half mayo, half yoghurt)
1 large onion, halved and thinly sliced
2 packs streaky bacon (200-250 g each), diced and fried crisp

steps: Whisk the dressing ingredients.
In a straight-sided glass bowl, layer half of each: lettuce, onion, pepper, peas, bacon, egg, cheese. Spoon over half the dressing.
Repeat and finish with the dressing. Garnish with a little egg, bacon, peas or cheese.
Cover and refrigerate overnight. Don't toss before serving.

recipes.intro: A make-ahead classic.

recipes.title: Zannie's Sweet Mustard Sauce

steps: Whisk everything together until smooth.
Cook in a double boiler (or a glass bowl over boiling water) for 20 to 30 minutes until thick, stirring occasionally.
Cool and store in the fridge.

recipes.src: The Optimist Cookbook Vol. 1; Zannie's typed card (photographed)
recipes.intro: My late aunt Zannie had a sauce for every occasion, but none more beloved than this. Bottled, it keeps in the fridge for 6 months, not that it ever lasts that long.
checks: Zannie's original card: 3 eggs, 250 ml sugar, 100 ml vinegar, 25-30 ml mustard powder, ½ tsp salt, pinch cayenne. Vol. 1 uses 250 g sugar and adds wholegrain mustard.

recipes.title: Marikie's Koeksisters

items: 56 g (4 tbsp) butter, at room temperature
About 750 ml vegetable oil, for deep-frying

steps: Bring everything to the boil, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Simmer 5 minutes without stirring.
Strain into a glass bowl and refrigerate overnight. It must be ice-cold.
Sift the flour, baking powder and salt. Rub in the butter.
Beat the eggs and milk and mix in to a soft dough. Knead until smooth, cover and rest for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Roll out 5 mm thick, cut into 10 x 1.5 cm strips and plait, pinching the ends.
Deep-fry at 180°C in batches, 2 to 3 minutes a side, until golden.
Dip straight into the cold syrup, coat well and cool on a rack.

recipes.src: The Optimist Cookbook Vol. 1; Marikie's Koeksisters PDF
recipes.intro: My cousin's husband is obsessed with koeksisters, so my mom gave them this recipe to make in London. We tested it together, and it's a really good one.
tips: Keep in the fridge for several days, or freeze. Thaw 15 minutes before serving.

recipes.title: Easy Peasy Baklava

items: 1 roll phyllo pastry, at room temperature

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C and grease a deep baking tray.
Grind the cashews and 40 g of the pistachios with the sugar until rough.
Layer a few phyllo sheets in the tray, brush with ghee and scatter with nuts. Repeat twice.
Top with the remaining pistachios, then cut into three rows and on the diagonal.
Bake until golden, then leave to cool.

recipes.intro: I love a good baklava, and this one is so easy you'll make it every week.
checks: Vol. 1 says bake 10 minutes and has no syrup. Most baklava needs 30-45 min and a honey syrup. See "The Best Ever Baklava" in Sweet Dreams for a syruped version.

recipes.title: No-Bake Fridge Cheesecake

items: 1 packet (200 g) Tennis biscuits, finely crushed

steps: Mix the biscuits and butter and press into a springform tin. Refrigerate.
Whisk the Cremora and cold water until smooth, then add the condensed milk and cottage cheese.
Sprinkle the gelatine over the cold water, leave 10 minutes, then dissolve in the boiling water. Stir in.
Stir in the lemon juice, then fold in the cream.
Pour onto the crust and refrigerate for at least 4 hours. Top with lightly crushed raspberries.

recipes.src: The Optimist Cookbook Vol. 1; Marikie's green recipe card (photographed)
recipes.intro: Our goddaughter Lua is a cheesecake connoisseur. This no-bake one is easy enough for anyone.

recipes.title: Jan Ellis Pudding

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C and spray a 2-litre ovenproof dish.
Dissolve the bicarb in the milk. Mix the rest of the pudding ingredients, then beat in the milk mixture.
Pour into the dish and bake for 30 minutes.
Bring the sauce ingredients to the boil and pour over the hot pudding. Let it soak in.
Serve lukewarm with thin custard or cream.

recipes.intro: A staple of any South African menu, and this one works every time.

recipes.title: Apple or Pear Pie

items: 385 g (1 tin) apple or pear pieces

steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C and grease a 23 cm pie dish.
Cream the butter and sugar, beat in the eggs, fold in the flour and salt, then mix in the milk.
Spread in the dish, arrange the fruit on top and sprinkle with cinnamon sugar.
Bake for 30 minutes. Warm the syrup ingredients until combined and pour over the hot pie.
Serve hot or cold with mascarpone.

recipes.intro: Use tinned apple or pear. Delicious either way.

recipes.title: Lemon Drizzle Cake

items: 250 g unsalted butter, plus extra for greasing

steps: Preheat the oven to 160°C. Grease and line a loaf tin.
Beat all the cake ingredients until smooth. Spoon into the tin and level.
Bake 40 to 50 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Poke holes all over the warm cake. Mix the icing sugar and lemon juice and pour over.

recipes.src: The Optimist Cookbook Vol. 1; Taming Twins PDF; Padkos file
recipes.intro: One of my mom's go-to cakes when guests come for coffee.

recipes.title: Ultimate Chocolate Brownies

steps: Preheat the oven to 160°C. Grease and line a 20 x 20 cm tin.
Beat the eggs, sugar and vanilla until smooth. Mix in the butter.
Sift in the flour, cocoa and salt and mix. Stir in the chocolate.
Spread in the tin and top with sea salt flakes. Bake 45 to 55 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Melt the ganache ingredients together, pour over and cool. Cut into squares.

recipes.intro: I got this from Ilse Nel, and man oh man, they're great. I've tried so many brownie recipes, but this is the one.
checks: Vol. 1 left out the flour quantity. 140 g comes from the Padkos Episode 12 version of the same brownie (which also uses 5 eggs and 300 g white and milk chocolate, like Top Deck).

recipes.title: Sunday, Bloody Sunday

items: 100 ml vodka for a jug (1 part per serving)
2 tsp Tajín, plus extra for the rim
Celery, pickles and olives, to serve

steps: Rim tall glasses with honey and Tajín.
Shake or blend everything with ice.
Strain into the glasses and serve with celery, pickles and olives.

recipes.intro: Our take on a Bloody Mary, a staple on Sundays. We make a big jug that lasts till lunch.

recipes.title: The Mieu-Mieu Mule

steps: Rim a tumbler with brown sugar.
Shake everything with ice and strain into the glass. Garnish with a lime coin.

recipes.intro: When I feel sorry for myself (which happened a lot during Covid) I say "mieu-mieu". I created this one day to help with the bleakness, and it did.

recipes.title: The Vesper

steps: Shake with ice and strain into a martini glass. Garnish with an olive.

recipes.intro: My favourite version of a martini.

recipes.title: The Turkish Delight

steps: Shake everything except the ginger ale with ice, strain into a glass and top with ginger ale.

recipes.intro: My dad's favourite sweet was Turkish delight. This is a homage to him.

recipes.title: El Pepino Verde

steps: Shake the gin, lemon and elderflower with ice and cucumber.
Pour into a glass and garnish with a cucumber ribbon.

recipes.src: The Optimist Cookbook Vol. 1; Instagram post
recipes.intro: Refreshing and easy.

recipes.title: Lost Boys Liquid

items: 1 part cold brew coffee or espresso

steps: Shake everything with ice vigorously for 20 seconds.
Strain into a martini glass and garnish with coffee beans.

recipes.intro: Our WhatsApp group with Zavion and John is "The Lost Boys", and we always have these when we see each other.

recipes.title: Negroni

steps: Chill a rocks glass with ice.
Stir the gin, Campari and vermouth with ice for 20 to 30 seconds.
Strain over fresh ice and express an orange twist over the top.

recipes.intro: Bitter, bold and beautifully balanced. I might be alone on this island.
tips: Swap the gin for mezcal, or for prosecco to make a Negroni Sbagliato.

recipes.title: Michelada

items: Honey and Tajín, for the rim

steps: Rim a tall glass with honey and Tajín.
Shake everything except the beer with ice and strain over fresh ice.
Top with beer and garnish with a lime wedge.

recipes.intro: Smoky, spicy Mexican beer cocktail with a chilli-lime kick. Perfect for hot days and braais.

recipes.title: Apple Tarte Tatin with Spiced Ice Cream & Sugar Nest

steps: Pre-chill the ice cream machine. Simmer the milk, cream, peel, cinnamon and salt, then infuse 15 minutes off the heat.
Whisk the yolks and sugar until light. Bring the cream back to a simmer and whisk it into the yolks. Strain into a clean pan.
Stir over medium heat until it coats a spoon, then churn and freeze.
Mix the flour, salt and sugar with a paddle, add the butter for 1 to 2 minutes, then stream in the water until a dough forms. Flatten and freeze 20 minutes.
Cut into 4, roll each to 2 mm and cut 12 cm circles. Freeze on baking paper until firm.
Freeze two ladles. Cook the sugar and water to golden caramel, shock the pan in iced water and let it thicken slightly.
Spray the ladle bases and drizzle thin strands of caramel back and forth to make a nest. Harden, remove and repeat to make 8 nests.
Preheat the oven to 240°C (fan). Peel the apples, top and tail, halve crossways and core.
Line 4 x 9 cm tart tins. Cook the sugar to a light caramel, add the salt and divide among the tins. Set 5 minutes.
Put an apple half on each, brush one side of the pastry with egg white and press it glazed side down over the apple, sealing the edges.
Bake 25 minutes until deep golden. Rest 2 minutes.
Invert onto plates, top with a nest, a scoop of ice cream and a second nest. Dust with icing sugar.

recipes.title: Fish Agnolotti with Sour Fish Broth & Chilli Oil

items: 4 pickled peppers, plus 1 tbsp pickling liquid

steps: Pressure-cook the trotter, chicken feet, ginger and water on high for 20 minutes. Strain.
Fillet the fish (keep the bones). Blend about 400 g flesh with the ginger, coriander, egg whites, 10 g cornflour, pepper, sesame oil, salt, sugar, rapeseed oil and ice to a smooth paste.
Mix 100 g of the paste with the flour and remaining cornflour, knead 5 to 7 minutes until smooth and rest 15 minutes.
Pulse the water chestnuts into the rest of the paste and pipe into a bag with a 1 cm nozzle.
Roll half the dough through a pasta machine to the second-thinnest setting. Pipe a line of filling down each sheet, fold over and seal.
Pinch at 15 to 20 mm intervals, cut the strip free and separate the agnolotti. Dust with flour and dry 15 minutes. Repeat.
Sear the fish bones with half the sliced ginger in 1 tbsp oil until deep golden. Add 2 cups meat stock and boil 15 minutes to 1½ cups. Strain.
Finely chop the pickled peppers, greens, garlic and remaining ginger. Fry in 1 tbsp oil until golden, set half aside, then deglaze with the broth and pickling liquid and simmer 5 minutes.
Chop the chillies and cook gently with the oil and shrimp for 10 to 12 minutes until deep orange. Strain and keep the crisp shrimp.
Boil the agnolotti about 3 minutes until they float. Divide among bowls, top with pickle mix, shrimp and chives, and pour over the broth and chilli oil.

recipes.title: Spice-Rubbed Pork with Smoked Beetroot & Hasselback Potatoes

items: 1 tsp fine wood chips (for a smoking gun)

steps: Pressure-cook the beetroot with the orange juice and salt for 30 minutes. Peel and blend smooth with the butter, adding cooking liquid if needed. Warm 5 minutes and season.
Cover with clingwrap, fill with smoke from a smoking gun and leave 10 minutes.
Boil the pickling ingredients. Punch a 7 cm tube from the raw beetroot, slice paper-thin, pour over the hot pickle and cool.
Soften the diced shallot in butter, add crushed caraway and sliced cabbage for 2 minutes, then the wine until almost gone, then the cream for 5 minutes. Season.
Slice the potatoes every 2 mm between two chopsticks. Cook in simmering clarified butter about 25 minutes, adding the garlic after 10 and the herbs for the last 5. Drain and salt.
Toast the seeds and peppercorns 2 minutes, grind fine and add the salt.
Trim the fillet, rub with the spice and oil and chargrill 15 to 16 minutes, turning, until medium. Rest.
Whisk the dressing and season.
Mould creamed cabbage with a 7 cm ring, add a potato and a swoosh of purée.
Slice the pork into 3 medallions, add pickled beetroot like petals, watercress and a drizzle of dressing.

recipes.title: Hokkaido Scallop Crudo with Nectarine & Thai Basil

items: Thai basil flowers and young leaves

steps: Halve the scallops widthways and chill. Slice the nectarines 1 mm thick on a mandoline.
Peel the ginger and lemon. Steep the ginger peel in the vinegar at a simmer for 5 minutes and strain 2 tbsp.
Juice the lemon (2½ tbsp) and ginger (2 tbsp). Blend with the vinegar, fish sauce, sugar, mirin, oils and salt and sieve into a squeeze bottle.
Blend the oil, lemon myrtle, basil and salt on high 3 minutes and strain over an ice bath.
Plate 4 nectarine slices, 5 scallop halves, dressing to cover the plate, drops of the green oil, roe and basil.

recipes.title: Watermelon & Tuna Salad with Crispy Nori Chips

items: 1 spring onion and black sesame seeds, to garnish

steps: Cut the tuna into 1.2 cm cubes, dress with sesame oil and salt and chill.
Cube the watermelon and marinate 15 minutes in the ponzu, yuzu and a pinch of salt.
Heat the oil to 180°C. Dip a rice paper sheet in water, press onto a nori sheet, pat dry and fry nori-side down 30 seconds. Drain and season with sugar and salt.
Blitz the avocado, lime juice and wasabi, season and pipe.
Drain the watermelon (keep the juice), toss with the tuna and spring onion and dome on a plate. Pipe avocado dots, sprinkle sesame and dress with the juices. Serve with nori chips.

recipes.title: Honey Garlic Pork Chops

items: 4 pork chops, bone in or out
2 tbsp rice wine vinegar (or any white vinegar)

steps: Heat the grill. Season the chops with salt, pepper and garlic powder.
Sear in the hot oil 4 to 5 minutes a side until golden and cooked. Set aside.
Lower the heat, melt the butter and scrape up the bits. Fry the garlic 30 seconds, then add the honey, water and vinegar.
Reduce on medium-high 3 to 4 minutes until slightly thick.
Return the pork, baste and grill 1 to 2 minutes until the edges char. Garnish with parsley.

tips: To bake instead, sear 2 minutes a side, baste and bake at 200°C for 10 to 15 minutes, then grill 2 minutes.

items: 2 kg whole beef brisket, bone in

steps: Preheat the oven to 190°C. Brown the seasoned brisket in a little oil in a heavy ovenproof pot.
Rub with the spice, return to the pot and add water to a quarter of the way up.
Cover and bake 2½ to 3 hours, checking the water every 30 minutes, until the bone pulls out cleanly.
Shred the beef. Reduce the cooking liquid and strain it into the beef. Adjust the seasoning.
Heat the oven to 180°C. Roll a line of beef in each tortilla and pack seam-down in a dish.
Spread with enchilada sauce, top with the cheeses and bake 20 to 25 minutes. Garnish with coriander.

recipes.title: Matt Manning's Wild Boar Scotch Eggs

items: 25 g Dijon mustard, plus extra to serve
Pinch each of sea salt and black pepper

steps: Boil the eggs 5 minutes, refresh in iced water 20 minutes and peel.
Mix the sausage meat with the mustards, herbs, yolk, breadcrumbs and seasoning. Divide into 6 and flatten each into a 1 cm patty.
Mould each patty around an egg without overlapping too much. Chill 1 hour.
Roll in salted flour, then egg, then panko, shaping in your hands. Chill 30 minutes.
Deep-fry at 180°C about 2 minutes until golden. Drain, halve lengthways and serve with Dijon.

recipes.title: French Onion Soup (Big Batch)

items: 6 large red or yellow onions (about 1.4 kg)
2 litres beef or chicken stock (or a mix)
½ cup dry vermouth or white wine
1 tbsp fresh thyme (or ½ tsp dried)

steps: Slice the onions thinly from root to stem (about 10 cups).
Cook in 3 tbsp oil over medium heat, stirring often, until soft (15 to 20 minutes).
Turn up to medium-high, add the rest of the oil and the butter and cook until browning (20 to 40 minutes).
Add the sugar and 1 tsp salt and cook 10 to 15 minutes more until well browned. Add the garlic for a minute.
Deglaze with the vermouth, then add the stock, bay and thyme. Simmer, covered, about 30 minutes.
Season, remove the bay and add the brandy.
Brush the bread with olive oil and toast at 230°C for 5 to 7 minutes. Turn, top with Gruyère and Parmesan and bake until bubbling.
Ladle the soup into bowls and float a cheesy toast on each.

recipes.intro: The success of this soup depends on your stock. Boost it with a little beef bouillon if it's weak.
